Thérapie anticancéreuse de précision pilotée par l’IA : intégration de données multimodales et aide à la décision en temps réel pour une pharmacothérapie oncologique personnalisée : https://t.co/HBwnDUAr1l

"Precision Medication 3 (2026) 100100 Contents lists available at ScienceDirect Precision Medication journal homepage: https://t.co/anSpdQkG4X AI-driven precision cancer treatment: Multimodal data integration and realtime decision support for personalized oncology medication Gayathri Krishnakumar, Karthikeyan Elumalai⁎ Saveetha College of Pharmacy, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Chennai 602105, India ARTICLE INFO Keywords: Artificial intelligence Precision oncology Multimodal integration Real-time decision support Deep learning ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to enhance precision oncology by utilizing multimodal data and real-time data provision to enhance cancer care. The analysis of digital pathology images is performed by AI, which allows for the definition of genetic traits to reduce the costs of genetic tests and save a substantial amount of money when diagnosing patients. In addition, AI in liquid biopsies helps to identify small residual disease earlier than conventional techniques do, which translates to more effective cancer progression monitoring. State-of-the-art technologies such as MR-Linacs and surgical robots apply AI to alter radiation therapy in real time and assist in cancer procedures immediately. AI systems can be used to provide treatment recommendations, such as IBM Watson, which is used to support decisions made by healthcare providers when treating patients. Recent precise oncology research has significantly improved the accuracy of predictions of treatment outcomes and the discovery of new markers, although with challenges such as data variability and model interpretation. Artificially intelligent systems have already proven to be effective in accurately predicting the response of patients to treatments and finding new means of disease prognosis in accurate oncology environments. AI systems need to be transparent so that trust is built and maintained with health service providers and patients to hold them accountable. To ensure fair and ethical use of AI in cancer care in the future, it is necessary to conduct thorough validation work, treat bias as a systematic issue, and maintain a high level of ethical standards to ensure that decisions made under the banner of AI are unbiased and that the results of the work are ethical to the maximum. Introduction AI has developed into a revolutionary technology that can transform the whole range of oncology care by working beyond simplistic pattern recognition models.1 First, the field of AI was associated with the study of single datasets such as medical images, histopathology slides, or genomic profiles. Currently, the field is shifting toward the integration of multiple types of data and providing real-time support to make clinical decisions. This transformation will allow oncologists to move beyond interpreting images in a static manner and move to a dynamic and data-driven understanding of tumor biology and individual treatment response.2 Precision oncology is emerging as a result of AI that integrates radiomics, genomics, pathology, and digital health records to increase personalized and effective cancer care. Recent developments in deep learning architectures, e.g., graph neural networks (GNNs) or transformer models, have further enabled rapid data modality integration and the creation of coherent patient representations.3 The sophisticated models are able to tie together the appearance of a tumor and alterations at the molecular level and clinical specifics to provide a comprehensive picture of the progression of the disease. Recent research has revealed that the combination of imaging information with omics, as well as fine clinical data, enhances the accuracy of diagnostic procedures, allows better classification of patients, and provides the possibility to predict treatment results in advance.4 As an example, multimodal frameworks with AI assistance in breast and lung cancers have attained predictive accuracies above 90, which are much better than when single methods are used. The information, or multimodal inputs, of various types is representative of the decision-making of clinicians.5 In addition, there is now a trend of real-time adaptation. AI currently uses wearable sensor data, laboratory data, and image updates to provide immediate treatment options. Major research centers and technology consortia have begun utilizing clinical AI systems to forecast adverse events as long as 48 h beforehand, decreasing emergency hospitalization and increasing hospitalization.6 These predictivehttps://doi.org/10.1016/j.prmedi.2026.100100 Received 2 December 2025; Accepted 4 June 2026 Available online 29 June 2026 2950-5232/© 2026 Chinese Journal Practice Publishing House Co.,Ltd.. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Ltd. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license (https://t.co/X5gMcPwIgz). ]]]] ]]]]]] ⁎ Corresponding author at: Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Saveetha College of Pharmacy, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Chennai, Tamilnadu 602105, India. E-mail addresses: karthikeyane.scop@saveetha.com, karthikeyanelumalai@hotmail.com (K. Elumalai). ChinaXiv:202610.00226v1 This version posted 2026-10-24. adaptive systems rely on advanced analytics and digital twin models to simulate patient responses, which facilitate personalized therapy. The equally crucial element in this change is the emergence of explainable and ethical AI in this respect. As AI systems are developed, issues of transparency, bias, privacy of data, and compliance with rules become more widespread.7 As illustrated in recent position papers and guidelines, explainability forms the core of clinician trust and patient safety. The understanding of how an algorithm comes to a decision makes it possible to validate it according to biological reasoning and reduce the possibility of unintended differences in medical care delivery. Efforts are underway to standardize data management designs, implement equitable model training across different entities, and promote responsible AI usage that is in line with international laws.8 Combined, these developments point to a dramatic shift in the field of oncology, where AI is able to be used not only in diagnosis but also in treatment planning, early response, and continuous monitoring. Healthcare providers can transform the traditional approach of responding to diseases to predict disease trends and customize treatment by combining imaging, genetic, and digital characteristics.9 This review investigates the present conditions and future outlook of AI in precision oncology and how multimodal integration and real-time decision support are transforming personalized cancer care. In the analysis of new technologies, research, and ethical considerations, this article reveals the ability of AI to go beyond predictive imaging in oncology. Radiomics, radiogenomics, and machine learning (ML): interconnected concepts in AI-driven oncology imaging In modern-day precision oncology, high-tech technologies are vital in revealing what human beings cannot detect. Radiomics and radiogenomics stand out as fundamental support structures for AI-advanced oncological imaging.10 Radiomics converts conventional clinical images that are CT, MRI, or PET scans into specific numerical data that reveal the structure, texture, and morphology of tumors (Fig. 1).11 These quantitative metrics define the nature of a tumor and the environment around it, which reveals very important information about the behavior of the tumor that may not be visibly noticeable at the same time.8 With the increased size and complexity of imaging databases, more sophisticated computational devices are therefore needed to decode the enormous feature space and be able to draw useful clinical correlations with these data. ML plays a critical role in finding significant features, data sorting, and prediction. Complex relationships between radiomic features and clinical outcomes are sought via methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), support vector machines (SVMs), random forests, and ensemble learners.12 The models are excellent for identifying latent imaging biomarkers, which are associated with tumor behavior, potential for metastasis, and, ultimately, treatment outcomes. The integration of radiomics and ML transforms raw imaging data into relevant information, which helps in early disease diagnosis, treatment preparation, and noninvasive monitoring of the disease. A study performed from 2024−2025 indicated that ML-enhanced radiomic patterns can predict the response to immunotherapy and chemoradiation with an accuracy of over 85−90, which is useful in assisting in clinical decisions.13 The next step in this direction is radiogenomics, which attempts to connect imaging phenotypes to genomic and transcriptomic changes. Radiogenomics can be used to generate imaging surrogates for genetic tests by linking particular radiomic signatures with individual molecular aberrations, including EGFR, KRAS, and TP53 mutations. Radiogenomics facilitates noninvasive molecular assessment by creating an imaging surrogate.14 This combination of phenotype and genotype helps in the development of virtual biopsies that could present a source of molecular data without being invasive. An example is radiogenomic models based on MRI, which have been used successfully to study glioblastoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and breast cancer to infer noninvasively gene expression profiles and tumor heterogeneity. In addition to diagnostics, radiogenomics can also be used to measure changes in molecular evolution over time and to monitor both tumor adaptation to therapeutic pressure and personalized changes in regimens in real time.15 Radiomics, radiogenomics, and ML are all synergistic and form the core of AI-driven oncology imaging. Radiomics transforms medical images into data; ML interpretations of these data illustrate predictive patterns, and radiogenomics contextualizes these patterns on a molecular framework of cancer (Fig. 2). This web system enables medical practitioners to advance the vision of personalized medicine, which is directed by the concordance between imaging and genomics, where imaging not only depicts the presence of tumors but also deciphers the genetic content of the tumor.16 The combination of these AI-based techniques results in predictive, preventive, and participatory oncology, in which imaging biomarkers specific to individual patients are used to inform therapy choices, minimize invasiveness, and improve survival. These technologies will become the foundation of real-time, multimodal decision-support systems, which have the potential to learn continuously as clinical data enter the system and react to the cancer destiny of individual patients.17 AI-driven methodological innovations in oncology There is a correlation between artificial intelligence, ML, and deep learning. AI has a wide scope that covers systems that imitate human intelligence by reasoning, learning, perceiving, and solving problems. ML is a branch of AI, which consists of algorithms that allow computers to learn on the basis of the data and improve their performance independently.18 ML special techniques, including deep learning, a branch of artificial intelligence, are applied to tasks such as image and speech recognition by modeling complex and high-level data representations in a multilayered neural network (Fig. 3 and Table 1).19–22 AI in multimodal data integration AI has changed how intricate biomedical data streams can be integrated to help improve biological understanding and streamline clinical decision-making (Fig. 4). Traditionally, studies in the field of oncology have relied on a single type of data, which limits information on tumor diversity and response to therapy.23 On the other hand, multimodal platforms using AI combine data from diverse domains and capture the molecular, structural, and spatial characteristics of cancer via a single computational platform. This intersection enables oncologists to decipher tumor behavior at various biological levels, ranging from molecular changes all the way to phenotypic changes, which may be observed by imaging. At the molecular level, genomics and proteomics reveal the mutational landscape, signaling pathways, and patterns of protein expression that control tumor progression and resistance to therapy (Fig. 5).24 Radiomics is used to add to this information by quantifying textural, morphological, and spatial features of images via CT, MRI, and PET and converting visual data to high-dimensional numerical data (Fig. 6).25 Whole-slide imaging and deep learning-based digital pathology offer high-resolution images of cells, which have a histological structure connected to the underlying molecular process.20 Through machine learning systems that combine all of these modalities, a multidimensional digital twin of the tumor is generated, which can provide unprecedented precision in diagnosis, prognosis, and customization of therapy by simulating patient-specific responses and is similar to a virtual replica of the tumor to plan precise therapy. A number of recent reports emphasize the groundbreaking role of the inclusion of multimodal AI in oncology, demonstrating the revolutionary impact on the treatment of patients.26 Lung cancer: With the combination of radiomic features of CT and gene expression data, it was possible to predict the presence of EGFR mutations with a high level of specificity and noninvasive prediction, which outperforms the single-modality methods, as the AUC value is much greater and the prediction is more accurate.27 Similarly, histopathological slides with G. Krishnakumar and K. Elumalai Precision Medication 3 (2026) 100100 2 ChinaXiv:202610.00226v1 This version posted 2026-10-24. genetic markers, such as IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion, were found to be more effective in survival prediction models than either genomic or imaging data in glioma. MRI-based features combined with histopathological and clinical variables were found to improve the risk of bone metastasis in prostate cancer patients. In addition, multimodal radiomics and digital pathology fusion enhanced the response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy prediction in rectal cancer patients, which could be used to stratify patients into highly effective regimens.28 The use of radiomic features, paired with the tumor mutation burden (TMB) and proteomic markers in immuno-oncology, has greatly enhanced the ability to predict checkpoint inhibitor responses, which has offered beneficial technologies for selecting patients in immunotherapy trials. All of these methods have shown clear clinical improvements, and recent meta-analyses have revealed up to a 30% improvement in diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcome in comparison with unimodal approaches. Various data streams, such as Fig. 1. Integration of Radiomics and Omics through Artificial Intelligence for Precision Medicine.11. G. Krishnakumar and K. Elumalai Precision Medication 3 (2026) 100100 3 ChinaXiv:202610.00226v1 This version posted 2026-10-24. imaging, clinical notes, and omics data, are integrated into AI-based pipelines.29 Data collection (data quality control, data harmonization, and data standardization), model development (unimodal, multimodal processing, model training, and model selection), and translation into precision health outcomes are workflow components. The results include diagnosis and prognosis, target identification, drug discovery, treatment decisions, clinical trials, and subgrouping of patients to provide personalized information (Fig. 7).30 AI algorithms are based on the combination of imaging, genomics, proteomics, and pathology data. Together, these layers create a unified and adaptive patient profile to guide real-time adjustment of the therapy. In 2025, a study using a multicenter and collaborative approach confirmed that AI-based multimodal systems outperformed traditional methods in personalizing treatment decisions, particularly Fig. 2. In 2024, the CHIEF Foundation Model, trained on 19 cancer types, 15 million unlabeled, and 60,000 labeled whole-slide images (WSIs), revealed that transfer learning in histopathology can achieve a diagnostic accuracy of 98% across tumor subtypes—representing the capability of transfer learning in histopathology. Similarly, a deep learning-based endometrial cancer classifier with a macroaverage of 0.879, as measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, was able to classify molecular categories directly on the basis of histological data. One other groundbreaking system, the PACpAInt model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, applies AI to spatially map tumor–stroma interactions and find high-risk NSMP-like clusters linked to poor prognosis patterns, which cannot be seen in conventional pathology.32,33 EAGLE framework The EAGLE framework is based on the concept of pathologists examining diagnostically salient tissue areas, and this concept increased the model AUROC by 23%, steadily reduced the time required to review slides by 99%, and made near real-time analysis of digital pathology possible and ready for use in clinical practice. Although these have been achieved, there are still challenges.34 The heterogeneity of data in different institutions, inconsistency of imaging protocols, and inadequate interoperability between the data platforms do not allow generalized models to be consistently applied to different contexts. In addition, to establish clinician trust, there is a need for transparent interpretable models, which illustrate the role of multimodal inputs in predictions. These issues are important for handling explainable AI, federated learning, and standardized data for their application in clinical practice. However, there is growing evidence that AI-based multimodal integration is a foundation of future-generation precision oncology, where imaging, molecular, and histological data can be integrated to form intelligent systems that are capable of learning continuously, reasoning adaptively, and guiding therapeutic decisions in real time.35 The role of federated learning (FL) in enhancing the privacy and generalizability of AI in medical imaging Table The aforementioned stringent laws on data protection, institutional 1 Comparative overview of key AI architectures used in predictive imaging. Elumalai Precision Medication 3 (2026) 100100 5 ChinaXiv:202610.00226v1 This version posted 2026-10-24. barriers, and ethical considerations of patient privacy have limited the exponential growth of AI in the healthcare sector. FL has come out to address these challenges by enabling various institutions to collaborate in training ML models without direct access to individual patients.36 This type of decentralization approach guarantees a key issue in the field of medical AI: each model learns from various sources, ensuring that no single patient information is shared, which preserves data privacy and control. Unlike conventional centralized systems, which gather data, FL transmits coded model data from distinct locations to a central server, where it is combined with data from other locations to form an improved model. This ensures that sensitive patient information does not leave local servers, and as such, the chance of a privacy breach is reduced.,37 The FL can optimally cooperate with different datasets, including different types of imaging and patient demographics, to increase the credibility and usability of AI models. In turn, FL-trained models are characterized by higher cross-institutional performance, which is more reflective of diversity in the real world and reduces the biases related to single-center training. FL combines various privacy-preserving and cryptographic mechanisms to ensure privacy and security during training.38 Homomorphic encryption allows mathematical operations of encrypted data; thus, it is possible to perform computations on encrypted data without decryption. Secure multiparty computation (SMPC) enables more than two parties to compute model updates, but only with the outcome of the computation kept confidential. Differential privacy (DP) introduces random noise to model parameters, which is regulated to prevent the exposure of the individual patient.39 Collectively, these methods create a multilevel defense mechanism, which is compatible with modern regulatory and ethical requirements in the use of AI in the healthcare field. FL has demonstrated a reduction in projects such as the Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) Challenge, wherein institutions across the world have collaborated in training brain tumor segmentation models using different datasets without centrally storing data.40 The FeTS project demonstrated that FL is capable of producing diagnostic performance similar to that of centralized training and meets strict privacy laws. This has been followed by similar structures applied to radiology, pathology, and oncology imaging in lesion detection, organ segmentation, and biomarker prediction—with high reproducibility across geographically different datasets.41 In oncology, FL has been especially useful in the development of models that are able to generalize across variations in scanners, imaging processes, population genetics, and labeling procedures. FL can generate less demographic- or institutional-biased models by incorporating data diversity across centers, which allows more equitable healthcare outcomes. It is particularly applicable to precision oncology, in which strong generalizability is critical to make predictions made by AI, such as tumor characterization or treatment response, reliable in other populations.42 In addition to maintaining privacy, FL develops the translational capabilities of AI, which promotes collaborative innovation among academic centers, hospitals, and industry partners. It helps in developing foundation models of medical imaging that are continuously improved or refined with distributed learning to improve in an adaptive manner without needing data movement. With advancements in collaborative structures, integration with other types of data, such as imaging, genetics, and clinical information, will make them predictive and diagnostic.43 Bias mitigation in AI-driven clinical diagnosis AI rapidly redefined predictive imaging and precision oncology, and the problem of algorithmic bias has become a critical obstacle to equity in the delivery of healthcare. Despite impressive progress in the accuracy of diagnoses and decision support, AI models are susceptible to biases caused by imbalanced datasets, diverse healthcare systems, and inequities embedded in the system of data collection.44..."

🏇 CHELTENHAM WATCH | FRIDAY 30 OCTOBER

A fascinating Friday for the novice ranks. We've got established Grade 1 hurdle form going chasing, two significant Irish hurdles and a French youngster whose form received a timely boost yesterday.

Here are today's runners we're following.

🇫🇷 12:25 LYON-PARILLY | GOLDEN THREAD

A win and four seconds from five Flat appearances, including Class 1 placings, make him an interesting recruit to hurdles. Mickaël Seror sends him jumping for the first time today. His Flat ability is established; his obstacle credentials are not.

🇬🇧 12:35 UTTOXETER | HOLD THE SERVE

Finished 19 lengths behind Kabral Du Mathan on his chasing debut at Perth earlier this month. That was a difficult introduction against a high-class rival. Today's three-runner contest offers a better opportunity to establish where he stands over fences.

🇫🇷 13:00 LYON-PARILLY | DINO D'OR

His Fontainebleau victory on 3 October suddenly looks stronger. Grecian Lightning, beaten 7½ lengths that day, returned to win by three lengths yesterday. Dino D'Or was conceding weight in their meeting, making today's French juvenile hurdle particularly interesting.

🇬🇧 13:07 UTTOXETER | ST GABRIEL

Nicky Henderson's four-year-old won his only bumper and now makes his hurdling debut over nearly two and a half miles. Taranis Dubh has already won over hurdles, giving St Gabriel an experienced opponent rather than a field composed entirely of newcomers.

🇬🇧 13:20 WETHERBY | LE BEAU MADRIK

Dan Skelton's five-year-old was ninth in the Welsh Champion Hurdle at Chepstow three weeks ago. He switches to chasing against just Florida Dreams today. The opposition is limited, but this is our first opportunity to see how his hurdling ability translates to fences.

🇮🇪 14:00 DOWN ROYAL | ASH HOBBS

An impressive Fairyhouse maiden hurdle winner on 10 October, now pitched straight into Grade 3 company. Switch From Diesel brings a considerably deeper hurdling record, so this should tell us much more about the substance of Ash Hobbs's debut success.

🇮🇪 14:00 DOWN ROYAL | SWITCH FROM DIESEL

The highest officially rated mare in the field, but her recent Gowran performance was below her best. She now meets an improving Ash Hobbs and several experienced rivals. A useful test of whether her established form still sets the standard.

🇮🇪 14:35 DOWN ROYAL | MANGE TOUT

Won Aintree's Grade 1 four-year-old hurdle in April, having previously finished third behind Narciso Has at Leopardstown. Gordon Elliott brings her back in Listed company against older horses. The opposition includes Blake and El Cairos, so this is no routine seasonal return.

🇮🇪 14:35 DOWN ROYAL | BLAKE

A course-and-distance winner who finished second in a competitive Punchestown handicap hurdle in April. His recent eighth in the Irish Cesarewitch should have helped his fitness. Today's meeting with Grade 1 winner Mange Tout gives us a worthwhile comparison between established handicap form and top juvenile form.

🇬🇧 15:00 WETHERBY | MINELLA ROCKETT

Already a winner over hurdles, the Irish-trained three-year-old now contests the Listed Wensleydale. Vietnorm and Sacre Chef provide useful opposition. This is an important early comparison among juveniles who could develop into Triumph Hurdle candidates.

🇮🇪 15:45 DOWN ROYAL | BALLYFAD

Third behind Bossman Jack and Soldier Reeves in Aintree's Grade 1 Mersey Novices' Hurdle, having endured a difficult Cheltenham Festival run beforehand. Gordon Elliott now sends him chasing over two miles and three and a half furlongs. His novice-chase campaign starts here.

text:
Somebody's selling a six-year-old AI supercomputer on eBay for about a quarter of what it cost new. Rent it out around the clock and it earns back the whole $59.7 million in about a year.

So why dump it? The answer sits in the middle of a $176 billion fight on Wall Street.

A Minnesota reseller listed 300 racks pulled out of a hyperscaler's cloud, with 9,600 Nvidia A100 chips and 1.4 petabytes of RAM inside, for $59.7 million or best offer (plus $50 overnight shipping, which the replies are having way too much fun with). That works out to about $6,200 per GPU with the servers, networking and racks thrown in, or $199,000 a rack. Funny thing is, $199,000 is what Nvidia charged for a single A100 server back in 2020, and now it gets you four.

Hold the champagne on the AI bubble popping.

Microsoft and Google spread the cost of their AI servers over six years on the books. Michael Burry, the Big Short guy, says the real useful life is two to three years, which would mean the big clouds are overstating profits by $176 billion through 2028. If he's right, a six-year-old GPU should be worth close to nothing.

The A100 came out in May 2020, so these racks are six and a half years old. At launch prices, 1,200 of these servers ran about $239 million, and the asking price is a quarter of that. Even if the best offer comes in way lower, Tom's Hardware valued just the chips and memory at roughly $28 million, which is still about 12% of what they cost new. And they're still making money. A100s rent for roughly $0.60 to $1.70 an hour right now, so call it a buck. Run 9,600 of them around the clock and that's $84 million a year coming in, against a power bill in the single-digit millions.

The reason a cloud company sells anyway is electricity. 1,200 of these servers can pull up to 7.8 megawatts, and in AI right now megawatts are the one thing you can't get more of quickly. Put Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips on that same power and every watt earns several times more, so the A100s get kicked out of the building while they still work fine.

Burry's $176 billion argument needs these things to be worth zero, and somebody just asked $59.7 million for them.

The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall, a 46-year-old Nigerian citizen and U.S. permanent resident accused of fleeing before beginning an eight-year prison sentence. 

Hall, who was convicted for her role in a romance-fraud scheme, was sentenced to 96 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Jane Milazzo in January 2026 and ordered to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons by March 25. 

However, she failed to report as directed. Investigators said GPS data from her monitoring device showed her last known location was Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on March 24, 2026, where the device stopped transmitting. 

Hall had reportedly informed her probation officer that she was scheduled to fly to Minnesota, where she was to serve her sentence, but airline records showed she never boarded the flight. 

A federal grand jury subsequently indicted her on October 23, 2026, for failing to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons, and a warrant has been issued for her arrest. 

Hall had earlier pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud mostly older women through romance scams. Court documents said members of the syndicate posed online as generals, philanthropists and entrepreneurs, built romantic relationships with victims and later persuaded them to send money under false pretences.

text:
Socialism isn’t just government doing stuff, it’s integration of the worker into ownership”

That matches standard definitions (which I provided but you didn’t like the reference) of socialism: any of various egalitarian economic and political theories or movements advocating collective or governmental ownership and administration of the means of production and distribution of goods (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Politics, Tyssedal 2024; New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics, Nove).

“As opposed to capitalism which keeps the worker out of ownership since capitalism is privately owned.”

Not necessarily. Once companies go public in a market economy, workers (or anyone) can buy shares and become partial owners. Many firms also offer ESOPs, stock options, or employee stock purchase plans that give workers direct ownership stakes. Broad employee ownership is already common in the U.S. and elsewhere (Kruse, Freeman, and Blasi 2010; Blasi, Kruse, and Freeman).

China is a clear case of state capitalism. Markets and private firms drive a lot of growth and innovation, but the CCP dominates key sectors (banking, energy, telecom, heavy industry) through ownership, industrial policy, subsidies, and regulatory pressure. Private property rights are insecure and subordinate to party goals; profits from state-owned enterprises mainly benefit the state and party (Pearson, Rithmire, and Tsai 2023, 2021; Naughton and Tsai 2015).

What does that mean? It sounds so ominous, final, abrupt, and limiting. We never went any further because we both hand an understanding to a point what it meant, but not entirely until he was performing the surgery.

Either way, to me it is frightening. It is kind of hard to discuss specifics. Those three words carry quite a bit with them good and bad. When I get like this, I try to look on the better side of those words, maybe it opens up my options. Despite the situation, it offers directions to treat and better answers. text:
Meet TARA!
(Turns Ordinary Bombs into Precision Weapons)

What if India could turn its existing unguided bombs into precision weapons capable of striking targets over 150 km away?

DRDO has developed an indigenous technology designed to do exactly that!

> Named Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation (TARA)
> Developed by DRDO's Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad
> Designed to upgrade conventional unguided aerial bombs
> Uses a modular kit to improve their range and accuracy
> Incorporates advanced navigation and guidance systems
> Reportedly supports 250 kg, 450 kg and 500 kg configurations
> Designed to glide towards distant targets after release
> With a Reported range of approximately 150–180 km
> Aims to achieve accuracy within a few metres
> Developed with Indian industrial partners
> Successfully completed its maiden flight trial on 7 May 2026
> Tested jointly by DRDO and the Indian Air Force off Odisha's coast
> Further aircraft integration and operational qualification remain ahead

But, what makes TARA special?

Conventional unguided bombs follow a largely ballistic path after release.

TARA adds guidance and range-extension capabilities, allowing compatible bombs to glide towards distant targets with greater precision.

This could help Indian fighter aircraft engage threats from safer distances while reducing dependence on expensive stand-off weapons.

Its modular approach also offers the possibility of upgrading existing munitions instead of manufacturing entirely new missiles.

With its first successful flight trial in May 2026, TARA represents another step towards indigenous precision-strike capabilities.

A technology designed to make India's existing arsenal smarter, more accurate and more effective.

For the first time since 2022, a ceasefire covering a substantial section of the front line in Ukraine has held for more than 75 hours without a single reported violation.

The humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, has remained in effect for more than three days, allowing a humanitarian mission to proceed in an area where civilians have endured years of occupation and severely restricted access to essential supplies.

Ukraine’s Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, confirmed that neither side had violated the ceasefire.

“For more than 75 hours, we have maintained a ceasefire between Ukraine and the Russian Federation. Neither side has violated it even once,” Dmytro Lubinets told journalists.

He emphasized that this is the first time since 2022 that a ceasefire has been maintained for such a long period across such a large section of the front line.

Humanitarian assistance is now being transported to residents of Oleshky. The priority is to ensure that supplies reach everyone who needs them, particularly elderly residents, people with disabilities and those unable to care for themselves independently.

Ukraine has prepared 25 buses with a combined capacity of 750 passengers, along with ambulances to evacuate people with reduced mobility.

Every resident wishing to leave Oleshky will be offered an opportunity for safe evacuation. Those who choose to remain will be able to stay and receive humanitarian assistance.

The mission began on Oct. 27 under a bilateral ceasefire arrangement.

For Ukraine, the objective is to protect civilian lives, deliver humanitarian assistance and ensure that people living under Russian occupation have a genuine choice to leave safely or remain.

The absence of ceasefire violations for more than 75 hours is an important development. The next priority is ensuring that humanitarian aid reaches civilians and that evacuation arrangements are implemented safely.

Source: Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights / ArmyInform, Oct. 30, 2026.

"The New Testament addresses the issue of food sacrificed to idols primarily in the context of the early church's interaction with Gentile converts. The Jerusalem Council, as recorded in Acts 15, addressed this issue directly. The apostles and elders, guided by the Holy Spirit, decided to impose certain restrictions on Gentile believers, including abstaining from food sacrificed to idols (Acts 15:29: "You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.").

The Apostle Paul provides further insight into this issue in his letters to the Corinthians and Romans. In 1 Corinthians 8, Paul acknowledges that "an idol is nothing at all in the world" (1 Corinthians 8:4) and that eating food offered to idols is not inherently sinful. However, he emphasizes the importance of considering the conscience of weaker believers who might be led into sin by witnessing others eat such food. Paul advises that love and concern for fellow believers should guide one's actions, even if it means refraining from eating food sacrificed to idols to avoid causing others to stumble (1 Corinthians 8:9-13).

In 1 Corinthians 10, Paul further elaborates on the matter, warning against participating in pagan feasts, which could imply fellowship with demons (1 Corinthians 10:20-21: "No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God, and I do not want you to be participants with demons. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too."). Here, Paul draws a distinction between eating food sold in the marketplace, which may have been sacrificed to idols, and actively participating in idolatrous rituals.

Practical Implications

The issue of food sacrificed to idols highlights the broader principle of Christian liberty and responsibility. While believers are free in Christ, this freedom is not to be exercised at the expense of others' spiritual well-being. The guiding principle is love, which seeks the edification of others and the glory of God. As Paul concludes in 1 Corinthians 10:31 , "So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God."  https://t.co/BJdFpN7deX

text:
Where was this concern for human dignity when Graham Staines, an Australian missionary, was burnt alive along with his two young sons in Odisha in 1999?

His killers were not defending Hindu philosophy through intellectual debate. They committed a horrific crime. Dara Singh was convicted for the murders.

Where is the outrage when pastors are assaulted, prayer meetings disrupted and Christian families threatened over allegations that have not been established in court?

The Evangelical Fellowship of India’s Religious Liberty Commission documented 747 incidents affecting Christian communities in 2025. This is an organisation’s documented incident count, not a government crime statistic, but it deserves serious attention and independent scrutiny.

Why is there so little outrage from those who otherwise claim to be guardians of Indian civilisation?

WHAT IS THE HINDUTVA ESTABLISHMENT REALLY AFRAID OF?

Is it Christianity? The Bible? The missionary?

Or is it the possibility that an educated person may no longer blindly accept everything he is told?

A person who learns to think independently may question caste discrimination, religious superstition, political propaganda and the authority of those who demand unquestioning loyalty.

He may refuse to hate another human being simply because someone tells him that the other person belongs to a different religion.

He may even question the ideology of those who claim to speak on behalf of his religion.

That is the real strength of education.

An educated citizen is not necessarily anti-religion or anti-national. But he is more capable of distinguishing faith from manipulation, patriotism from propaganda and genuine leadership from the demand for blind obedience.

LET PEOPLE CHOOSE.

I am not suggesting that every missionary is perfect, every conversion is voluntary or every Christian institution is beyond criticism.

Nor am I suggesting that Hinduism has nothing valuable to offer. India’s philosophical and spiritual traditions deserve respect and serious engagement.

But a civilisation confident in its own intellectual and spiritual traditions should have nothing to fear from debate, education or the freedom of individuals to choose their beliefs.

If Christianity has something to offer, let people discover it.

If Hinduism has something to offer, let people discover that too.

The individual must have the freedom to decide.

No threats. No intimidation. No coercion. No religious privilege. And certainly no vigilante deciding what another Indian is allowed to believe.

SOME QUESTIONS FOR THE SELF-PROCLAIMED DEFENDERS OF HINDU CIVILISATION:

If Hinduism is so intellectually strong, why should educating someone about another faith be considered a threat?
If mass conversion is the concern, why not produce verifiable evidence instead of relying on sweeping allegations and conspiracy theories?
If a missionary commits a crime, why not prosecute that individual through evidence and due process instead of allowing mobs to become judges?
If your nationalism is founded on the Constitution, why should a Christian Indian have to prove his patriotism any more than a Hindu Indian?
If the preservation of Indian culture is genuinely your concern, why should it require the suppression of another Indian’s constitutional freedoms?

India does not need citizens who blindly accept one religion, one ideology or one political organisation.

It needs citizens who can think, question and make informed choices.

Perhaps the greatest contribution of education is not that it teaches a person what to believe. It gives that person the courage to decide what deserves to be believed.

That is not a threat to India.

That is what makes India worth defending.

2/2

text:
Binance estimates $6.3 billion impact as it halts deposits and withdrawals

Binance said a major hacking incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion and that it had temporarily stopped deposits and withdrawals across the exchange. A separate report also put the total effect at around $6.3 billion, matching the exchange’s estimate in scale while describing it as an overall impact. The halt covered both money entering Binance and withdrawals leaving it, so users could not move funds through those services while the suspension remained in place. The incident was reported as still developing, making the estimate a measure of the apparent scale at that point rather than a final accounting of losses. Bitcoin’s price dropped more than 4% after the announcement, a market movement reported alongside the exchange’s response to the breach.

The incident was reported to have started at about 4:30 p.m. EDT, also given as 2030 GMT, and was apparently continuing when the information was reported. Binance described the event as a major hack, while founder Changpeng Zhao said the available signs indicated that a hack had likely occurred. The company said an attacker might have gained access through an engineer’s laptop, after which unauthorized withdrawals took place. That account was framed as a possibility, rather than a confirmed explanation of how the attacker entered or how the incident unfolded. The reported start time and continuing status provide a limited timeline; the available facts do not specify when the suspension would end.

Binance separately reported freezing $3 billion in crypto assets while it examined a possible security breach. Circle and Tether also blocked assets connected to the incident: Circle froze more than $800 million, while Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion. A second report described Tether’s action as involving more than $1.5 billion and Circle’s as involving more than $800 million, broadly consistent with the amounts reported elsewhere. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of its own tokens, while Ripple froze roughly $200 million in funds. These are reported amounts frozen by different organizations; they should not be added to the estimated $6.3 billion impact as though they were separate confirmed losses.

Binance said it would bear the losses from the hack, and co-founder Yi He made the same assurance in a statement reported by https://t.co/cVqofZEDnr. Yi He also thanked cryptocurrency issuers that had frozen assets, recognizing their role in the response without changing the reported size of the incident. Binance temporarily stopped trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution, in addition to suspending deposits and withdrawals. The reports describe distinct measures: a pause in exchange services, a separate trading suspension, and freezes imposed by Binance and other organizations. They do not establish that each frozen sum represents a recovered loss or that every affected asset was held by Binance itself.

Binance reported more than 335 million registered users worldwide and about $160 billion in assets under custody in its 2024 annual report. Those figures describe the platform’s registered user base and the assets it held in custody, not the number of people confirmed to have lost money in this incident. The reported $6.3 billion impact is much smaller than the approximately $160 billion custody figure, but the two measures refer to different things and cannot be treated as a direct comparison of losses. Binance also operates a user asset protection fund held entirely in bitcoin, intended to safeguard user assets in security breaches. The available information gives no amount for that reserve and does not say whether it was used in this response.

The reported division between Binance services matters: https://t.co/mVHSF7vrtT was affected, while https://t.co/YePAfOTOEF said its platform was not. https://t.co/YePAfOTOEF’s statement limits the reported reach of the incident within the company’s services, but it does not alter the estimate for the overall impact. Coinbase also said it had not been affected and was watching developments. The statements from https://t.co/YePAfOTOEF and Coinbase are reports about those platforms, not evidence that the broader cryptocurrency market was unaffected. Bitcoin fell more than 4% after the alerts, showing that a market price moved during the incident even as other exchanges reported no direct effect on their services.

About half of the affected assets had been frozen with assistance from other platforms, according to the BBC World report. That proportion describes assets frozen, not assets returned to users, and the report does not provide a separate confirmed recovery total. The freezing actions reported by Circle, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Ripple illustrate how organizations beyond Binance took steps involving related funds. Yi He’s thanks to cryptocurrency issuers likewise points to their participation in the response, although the facts do not detail the coordination process. The estimated impact and the approximate share frozen therefore describe different stages: the first concerns the apparent overall scale, and the second the portion reportedly blocked.

Analytics firms attributed the incident to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit, while TRM Labs said aspects of the attack resembled earlier incidents linked to North Korea, including the Bybit hack. Chainalysis said it had high confidence in a link between the North Korean group and this hack, presenting that conclusion as an assessment by the firm. The attribution comes from analytics companies; the available facts do not describe a public finding by law enforcement or establish the identity of an individual attacker. A historical comparison offers scale: researchers at TRM Labs recorded $2.9 billion stolen across nearly 150 attacks last year. That prior-year total is below the current $6.3 billion estimate, but one is an aggregate across nearly 150 attacks and the other is an estimate for a single incident, so the measures are not equivalent.

In 2023, Binance admitted guilt in a U.S. case involving anti-money-laundering violations and was ordered to pay the government $4.3 billion in penalties. That penalty was imposed in a separate matter and is not described as connected to the current security incident. The incident’s reported response combines Binance’s service suspensions and assurance to cover losses with asset freezes by multiple organizations. The overall estimate remains provisional in the information available because the incident was described as ongoing, and the reported freezes do not by themselves establish the final amount lost or recovered. For users, the clearest confirmed distinction is between the large global scale of Binance’s registered base and custody holdings, and the narrower facts reported about which platforms were directly affected.

text:
$INTC beat Q3 expectations. Liwei woke up to a bloodbath.

Intel delivered $16.5 billion in revenue, 78% year-over-year growth in DCAI and $0.52 in adjusted EPS. But weak Q4 guidance, hit by the Fab 28 incident in Israel, softer PC demand and margin pressure, sent the stock down more than 20% after hours.

The outlook already includes an estimated $300 million revenue hit and two percentage points of margin pressure from Fab 28. Combined with weaker PCs, poorer fixed-cost absorption and product mix, adjusted gross margin is expected to fall from 44.1% to 38%. That’s a rough outlook.

Liwei has also been hearing concerns about the EMIB-T yield ramp. That’s another potential problem to watch in the near term.

Liwei woke up to the results this morning and spent hours working up the courage to open X. 😮‍💨

Still, once the initial shock wore off, there were reasons for Liwei to stay bullish long term:

• DCAI revenue rose 16.9% quarter over quarter, while operating income grew 22.8%. Segment operating margin reached 41.5%. Intel’s server business is growing more profitable as it scales.
• Even after accounting for the factory disruption, Intel expects mid-teens sequential DCAI revenue growth in Q4. The data-center business still has momentum.
• Foundry’s quarterly operating loss narrowed by 11.3%. The 18A-P and 14A customer pipelines, together with advanced-packaging opportunities, offer further growth potential.

A brutal selloff doesn’t erase those improvements. But it certainly hurts when Intel is Liwei’s second-largest US stock position.

This move wiped out everything Liwei had made since returning in September, and then some. Liwei had cut Taiwan stock exposure substantially near the highs, but overall, it’s still been painful. 😮‍💨😮‍💨

Liwei’s partners joke that the market always rallies whenever Liwei heads back to Italy on holiday.

Unfortunately, the kids don’t start their winter break until January.

So, to all the semiconductor bulls out there: sorry. If the Liwei holiday indicator is anything to go by, we may have another two months of pain ahead. 😂

text:
ANNE, LET’S EXAMINE DANIEL 9:24–27 IN ITS ENTIRETY — NOT JUST VERSE 24.

First, Anne, I AGREE WITH YOU on something fundamental.

JESUS CHRIST IS THE ONLY ONE WHO CAN PROVIDE ATONEMENT FOR SIN AND EVERLASTING RIGHTEOUSNESS.

His sacrifice was sufficient, final, and complete.

Hebrews 10:12 (NKJV) tells us:

“But this Man, after He had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down at the right hand of God.”

There is absolutely no disagreement about WHO accomplished our redemption.

BUT HERE IS WHERE OUR INTERPRETATIONS DIFFER.

Daniel 9:24 identifies SIX prophetic objectives:

To finish the transgression.
To make an end of sins.
To make reconciliation for iniquity.
To bring in everlasting righteousness.
To seal up vision and prophecy.
To anoint the Most Holy.

Christ’s first coming accomplished the decisive work of atonement and established the basis for everlasting righteousness.

But does that automatically mean every prophetic objective has reached its FINAL, VISIBLE fulfillment?

Consider Hebrews 9:28, which speaks of Christ appearing a SECOND TIME, apart from sin, for salvation to those eagerly awaiting Him.

And consider Romans 11:25–27, where Paul describes Israel’s partial hardening and a future fulfillment of God’s covenant promises.

NOW LET’S ADDRESS YOUR QUESTION ABOUT THE SEVENTY WEEKS.

You asked whether Daniel says seventy weeks or sixty-nine.

It says SEVENTY.

But Daniel 9:25–26 specifically distinguishes the seven weeks, the sixty-two weeks, and what happens AFTER those sixty-nine weeks.

Daniel 9:26 (NKJV):

“And after the sixty-two weeks Messiah shall be cut off, but not for Himself.”

Those sixty-two weeks follow the initial seven, totaling sixty-nine.

The passage then describes the destruction of the city and sanctuary.

That is significant because Jerusalem and the Second Temple were destroyed by Roman forces in AD 70.

NOW NOTICE SOMETHING IMPORTANT.

Daniel 9:27 introduces a final period described as ONE WEEK.

Futurist interpreters understand this as Daniel’s seventieth week, involving a covenant, the cessation of sacrifice, and an abomination associated with desolation.

Jesus Himself refers to Daniel’s abomination of desolation in Matthew 24:15.

And in Matthew 24:21, He describes a Great Tribulation.

Revelation likewise describes periods of forty-two months and 1,260 days (Revelation 11:2–3; 13:5).

These passages form the basis for the futurist interpretation of a final seven-year period.

BUT WHAT ABOUT THE GAP?

You asked for a verse explicitly declaring a 2,000-year interval.

There isn’t one.

And I am not going to manufacture a Scripture reference to pretend otherwise.

The futurist understanding is that Daniel 9:26 describes events occurring after the sixty-ninth week, while verse 27 describes the final week. The interval is an interpretation of the prophetic sequence, not an explicitly numbered period.

The length of that interval is not specified.

HERE IS MY QUESTION FOR YOU, ANNE.

If the entirety of Daniel’s seventy weeks, Matthew 24, and the related prophecies in Revelation were fulfilled by AD 70, how do you account for the following?

Matthew 24:29–31 — The coming of the Son of Man and the gathering of His elect.
Revelation 11:3–12 — The ministry, death, resurrection, and ascension of the Two Witnesses.
Revelation 13:5–7 — The beast exercising authority for forty-two months.
Revelation 19:11–21 — Christ’s victorious appearing.
Revelation 20:1–6 — Satan’s binding and the reign described in the passage.

I recognize that preterist interpreters offer symbolic or first-century explanations for these passages.

But I do not believe those explanations adequately account for the full prophetic picture.

AND ONE FINAL POINT.

You say we should read Daniel without a theological lens.

But EVERY interpreter must decide how Daniel’s symbolic language, chronological divisions, and prophetic events relate to one another.

That includes futurists, historicists, and preterists.

text:
In 1998, Warren Buffett gave a 1-hour masterclass on how to never lose money investing.

Here are the 22 most valuable lessons from his lecture:

1. You only have to get rich once. If you have $100 million and can make 10% unleveraged or 20% leveraged, the difference between $110 million and $120 million at year-end means nothing to your life, your family, or anything. But the downside, especially with other people's money, is disgrace, humiliation, and facing the friends whose money you lost. The equation never makes sense.

2. To make money they did not need, they risked money they did have and needed. That is just plain foolish, Buffett says, regardless of your IQ. If you hand him a gun with a million chambers and one bullet and offer him any sum to put it to his temple and pull once, he will not do it. There is nothing on the upside that justifies the downside. People do this financially all the time without thinking.

3. The smartest people in finance went broke, and that is the most fascinating story Buffett knows. Long-term Capital Management had 16 people with possibly the highest average IQ of any business in the country, 350 to 400 combined years of experience, and most of their own net worth in the firm. They still went bankrupt. Buffett says if he ever wrote a book, it would be called why smart people do dumb things.

4. Beta and sigmas tell you nothing about the real risk of going broke. The LTCM team relied heavily on mathematics and believed a six- or seven-sigma event could not touch them. They were wrong. History does not tell you the probabilities of future financial events. The real risk is not volatility. It is a permanent, irreversible blind spot in something crucial, often caused by knowing a great deal about something else.

5. Invest only in businesses you can understand. That one rule narrows the field by about 90%, and that is fine. Buffett can understand Coca-Cola. he cannot value an internet company, and he says if a student handed him a valuation of one on a final exam, he would flunk them. People thought Enron was incredible because it had a good track record, but almost nobody understood how it made money. That was the signal to avoid it.

6. You want a business that is a castle with a wide moat around it. Inside the castle, you want an honest, able, hard-working duke. The moat can be low cost, like Geico in auto insurance, or brand, or patents, or location. But a wonderful castle will always be attacked, so the job of every manager Buffett owns is one thing: widen the moat. Throw crocodiles and sharks into it to keep competitors out.

7. Moats change slowly and invisibly, but they change. Thirty years ago, Kodak's moat was as wide as Coca-Cola's. They had share of mind; the little yellow box meant best in everyone's head. Then they let Fuji into the Olympics and narrowed their own moat. Coca-Cola's moat, by contrast, is wider now than 30 years ago. Every time infrastructure gets built in a country that is not yet profitable, the moat widens a little. You cannot see it day by day, but in 10 years, the difference is enormous.

8. Share of mind beats share of market. When you say Disney, every person in the room has something in their head. Say Universal Pictures or 20th Century Fox, and you have nothing. A mother with two kids will pick the $17.95 Disney video over the $16.95 alternative because she knows it will be fine and does not want to preview ten videos to decide. That little bit of certainty in the customer's mind is worth a fortune.

9. The best businesses have pricing power and require little capital. see's candy sold 16 million pounds at $1.95 when Buffett bought it for $25 million. The entire thesis was whether the price could go to $2.25 without hurting sales. It could, because nobody wants to hand their valentine a box of candy and say, "This year I took the low bid." Today, See's makes $60 million on the same formulas and still takes almost no capital. Compare that to GM, which had to reinvest every dollar into better factories and whose stock barely moved over 50 years.

10. The best businesses earn a royalty on other people's capital. Coca-Cola sells a formula and collects a royalty on every drink. American Express takes a few percent of every dollar you spend. You put up the capital, they take a cut. Low capital intensity is one of the most underrated qualities in a business and one of the surest paths to durable wealth.

11. Define your circle of competence and stay inside it. The size of the circle does not matter. Staying inside, it does. If you know which 30 companies out of thousands you actually understand, you are fine. Buffett understood H.H. brown shoes and Frank Rooney, so he closed that deal in five minutes. If you do not know enough to understand a business instantly, you will not understand it in a month either.

12. Ignore the macro entirely. Buffett has never bought or skipped a business because of a feeling about interest rates, the economy, or any macro forecast. If Alan Greenspan and Bob Rubin both whispered exactly what they would do for the next 12 months, it would not change what he pays for anything. You want to focus on what is important and knowable. The macro is important but not knowable, so you ignore it.

13. Inactivity is the strategy, not a flaw. Wall Street makes money on activity. You make money on inactivity. A broker is like a doctor paid by how often he changes your pills. If everyone in a room trades their portfolio with everyone else every day, they all end up broke, and the intermediary keeps the money. Buffett looks for one good idea a year and rides it to its full potential. He measures Berkshire by how little turnover there is, like a church where the same people fill the seats every Sunday.

14. If you understand businesses, diversification is a mistake. For the 99% who will not evaluate businesses, Buffett recommends a low-cost index fund and extreme diversification. But if you bring real intensity to evaluating companies, owning more than six is a terrible idea. Very few people got rich on their seventh best idea. A lot of people got rich on their best one. Buffett keeps about half his money in what he likes best.

15. Buffett's biggest mistakes are mistakes of omission, not commission. The times he understood a business well enough to act and instead sat there sucking his thumb. He passed on healthcare stocks during the Clinton plan and on Fannie Mae in the mid-eighties, each a multi-billion-dollar miss. Accounting never captures these. The $2,000 he put into a Sinclair service station as a young man, money he lost, has an opportunity cost of about $6 billion today.

16. Focus on what will happen, not when. Coca-Cola went public in 1919 at $40 a share and dropped to $19 within a year. There was always a reason not to buy: the great depression, world war, sugar rationing, thermonuclear weapons. But one share bought then and reinvested would be worth about $5 million. If you are right about the business, you will make a lot of money. The timing is the tricky part, so do not focus on it.

17. When hiring, look for integrity, intelligence, and energy. But if the person lacks the first one, you actually want them dumb and lazy. Because a person with intelligence and energy but no integrity will destroy you. Buffett borrowed this from Pete Kiewit. The trait everyone screens for last is the one that matters most.

18. Here is a thought experiment Buffett gives students. Imagine you could own 10% of one classmate for the rest of their life. You would not pick the highest IQ or the best grades. You would pick the person you respond to best, the one who is generous, honest, gives credit to others, and has leadership qualities. Now imagine you also had to short one classmate. You would pick the egotistical, greedy, slightly dishonest one. The qualities that decide both are not talent. They are character.

19. Every quality on the admirable side is achievable, and every quality on the repellent side is removable. The things that make you want to own 10% of someone are not the ability to throw a football or run fast; they are behavior, temperament, and character, all of which anyone can choose. Buffett's point: you already own 100% of yourself, so you might as well become the person worth betting on.

20. The chains of habit are too light to be felt until they are too heavy to be broken. Buffett sees people in their forties and fifties trapped by self-destructive patterns they can no longer change. At a young age, you can choose any habits you want. Ben Franklin and Ben Graham both did exactly this, looking at people they admired and simply deciding to behave like them. There was nothing impossible about it.

21. Take a job you would take if you were already independently wealthy. Buffett told a 28-year-old at Harvard who wanted a consulting job "to look good on his resume" that it was like saving up sex for your old age. There comes a time to just start doing what you love. Buffett offered to work for Ben Graham for free, was told he was overpriced, and kept pestering him for years. Take the job you would jump out of bed for. You cannot miss.

22. You won the ovarian lottery, and that should shape how you think. Buffett imagines a genie 24 hours before your birth letting you design the world's rules, with one catch: you do not know which of 5.8 billion balls you will draw. Born here or in Afghanistan, with an IQ of 130 or 70, male or female, able-bodied or not. If you could put your ball back and draw one of 100 random others, most people would not, because they are already in the luckiest 1%. Buffett knows he is perfectly wired for a market economy that pays him like crazy, while an equally good citizen leading scout troops and teaching Sunday school is not, purely by luck.

Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan is once again making headlines. On October 25, 2026, Sara visited Kedarnath Dham where she offered prayers and sought the blessings of Lord Shiva. Following her visit Maulana Mufti Shahabuddin Razvi Barelvi from Bareilly Uttar Pradesh, issued a fatwa against her.

Som verdipapir har kryto null verdi - null fremtidig kontantstrøm. Så det er et even-greater-fool game, og når even-the-greater-fool begynner å bli redd for å bli hacket, så vil even-the-greater-fool begynne å bekymre seg for "store-of-value". 

"Buffett compared bitcoin to assets that produce something

Buffett framed his response around a core investing principle. In his view, assets should produce something tangible.

Farmland produces crops. Apartment buildings produce rent. Businesses generate earnings.

Bitcoin, Buffett said, produces none of those things.

"If you told me you owned all of the bitcoin in the world and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it," Buffett said.

The line drew laughter from the crowd packed into the Omaha, Nebraska arena.

When Buffett finished, Munger leaned toward the microphone.

"Well, I have a slightly different way of looking at it," Munger said.

Munger's blunt three-part critique

Munger started by describing the decision rule he said guided much of his thinking.

"In my life I try and avoid things that are stupid and evil and make me look bad in comparison with somebody else," Munger said. "And bitcoin does all three."

He then walked through each of those criticisms.

"In the first place, it's stupid because it's very likely to go to zero," Munger said.

His second concern focused on the financial system.

"In the second place, it's evil because it undermines the Federal Reserve system and the national currency system, which we desperately need to maintain its integrity and government control and so on."

The third point referenced China's crackdown on cryptocurrency.

"And third, it makes us look foolish compared to the communist leader in China," Munger said. "He was smart enough to ban bitcoin in China, and with all of our presumed advantages of civilization we are a lot dumber than the communist leader in China."

The audience laughed and applauded.

Buffett added a quick joke.

"Yeah, and when 25% of the people of the country get mad because we've said what we said today, just remember Charlie spoke last," Buffett said."

text:
MARKET UPDATE — FRIDAY, 30 OCTOBER 2026

For two years, Big Tech's promise was simple: spend now, profit later. This week, investors asked to see the receipt.

Alphabet lost a record $500bn in a single day, Amazon and Intel added fresh bruises overnight, a record $6.3bn crypto heist hit Binance, and Brent crude climbed back above $112 as the Gulf heated up again.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 BIG TECH: AI IS EATING THE OLD MONEY MACHINES

💠 Alphabet fell 13% on Thursday, wiping roughly $500bn off its value, a record. Google Cloud sales doubled, but search advertising missed because searches in "AI mode" earn less from ads. It was also Alphabet's second straight quarter of burning cash. The Nasdaq fell 1.4%.

💡 In plain English: Google is building the AI that answers your question directly, and that answer replaces the ad-filled links that made Google rich.

💠 Amazon is down about 7% before the open. Revenue of $201.9bn and earnings of $1.89 a share both missed forecasts, and it guided fourth-quarter operating profit to about $31bn versus the $33.2bn expected, blaming higher fuel and delivery costs over Christmas.

🔸 The bright spot: AWS, its cloud arm, grew 39% to $46bn, its order backlog reached $578bn, and CEO Andy Jassy expects roughly 40% growth in both 2027 and 2028.

🔸 The worry: advertising growth slowed to 12%, quarterly capital spending hit about $76bn, and free cash flow over the past 12 months was minus $42.4bn. Part of the weakness was timing, as Prime Day moved into the second quarter.

💡 Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays its bills and invests in the business. When it is negative, the company is spending more than it brings in, and must fund the gap from savings or borrowing.

💠 Intel is down about 25% premarket, heading for its biggest one-day fall in over two years. It forecast fourth-quarter sales of $15bn–$16bn against $17bn expected, and gross margins of just 37%. The cause: AI data-centre builders are outbidding PC makers for scarce memory chips.

"I'm disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter."— Lip-Bu Tan, Intel CEO

💡 In plain English: the AI boom is so hungry for memory chips that it is starving the PC market, which is Intel's core business.

💠 The same pattern is spreading. Reddit fell 18% after hours as daily users came in at 130.3m against 134m expected, with Google referrals dropping by over a million a week because people read AI summaries instead of clicking links. Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse shopping agent from its site. DoorDash is buying Instacart for about $17bn, even as AI assistants threaten to bypass delivery apps altogether.

🔸 Only three of the "Magnificent Seven" mega-caps are now up this year: Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia.

As Swissquote's Ipek Ozkardeskaya put it, strong AI demand "doesn't automatically guarantee attractive returns."

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 THE DEBT BEHIND THE DREAM

💠 Microsoft sold $25bn of bonds in 10 parts, some maturing in 40 years, its first long-term borrowing for new money since 2017. Bloomberg reports $115bn of orders, 4.6 times the amount on offer; Microsoft declined to confirm.

🔸 Microsoft was the only one of the five giant cloud spenders with positive free cash flow last quarter ($18.6bn). FactSet estimates that, for the first time ever, the five combined are now burning cash.

💠 Lenders are still relaxed about strong companies. Top-rated firms pay just 0.86 percentage points more than the US government to borrow, down from 1.3 points three years ago. The weakest borrowers, however, now pay 13.07 points more, the highest since the pandemic.

💡 This gap is called a "spread". A small spread means lenders feel safe; a wide one means they are nervous. Today the strong borrow cheaply while the weak are already being squeezed.

🔸 Concentration risk: Anthropic's IPO prospectus, published on Monday, revealed a $110bn, 10-year AWS contract. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, AMD and Broadcom are all counting on a small group of AI labs being able to pay very large bills for years to come.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 MARKETS: A GLOBAL TECH ROUT

💠 US futures around 5am ET: Nasdaq 100 down 2.0% (28,967), S&P 500 down 0.9% (7,687), Dow up 0.1% (52,585). Money is moving out of tech and into older, steadier businesses.

💠 Asia and Europe followed: Japan's Nikkei −2.1%, South Korea's Kospi −3.5%, SK Hynix −7.1%, Samsung −3%, SoftBank −6% (now 48% below its June peak), Tokyo Electron −5.2%, Fujitsu −16.2%. In Europe, ASML fell 4.5% early and the Euro Stoxx 50 is down 0.5%.

💠 The VIX, Wall Street's "fear gauge", rose 5% to 18.1.

💡 The VIX measures how much turbulence investors expect. Readings above 30 signal panic; 18 signals unease, not fear.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 THE ECONOMY: HOT GROWTH, STICKY PRICES

💠 The US economy grew at a 3.4% annual pace in the third quarter, beating the 3.2% forecast and up from 2.2%. Business investment jumped 9.4%, the most since 2020, driven by AI data centres. Consumer spending rose 3.8%.

💠 But September's figures show the strain. PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred price gauge, rose to 3.6% from 3.4%; core inflation (excluding food and energy) was 3.1%. Both were as expected. Incomes rose only 0.2% and, after inflation, spending was flat.

💡 In plain English: people spent more money in September but got no more for it. Higher prices swallowed the difference.

🔸 For balance: quarterly price measures actually cooled (PCE prices rose at a 2.1% annualised pace, down from 5%), and jobless claims stayed low at 194,000, so the economy is not cracking.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 BONDS & CENTRAL BANKS

💠 The Fed, under chair Kevin Warsh, held rates on Wednesday, saying it needs more data before voting for another rise. With inflation at 3.6%, some analysts are openly asking why it did not hike.

💠 Treasury yields edged lower today as investors sought safety: 10-year 4.93%, 2-year 4.59%, 30-year 5.29%. The average 30-year mortgage eased to 7.24% from 7.32%.

💡 When stocks fall, money often moves into US government bonds. Higher demand pushes bond prices up and their yields (interest rates) down.

💠 The ECB held at 2.5% but strongly hinted at a rise on 17 December. Christine Lagarde will step down on 7 February, nine months early, saying she wants freedom to speak on France, where long-term borrowing costs recently hit 5% for the first time since 2002. The Netherlands backs Klaas Knot to succeed her; Spain backs Pablo Hernández de Cos.

💠 The Bank of Japan held at 1.25%, its highest since 1995, and reportedly judged that inflation has met its 2% target.

💠 The dollar index slipped 0.1% to 101.7.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 OIL & THE GULF

💠 Brent crude is up 1.7% at $112.73 after three shocks:

🔸 A tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations.

🔸 Ukraine struck Russia's Novokuibyshevsk refinery, ending a two-week pause that the Trump administration had pushed for ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections.

🔸 Yemen's Houthis claimed six strikes on Saudi targets, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries, Abqaiq and airports in Riyadh and Dammam. These claims are not independently verified.

💠 Washington is weighing its next move. Adm. Brad Cooper briefed President Trump in person on Iran options, and Gulf states have been told to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the midterms. The White House says there will be no attack before the vote and the blockade stays in force.

🔸 US escorts have helped 3,000+ ships through Hormuz and Gulf oil exports are now above pre-war levels, but October saw more than 35 attacks on shipping. A Reuters investigation found Iran imported at least $2bn of military hardware since January 2025, suggesting it can sustain a long fight.

💠 Qatar, cut off since March, is buying long-term US gas supplies (7m tonnes a year in two weeks) as a hedge against future Hormuz closures. Its damaged gas plants need about three years to repair.

💡 Why oil matters to everyone: $112 oil raises the cost of petrol, shipping and food. That is a big reason inflation is stuck near 3.6%, why central banks are leaning towards raising rates, and why Amazon is warning about delivery costs.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 CRYPTO: A RECORD HEIST

💠 Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, suspended all deposits and withdrawals after an attack it estimates at about $6.3bn, the largest crypto theft on record. Around $3bn has been frozen. Hackers appear to have compromised an engineer's laptop; Binance says there is no evidence its wallet keys leaked.

🔸 Blockchain analysts at TRM Labs link the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit. Binance says customers will be fully reimbursed from its protection fund and company money, and expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours.

🔸 Tether froze about $1.57bn of USDT and Circle about $800m of USDC. Lending platform Aave froze its markets as a precaution. BNB, Binance's token, fell over 5%.

💡 In plain English: the blockchain itself was not broken. The thieves got in through an employee's computer, like stealing a bank clerk's keycard rather than cracking the vault.

💠 Bitcoin briefly dropped below $77,000 in Asia before steadying near $77,700. Ether is down 1.2% at $2,222. Separately, Polymarket paused trading after a third-party software breach.

💠 Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, posted a $21bn paper gain on its 847,666 bitcoins. But bitcoin per share fell 3.7% this year as it issued new shares, and it sold $432m of bitcoin to fund dividends and buybacks. MSCI decides on 11 November whether to drop it from its indexes, which could force billions in selling by index funds.

"At the beginning of the next bitcoin bull market."— Michael Saylor, Strategy executive chairman

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 BRIGHT SPOTS & STRUCTURAL SHIFTS

💠 Rivian beat forecasts with $176m gross profit on $2.2bn of sales and expects about 27,000 fourth-quarter deliveries versus 25,000 forecast. Shares rose 2.8% after hours.

💠 China is moving up the value chain: it is now the world's largest exporter of machine tools, BYD's profit jumped nearly 30% on exports, and an upgraded China–Switzerland deal gives 99.8% of Swiss exports duty-free access. Even factories built to replace China often need Chinese machinery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 CALENDAR

Today (ET):

🔸 8:30am: Employment Cost Index, Q3 (forecast 0.8%, prior 0.9%), a key wage-inflation gauge

🔸 9:45am: Chicago PMI (forecast 56.1, prior 58.8)

🔸 12:00pm: Fed's Mary Daly; 12:30pm: Fed's Alberto Musalem

🔸 1:00pm: Baker Hughes rig count

🔸 Earnings: ExxonMobil, Chevron, BP, AbbVie, Regeneron, Colgate-Palmolive

Look ahead:

🔸 Within 48 hours: Binance aims to reopen withdrawals

🔸 Tue 3 Nov: US midterm elections

🔸 Wed 11 Nov: MSCI index decision (Strategy)

🔸 Thu 17 Dec: ECB decision

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 WHAT IT MEANS

🔸 The question has changed from "who spends most on AI?" to "who can afford it?" Strong cash flow and balance sheets are being rewarded; cash burners are being punished.

🔸 AI is disrupting Big Tech's existing cash machines (search ads, retail ads, web traffic) faster than new AI revenue is replacing them.

🔸 Strong growth, 3.6% inflation and $112 oil point to higher rates, not cuts. That makes debt-funded AI spending more expensive.

🔸 Next week is loaded: the midterms, possible US action on Iran afterwards, and Binance's reopening.

Bull case: AI demand is real. AWS has a $578bn backlog and is largely sold out for 2027, Google Cloud doubled, the economy is growing at 3.4%, and credit markets remain open. Sell-offs like this reset prices for long-term buyers.

Bear case: cash burn, higher rates and shrinking legacy profits are colliding. If one major AI customer stumbles, contracts across the industry could unravel, and an Iran escalation could push oil and inflation higher still.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
