Study Notes - (ISBE Dictionary) (PART A) 
Priests and Levites
(כּהן, kōhēn, “priest”; nothing is definitely known as to the origin of the word; לוי, lēwı̄, “Levite,” on which see LEVI):
I. DIFFERENT VIEWS OF THE HISTORY
1. The Old View
2. The Graf-Wellhausen View
3. Mediating Views
4. An Alternative View
II. THE DATA OF THE PRIESTLY CODE (P) IN THE PENTATEUCH
1. The Levites
2. Aaron and His Sons
III. THE OTHER PORTIONS OF THE PENTATEUCH
IV. FROM MOSES TO MALACHI
1. The Sources Other than Ezekiel
(1) The Custody of the Ark
(2) On Its Return from the Philistines
(3) In Abinadab's House
2. Ezekiel
V. EZRA, NEHEMIAH, CHRONICLES
1. Estimates of the Chronicler
2. His Data
VI. LEGAL PROVISIONS
LITERATURE
In some Minaean inscriptions found at El-'Ola, dating back about 1200-800 BC (Hommel in Hilprecht, Explorations in Bible Lands, 719), certain “priests and priestesses of the god Wadd are designated by the term lawı̂, feminine lawı̂'at” (op. cit., 749). It is not known whether this is due to Israelite influence.
I. Different Views of the History.
1. The Old View:
There are great divergences of opinion among modern writers as to the true course of history and the dating of the different documents. It will therefore be best to sketch these views in rough outline, and then give the evidence of the various authorities, together with the reasons that in each case arise naturally from the consideration of that evidence.
The old belief was that the whole of the Pentateuchal laws were the work of Moses, that the account of the subsequent history given in the Books of Chronicles was correct, that Ezekiel's vision, if taken literally, could not be reconciled with the other known facts and was inexplicable, and that in the case of all other discrepancies harmonistic explanations should be adopted.
2. The Graf-Wellhausen View:
The modern critical school have traversed every one of these doctrines. The Chronicler is declared to be in constant and irreconcilable conflict with the older authorities, harmonistic explanations are uniformly rejected, the Pentateuch is denied to Moses and split up into a variety of sources of different ages, and Ezekiel gains a place of honor as representing a stage in a continuous and normal development. The subject is thus inextricably linked with the Pentateuchal problem, and reference must be made to the article PENTATEUCH for an explanation of the supposed documents and a consideration of the analysis with its nomenclature. On the other hand the present article and the article SANCTUARY (which see) explain and discuss the most widely held theory of the historical development into which the history of the supposed Pentateuchal sources has been fitted.
The dominant theory is that of Wellhausen. According to this, “Levite” was originally a term denoting professional skill, and the early Levites were not members of the tribe of Levi, but professional priests. Anybody could sacrifice. “For a simple altar no priest was required, but only for a house which contained a sacred image; this demanded watching and attendance” (Wellhausen, Prolegomena, 130). The whole Levitical Law was unknown and the distinction between priests and Levites unheard of. There were a few great sanctuaries and one influential priesthood, that of Shiloh (afterward at Nob). With the monarchy the priesthood became more important. The royal priests at Jerusalem grew in consequence and influence until they overshadowed all the others. Deuteronomy recognized the equal priestly right of all Levites, and Josiah's reformation placed the sons of Zadok, who were the priests of Jerusalem and not descendants of Aaron, in a position of decisive superiority. Then Ezek drew a new and previously unknown distinction between “the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok” who are “keepers of the charge of the altar,” and the other Levites who were made “keepers of the charge of the house” as a punishment for having ministered in the high places. The Priestly Code takes up this distinction and represents it as being of Mosaic origin, making of the sons of Zadok “sons of Aaron.” “In this way arose as an illegal consequence of Josiah's reformation, the distinction between priests and Levites. With Ezekiel this distinction is still an innovation requiring justification and sanction; with the Priestly Code it is a 'statute forever,' although even yet not absolutely undisputed, as appears from the priestly version of the story of Korah's company. For all Judaism subsequent to Ezra, and so for Christian tradition, the Priestly Code in this matter also has been authoritative. Instead of the Deuteronomic formula 'the priests the Levites,' we henceforward have 'the priests and the Levites,' particularly in Chronicles” (op. cit., 147). From that time onward the priests and Levites are two sharply distinguished classes. It is an essential part of this theory that the Chronicler meant his work to be taken as literal history, correctly representing the true meaning of the completed law. See CRITICISM.
3. Mediating Views:
There have been various attempts to construct less thoroughgoing theories on the same data. As a rule, these views accept in some form the documentary theory of the Pentateuch and seek to modify the Wellhausen theory in two directions, either by attributing earlier dates to one or more of the Pentateuchal documents - especially to the Priestly Code - or else by assigning more weight to some of the statements of Chronicles (interpreted literally). Sometimes both these tendencies are combined. None of these views has met with any great measure of success in the attempt to make headway against the dominant Wellhausen theory, and it will be seen later that all alike make shipwreck on certain portions of the evidence.
4. An Alternative View:
The independent investigations on which the present article is based have led the writer to a view that diverges in important particulars from any of these, and it is necessary to state it briefly before proceeding to the evidence. In one respect it differs from all the rival schemes, not merely in result, but also in method, for it takes account of versional evidence as to the state of the texts. Subject to this it accepts the Mosaic authenticity of all the Pentateuchal legislation and the clear and consentient testimony of the Law and the Prophets (i.e. of the two earlier and more authoritative portions of the Hebrew Canon), while regarding Chronicles as representing a later interpretation, not merely of the history, but also of the legal provisions. In outline the story of the priesthood is then as follows: Moses consecrated Aaron and his sons as the priests of the desert tabernacle. He purified the rest of the tribe of Levi as a body of sacred porters for the period of wanderings, but in the legislation of Numbers he made no provision whatever for their performing any duties after the sanctuary obtained a permanent location. At the same time he gave a body of priestly teaching requiring for its administration in settled conditions a numerous and scattered body of priests, such as the house of Aaron alone could not have provided immediately after the entry into Canaan. To meet this, Deuteronomy - the last legislative work of Moses - contains provisions enlarging the rights and duties of the Levites and conferring on them a priestly position. The earlier distinction was thus largely obliterated, though the high-priestly dignity remained in the house of Aaron till the time of Solomon, when it was transferred from the house of Eli to that of Zadok, who, according to Ezekiel's testimony, was a Levite (but see below, IV, 1). So matters remained till the exile, when Ezekiel put forward a scheme which together with many ideal elements proposed reforms to insure the better application of the Mosaic principle of the distinction between holy and profane to greatly altered circumstances. Taking his inspiration from the wilderness legislation, he instituted a fresh division in the tribe of Levi, giving to the sons of Zadok a position similar to that once held by the sons of Aaron, and degrading all other Levites from the priesthood conferred on them by Dt to a lower rank. The duties now assigned to this class of “keepers of the charge of the house” were never even contemplated by Moses, but Ezekiel applies to them the old phrases of the Pentateuch which he invests with a new significance. As a result of his influence, the distinction between priests and Levites makes its appearance in post-exilic times, though it had been unknown to all the writers of the second division of the Hebrew Canon. At the same time a meaning was read into the provisions of the Law which their original author could not have contemplated, and it was this interpretation which is presented (at any rate to some extent) in Chronicles, and has given us the current tradition. Many of the Chronicler's statements are, however, not meant to be taken literally, and could not have been so taken by his original public.
II. The Data of the Priestly Code (P) in the Pentateuch.
1. The Levites:
To arrive at an objective conclusion it is necessary, in the first instance, to examine the facts without such bias as any view put forward by any other author, ancient or modern, sacred or profane, might impart. Every legislator is entitled to be judged on his own language, and where he has, so to speak, made his own dictionary, we are compelled to read his meaning into the terms used. The very first of the material references to the Levites drives this truth home. “But appoint thou the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all the furniture thereof” (Num_1:50). It is necessary to consider whether such expressions are to be read in a wide or a narrow sense. We learn from Num_18:3 that death would be the result of a Levite's touching any of these vessels, and it therefore appears that these words are meant to be construed narrowly. “They shall bear the tabernacle, and all the furniture thereof; and they shall minister unto it,” are the next words (
Num_1:50); but yet we read later of the Kohathites who were to bear it that “they shall not touch the sanctuary, lest they die” (Num_4:15). This shows that the service in question is strictly limited to a service of porterage after the articles have been wrapped up by Aaron and his sons. By no possibility could it include such a task as cleaning the vessels. It is then further directed that the Levites are to take down and set up the dwelling and camp round about it. All these are desert services and desert services only. Then we read that “the Levites shall keep the charge of the tabernacle (dwelling) of the testimony. This concludes the first material passage (Num_1:50-53). The other passages of Nu only amplify these directions; they never change them. But some phrases are used which must be more particularly considered.
(1) Technical Phrases.
We hear that the Levites are “to serve the service of the tent of meeting,” and this looks as if it might refer to some general duties, but the context and the kindred passages always forbid this interpretation. Num_7:5 ff is an admirable instance. Six wagons are there assigned to the Levites for this service, two to the Gershonites and four to the Merarites. “But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the sanctuary belonged unto them; they bare it upon their shoulders.” Here service is transport and nothing else. Again we read of the charge of the Levites in the tent of meeting, e.g. Num_4:25 f. If we look to see what this was, we find that it consisted of transporting portions of the tent that had been packed up. The “in” of English Versions of the Bible does not represent the meaning of the Hebrew fairly; for the context makes it clear that the legislator means “in respect to.” “But they shall not go in to see the sanctuary even for a moment, lest they die” (Num_4:20). In English idiom we cannot speak of the transport of portions of a dismantled tent as service in that tent. One other expression requires notice, the phrase “keep the charge” which is distinguished in Num_8:26 from “doing service.” The exact meaning cannot be determined. It appears to denote something kindred to service, but of a less exacting nature, perhaps the camping round the tent and the guardianship of the articles on the march. We shall see hereafter by comparison with other books that in P it does not bear the same meaning as elsewhere.
(2) Other Legal Provisions.
The Levites were to act under the orders of Aaron and his sons, who were to assign to each man his individual functions (Nu 3; 4, etc.). They were to undergo a special rite of purification (Nu 8), but not of consecration. They were taken in place of the firstborn (Nu 3). The age for beginning service is given in Nu 4 as 30 years, but in Num_8:24 as 25 years, if the text is sound. The age for ceasing to serve was 50. In many passages the versions suggest that a good many phrases are textually doubtful, and it is probable that when a critical text of the Pentateuch is formed on scientific principles, a good many superfluous expressions will be found not to be original; but there is no reason to suppose that any real difference in the meaning of the passages would be revealed by such a text.
The story of Korah is easily misunderstood. It appears from Num_16:3 that his real object was to put himself on an equality with Moses and Aaron, and this is the “priesthood” referred to in Num_16:10. Nu 18 reinforces the earlier passages. It is noteworthy as showing that in the conception of the legislator the Levites were not to come near the vessels or the altar (Num_18:3). The penalty is death for both Levites and priests.
(3) Contrast with Ezekiel and Chronicles.
The impression as to the meaning of P which may be gathered from an examination of its statements is powerfully reinforced when they are tested by reference to Ezekiel and Chronicles, Ezk_44:9-14 seems to demand of the Levites some service as gatekeepers, the slaying of burnt offering and sacrifice for the people and a keeping of “the charge of the house, for all the service thereof,” which in the light of Ezk_44:7 f appears to mean in his terminology, not a service of transport, but an entry into the house and the performance of certain duties there. The Priestly Code (P), on the contrary, knows nothing of gatekeepers, regards the slaying of the burnt offering and sacrifice as the duty of the individual sacrificant (Lev 1; 3), and - if, as Wellhausen thinks, it refers to the temple - it would have visited with death a Levite who was present in the places in which Ezekiel requires him to minister. Similarly with the Chronicler. For instance, he the Levites being 'for the service of the ... in the courts and over the chambers, and over the cleansing of every holy thing' (1Ch_23:28), but P knows nothing of any chambers, would not have allowed the Levites to touch (much less clean) many of the holy things, and regarded service simply as porterage. In 1Ch_23:31 the Levites are to offer burnt offerings on certain occasions; in P their approach to the altar would have meant death both to themselves and the priests (Num_18:3). Other instances will be found in PS, 238 f.
(4) What the Foregoing Proves.
In view of these facts it is impossible to hold that the Levites in P represent a projection of the Levites of the second temple or any post-Mosaic age into the desert period. To P they are a body of sacred porters. The temple of course could not be carried about, and it cannot be held that in this respect the legislation mirrors later circumstances. “Secondly, the net result of such a scheme would be to create a body of Levites for use during the period of wanderings and never thereafter. As soon as the desert age was over the whole tribe would find their occupation gone. How can we conceive that any legislator deliberately sat down and invented such a scheme centuries after the epoch to which it relates, well knowing that in so far as his scheme purported to be a narrative of events it was fictitious from beginning to end, and in so far as it might be regarded as a legislation applicable to his own or any future day, there was not a line in it that could conceivably be put into practice? If any theorist can be conceived as acting in this way, how are we to suppose that his work would meet with acceptance?... Thirdly, P neither embodies the views of Ezekiel nor finds an accurate reflection in Chronicles. The facts are such as to enable us to say definitely that P is not in line with them. It is impossible to assume that he appointed the death penalty for certain acts if performed by Levites because he really wished the Levites to perform those acts” (PS, 241 f).
2. Aaron and His Sons:
Priests and Levites also speaks of Aaron the priest and the sons of Aaron the priest. It is doubtful whether the expression “the sons of Aaron the priests,” which occurs frequently in the Massoretic Text, is ever original; the Massoretic expression is nowhere supported by all the authorities. “The phrase ‛Aaron the high priest' is entirely unknown to Priests and Levites. Where the high priest's name is given the only qualifying apposition possible in his usage is 'the priest.' “ Aaron and his sons, unlike the Levites, were consecrated, not merely purified.
At this point two features only of the legislation need be noticed: the inadequacy of the staff to post-conquest conditions and the signs of date. For example, the leprosy laws (Lev 13 f) postulate the presence of priests to inspect and isolate the patient. “Remembering that on the critical theory P assumes the capital at Jerusalem as self-evident, we must ask how such provisions were to work after the conquest. During the desert period nothing could have been simpler, but what was to happen when the Israelites dwelt all over Canaan from Beersheba to Dan?” (PS, 246). The difficulty is immensely increased if we postulate an exilic or post-exilic date, when the Jewish center of gravity was in Babylonia and there were large colonies in Egypt and elsewhere. And “What are we to say when we read of leprous garments (Lev_13:47 ff)? Was a man to make the pilgrimage from Babylonia to Jerusalem to consult a priest about a doubtful garment? And what about the leper's offerings in Lev 14? Could they conceivably have been meant to apply to such circumstances?” (PS, 247). The case is no better with the law of leprous houses, which is expressed to apply to the post-conquest period (Lev_4:33 -53). The notification to the priest and his inspections require a priesthood scattered all over the country, i.e. a body far more numerous than the house of Aaron at the date of the conquest. Such instances could easily be multiplied from the legislation; one more only will be cited on account of its importance to the history of the priesthood. According to Leviticus, the individual sacrificant is to kill the victims and flay the burnt offerings. How could such procedure be applied to such sacrifices as those of Solomon (1Ki_8:63)? With the growth of luxury the sacrifices would necessarily become too large for such a ritual, and the wealthy would grow in refinement and object to performing such tasks personally. This suggests the reason for later abuses and for the modifications of Ezekiel and the representations of the Chronicler.
Result of the Evidence.
Thus, the evidence of P is unfavorable alike to the Wellhausen and the mediating views. The indications of date are consistently Mosaic, and it seems impossible to fit the laws into the framework of any other age without reading them in a sense that the legislator can be shown not to have contemplated. On the other hand P is a torso. It provides a large body of Levites who would have nothing to do after the conquest, and a corpus of legislation that could not have been administered in settled conditions by the house of Aaron alone.
III. The Other Portions of the Pentateuch.
In Exo_19:22, Exo_19:24 we read of priests, but a note has come down to us that in the first of those verses Aquila had “elders,” not “priests,” and this appears to be the correct reading in both places, as is shown by the prominence of the elders in the early part of the chapter. In Hebrew the words differ by only two letters. It is said by Wellhausen that in 
Exo_33:7-11 (E) Joshua has charge of the ark. This rests on a mistranslation of Exo_33:7, which should be rendered (correcting English Versions of the Bible), 'And Moses used to take a (or the) tent and pitch it for himself without the camp.' It is inconceivable that Moses should have taken the tent of the ark and removed it to a distance from the camp for his private use, leaving the ark bared and unguarded. Moreover, if he had done so, Joshua could not have been in charge of the ark, seeing that he was in this tent while the ark (ex hypothesi) remained in the camp. Nor had the ark yet been constructed. Nor was Joshua in fact a priest or the guardian of the ark in E: (1) in the Book of Joshua E knows of priests who carry the ark and are quite distinct from Joshua (3 ff); (2) in Deu_31:14 (E) Joshua is not resident in the tent of meeting; (3) in E, Aaron and Eleazar are priests (Deu_10:6), and the Levitical priesthood is the only one recognized (Deu_33:10); (4) there is no hint anywhere of Joshua's discharging any priestly duty whatsoever. The whole case rests on his presence in the tent in Exo_33:7-11, and, as shown in the article PENTATEUCH (which see), this passage should stand after Exo_13:22.
Then it is said that in Exo_4:14; Jdg_17:7, “Levite” denotes profession, not ancestry. In the latter passage the youth whom Micah made a priest was of Levitical descent, being the grandson of Moses (Jdg_17:13), and the case rests on the phrase, “of the family of Judah.” Neither of the Septuagintal translations had this text (Field, Hexapla, at the place), which therefore cannot be supported, since it cannot be suggested that Moses belonged to the tribe of Judah. As to Exo_4:14, the phrase “Aaron thy brother the Levite” is merely an adaptation of the more usual, “Aaron, son of Amram, the Levite,” rendered necessary by the fact that his brother Moses is the person addressed. The Wellhausen theory here is shown to be untenable in PS, 250 and RE3, XI, 418.
Exo_32:26-29 foreshadows the sacred character of Levi, and Deu_10:6 (E) knows the hereditary Aaronic priesthood. In D the most important passage is Deu_18:6-8. In Deu_18:7 three Septuagintal manuscripts omit the words “the Levites,” and if this be a gloss, the whole historic sense of the passage is changed. It now contains an enactment that any Levite coming to the religious capital may minister there “as all his brethren do, who stand there,” etc., i.e. like the descendants of Aaron. “The Levites” will then be the explanation of a glossator who was imbued with the latest post-exilic ideas, and thought that “his brethren” must mean those of his fellow-Levites who were not descended from Aaron. The passage is supplemented by Deu_21:5, giving to the Levites judicial rights, and Deu_24:8 assigning to them the duty of teaching the leprosy regulations. Together with Deu_33:10 (E), 'they shall teach thy judgments to Jacob and thy law to Israel: they shall put incense in thy nostrils and whole burnt-offering on thine altar,' these passages complete the provisions of P in giving to the Levites an occupation in place of their transport duties, and providing the necessary staff for administering the legislation when the Israelites were no longer massed together in a single camp, but scattered over the country. We shall see in the next section that this view of the meaning of the Law was taken by every writer of the second part of the Canon who touches on the subject. Everywhere we are confronted with the legitimacy of a Levitical priesthood; nowhere is there any mention of an exclusive Aaronic right. Smaller points which cannot be discussed here are examined in PS. It only remains to notice that these provisions fully explain the frequent Deuteronomic locution, “the priests the Levites.” One other remark must be made. Though it is not expressly stated, we may assume that consecration would be necessary in the case of any Levite acting on the provisions of Deu_18:6-8, and was not mentioned because in Hebrew antiquity it went without saying that every priest must be consecrated (compare Jdg_17:1-13).
IV. From Moses to Malachi.

text:
The Orphan of Yunnan Who Invited the Internet to His Wedding

In Yunnan Province a 24 year old orphan named Xu Xiaoxu is getting married on October 31 and his wedding has become the biggest story in China.

Xu lost his father at age 3. When he was 7 his mother remarried and left the village. He was raised by his grandmother and after she passed by his older brother. The brothers left school early and worked construction and delivery jobs. Over years Xu saved 167,500 yuan to pay for his own wedding.

He knew his wedding would be quiet. He had almost no relatives to fill even three tables. So he posted a short video on Douyin. He said he was an orphan with no family and invited strangers to come have a meal so his wedding would not be empty. He expected about 20 people.

The video went viral. By October 27 he had welcomed nearly 200 guests to his home two days early. By October 30 the mountain roads to Yiliang County in Zhaotong City were jammed with cars.

People are bringing gifts that show rural China. Live ducks, a pig, a cow, sacks of apples, a refrigerator, bedding, 9999 roses and even a used Audi. One man offered his Maybach as the lead wedding car for free.

Forty volunteer chefs are cooking a flowing water banquet where tables are added as more people arrive. Wedding planners drove from Henan Province to decorate for free. Villagers installed new streetlights and China Mobile added temporary 5G stations for livestreams.

What moved people is simple. In Chinese weddings parents and uncles usually lead the ceremony. Xu had no one. Commenters wrote we will be your uncle, we will be your aunt. On October 31 his brother will stand in as family while thousands of strangers who decided he should not marry alone fill the courtyard.

text:
The plan briefed to Sen. Chris Murphy includes a landing on Iranian islands, Kharg and Qeshm among the names.

Qeshm is the largest. "You'd need what, 75, 100,000 troops to take this island, and we don't have that. We have maybe 10,000 total," per Daniel Davis.

The smaller islands offered instead sit inside the range of every missile, drone and artillery piece on the mainland: "nowhere to hide there. You'd be just sitting ducks."

Trump's own Pentagon has warned him the result would be "a visual debacle of a bunch of US soldiers taken out or effectively held hostage," per Robert Barnes.

The generals' objection in one sentence: "We can get them there. It's keeping them there and getting them out that is the problem."

The islands can be reached. They cannot be held.

text:
Short version: I should’ve said the government *helped* make her.But yes, it did.

Longer version: Parents bear the primary and heaviest responsibility for the conditions that shaped Christa Pike, but the record shows a series of clear government institutional failures that left her unprotected and untreated long before the 1995 murder.

—

Details: Her mother drank heavily during pregnancy, both parents were alcoholic and neglectful, the household was chaotic and violent, and she was repeatedly left in the care of people who abused her. The state did not create those parents or that home; they did.

When Pike was a toddler and still in preschool, she was sexually abused by her grandmother’s boyfriend. After she started school, she drew a man with a large penis and a demonic face when asked what happened at home. School staff contacted the parents. Child protective services and police were never called. No investigation followed. The abuse continued until kindergarten.

At age 11 she was raped by a neighbor. Her mother initially did not believe her. Only after a teacher noticed the resulting infection did the case reach authorities. The man pleaded to a lesser charge, received a short sentence, and returned to the neighborhood. No sustained protective or therapeutic intervention for Pike is documented.

Around the same period, after further physical and sexual abuse by one of her mother’s boyfriends, North Carolina social services temporarily removed her from the home. She was returned after roughly three months with minimal follow-up. The same household conditions resumed.

At age 12, after the death of the one relative she described as nurturing, she attempted suicide by overdose. She received some psychiatric contact, but the evaluations and later accounts indicate no consistent treatment for the accumulating trauma, depression, or emerging bipolar and PTSD symptoms. Brain damage linked to prenatal alcohol exposure and early seizures also went largely unaddressed.

She later entered the juvenile system after a minor property offense (breaking into a community center). The Juvenile Evaluation Center in North Carolina, by then operating under a more punitive points-based model, held her longer than most children. It produced a GED and a temporary role as a teacher’s assistant, but did not resolve the underlying trauma, mental-health issues, or family dysfunction. She was released and enrolled in Job Corps at 18, still untreated.

In short, schools flagged sexual abuse and received no institutional follow-through; a documented child rape produced only a brief, incomplete prosecution; child protective services removed and quickly returned her without lasting safeguards; mental-health and juvenile systems offered episodic contact rather than sustained intervention. These were not ambiguous gray areas. They were repeated points at which the state was notified, or should have been, and failed to act in ways that might have interrupted the trajectory.

None of this excuses the torture-murder of Colleen Slemmer. Most people who endure severe childhood abuse never kill anyone. Parental failure remains the root. But the documented pattern of missed interventions by schools, child protective services, police, and the juvenile system means the state also failed her repeatedly in the years before the crime. Those failures did not create the monster alone, but they left the damage unmitigated.

text:
From Claude: “**Short answer:** Soddy and Rand agree on a slogan and disagree on almost everything else, including who the villain is. I read Soddy's front matter and chs. I-IV, plus excerpts from chs. V and VIII (about 15 of 130 pages, from OCR text). Everything below about Rand is from my knowledge of the novel.

**Where they agree**
- Money is a claim on goods, not wealth itself.
- Creating money without matching production is a quiet transfer. Soddy's version (p. 30): "Ex nihilo nihil fit," and modern money is "an apparent outstanding exception" to the rule that you can't get something for nothing.

**Where they split**

| | Rand/Francisco (and the post) | Soddy, *Money versus Man* (1931) |
|---|---|---|
| Who creates the problem | Government printing | Private banks: "Every loan makes a deposit" (pp. 38-39). A "loan" is "a creation of new money." |
| Remedy | Gold, minimal state | State-issued money, banks lend only existing money, stable price index. He criticizes the 1925 return to gold. |
| Constraint on wealth | Production, driven by the mind | Energy: it "is not of fundamental importance" whether the work comes from a man or a donkey-engine (p. 31). |
| Diagnosis of the 1920s-30s | Producers withdraw when expropriated | Glut, not scarcity: "the problem of producing wealth has been essentially solved" (pp. 15-16). The failure is distribution and deflation from banks cancelling credit. |
| Moral frame | Producer versus looter | Ruskin's epigraph: "There is no wealth but life." Consumption is the end of production. |

**Where each is stronger**
- **Soddy** describes bank deposit creation accurately. As far as I know, the Bank of England's 2014 paper confirms it, though I haven't checked that this session. This hits the post's "government prints" framing, since most money is bank credit.
- **Soddy** is weaker on the "conservation law" analogy, because money isn't conserved like energy. His glut thesis predates Keynes's *General Theory* (1936), and the post-WWII record is mixed. Mainstream economics treats him as heterodox, though Irving Fisher's 100% reserve proposal drew on his work.
- **Rand** is weaker on banking, as noted earlier. She is stronger on rent-seeking.

**What this does to the post:** it names a single villain (government) and a single remedy (gold). Soddy shows an author reading the same facts and indicting banks, and condemning the gold return for causing depression. The post's hyperinflation list also omits the deflationary failures Soddy writes about (1921).

**Next check:** the primary-source map I offered (Hume 1752, Smith 1776, Reichsbank/Zimbabwe data, the speech text). I haven't started it. Do you want it?”

text:
TWO PRESIDENTS, TWO VERY DIFFERENT MOMENTS WITH AMERICAN WAR HEROES 🇺🇦🇺🇸🇫🇷

When Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met Melvin Hurwitz, an American World War II veteran, the elderly soldier reached for his hand and attempted to kiss it. Zelenskyy gently pulled his hand away, lowered himself to the veteran’s level and embraced him instead.

What followed was a deeply moving exchange.

Veteran: “You’re the savior of the people!”

Zelenskyy: “No, no, no. You saved Europe.”

Veteran: “You bring tears to my eyes. You are my hero.”

Zelenskyy: “No, no, you are our hero.”

Veteran: “I pray for you.”

The encounter offers a contrast with controversies surrounding Donald Trump’s remarks and treatment of American military service members.

During a 2018 visit to France marking the centenary of the end of World War I, Trump cancelled a planned visit to the Aisne-Marne American Cemetery, where 2,289 American military personnel are buried. According to accounts published by The Atlantic, Trump privately questioned why he should visit a cemetery filled with “losers” and referred to fallen Marines at Belleau Wood as “suckers.” Trump has denied making those remarks.

The soldiers who died at Belleau Wood were fighting Germany in World War I, not the Nazi regime of World War II.

In 2024, Trump also attracted criticism for comparing the Presidential Medal of Freedom with the Medal of Honor. He called the civilian decoration “much better” while noting that Medal of Honor recipients are often severely wounded or awarded the distinction posthumously.

In 2025, Trump was criticised for playing golf in Florida rather than attending a dignified transfer ceremony for four fallen American service members, although presidential attendance at such ceremonies is not mandatory.

Zelenskyy’s exchange with Hurwitz was a simple moment of mutual respect between two men from different generations, both shaped by wars in Europe.

Neither wanted to be called a hero. Each insisted that the other deserved the honour.

text:
Three more nights. As much as we talk HHN year round that haunt season never really ends for us, there’s still something bittersweet about watching THIS event come to an end.

A recent post by @ZombieCT got us thinking about something that makes each HHN so special. You’ll never experience this exact iteration of the event again.

Years from now, we’ll get to look back and say, “We were there for HHN 35.” The Infernal Carnival of Nightmares. The year Jack and Oddfellow took over the event. The houses, the scare zones, the icons and scare actors, that carnival atmosphere… all part of an experience that existed for just a couple months and will never be the same again. HHN is an event that’s meant to change and evolve. It’s one of the best things about it, allowing new original stories and IPs to come to life each year. But it’s also one of the hardest parts of being a fan, knowing that the houses and scare zones we’ve grown to love over the course of the event may never be experienced the same way/if at all, again.

To HHN Creative and the Art & Design teams: Thank you for continuing to build these incredible stories and worlds that allow us to completely lose ourselves in. Being able to escape the stresses of everyday life and spend a few nights wandering through the fog at Universal Studios Florida is something we look forward to every single year, just like so many other maniacs.

To the HHN fan community: Thank you for sharing your experiences throughout the event, documenting your walkthroughs and adventures so we can revisit them years from now, interacting with us here on X, and for those that listen to us on the ITSZ Podcast. We genuinely enjoy being a small part of your HHN experience, not just during the event, but all year long.

And above all, to the scareactors: You’ve heard it before, but you truly are the heart and soul of Halloween Horror Nights. Whether you’re out in the zones finding new and creative ways to scare and interact with guests, or inside the houses repeating those same carefully timed movements night after night to deliver the perfect scare and tell your story, we see and appreciate the effort. We know this event is a marathon for you, and the energy, dedication, and passion you bring to it are what make these worlds come alive. Thank you for giving it your all.

So while HHN 35 may soon be officially put to rest, our conversations about it are just getting started. And with next year’s codenames already out, speculation season is right around the corner! 👀 We may never walk through these exact houses or scare zones again, but we’ll carry those memories with us for years to come. To all involved in bringing the Infernal Carnival of Nightmares to life: THANK YOU! 

So for those still able to attend, enjoy these last few nights in the fog! Take it all in, make a few more memories, and enjoy everything HHN 35 has left to offer. The carnival may be coming to an end, but the fog will be back before we know it. And we'll all be right there waiting for it! #HHN35 #HHNForever

BREAKING: Meta SUSPENDS Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon's Latino voter organizing Instagram account in the middle of a get-out-the-vote rally – just ONE WEEK before the midterm elections!

Nixon's Instagram account, @latinosconangie, suddenly went dark Tuesday as her campaign mobilized voters at a Florida rally featuring Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and other Democratic lawmakers.

Meta accused the account of violating its rules on “account integrity,” but offered no specific explanation. The account was restored Wednesday morning after being offline for more than an hour.

Nixon isn't the first to experience this.
On October 17, Meta suspended the No Kings Coalition's Instagram account during a nationwide voter-mobilization event. The company later apologized, blaming automated security systems that mistook heavy activity for suspicious traffic.

Now 14 state attorneys general are demanding answers from Meta about that earlier suspension, including what safeguards the company has in place to prevent similar disruptions as Election Day approaches.

While there is no concrete evidence that Meta deliberately targeted Nixon's campaign for political reasons, the timing could hardly have been worse for a candidate trying to reach voters in the final days before November 3.

With the midterms days away, campaigns need their organizing tools to work. Meta still hasn't publicly explained why Nixon's account was shut down at such a critical moment.

It owes that explanation to everyone who cares about American democracy.

Baptist history deserves to be read—not left buried in old scans and out-of-print books.

Through "The Baptist Bookshelf", I’m bringing public-domain Baptist books back into circulation in clean, readable editions. These works tell the stories of missionaries, pastors, churches, and ordinary believers whose lives helped shape Baptist history. The work includes correcting scanning errors, restoring readable formatting, and carefully checking the text while preserving the authors’ historical language.

Recent additions include:

📚 **Fifty Years in China** — the story of Tarleton Perry Crawford and a half century of missionary work, hardship, and debate over how missions should be supported.

📚 **Flowers and Fruits in the Wilderness** — Z. N. Morrell’s firsthand account of pioneer Baptist life in Texas, from frontier preaching to the growth of churches and associations.

📚 **John Gano’s memoirs** — the recollections of a Baptist pastor whose ministry stretched from colonial America through service as a Revolutionary War chaplain and his later years in Kentucky.

📚 **Hair-breadth Escapes from Slavery to Freedom** — Baptist minister William Troy’s account of his own life and the journeys of people who escaped slavery.

You can find Kindle and paperback options on Amazon through the Bookshelf page, or browse 35 digital titles on Gumroad, most with both a PDF and an EPUB for your preferred reading app.

text:
This exact email framework has booked me more meetings than I can count. And now AI writes it all.

{{firstName}}, reaching out because you guys just did a 3.2M multifamily bridge in Austin, so this could be relevant.

If we could introduce you to more sponsors financing similar transactions around Texas, would that be worth a conversation?

The first line comes from the lender’s website. 

The harness crawls it, finds a recent transaction, pulls the loan type, amount, property type and location, and saves the URL in that lender’s row. 

Then it checks that the transaction was actually theirs. 

If the site doesn’t give it enough context, I want {not enough context} in the row, not an opener it guessed.

The second line comes from the offer and the rest of that row. 

-Who does this lender finance? 
-What transactions do they want more of? 
-Which states do they cover? 
-What kind of borrowers can we actually bring them? 

I give the harness the offer we’re able to fulfill, and it writes that line around the borrower and transaction that make sense for this lender.

Here’s what has to happen before it can write either line:

1. Pull the list through your data providers and have the harness score every company yes, no, or review. 

Do they actually lend? 
What property types do they finance? 
Which states? 

I don’t want a company staying in my campaign because some database called them a bridge lender. 

Their site + my agent need to validate it because there’s always fat that bleeds into lists.

2. For every yes, crawl the site more and fill out what is basically a mini onboarding form in that row. 

Their products, the borrowers they work with, loan sizes if they publish them, coverage states, recent transactions, case studies, what they say makes them different, and the URLs where all of that came from. 

You’re trying to get the information you’d ask them for if they were already your client, before you write to them.

3. Give the harness access to your scraper and crawler, enrichment APIs, a copywriting skill, and the MD files that let it be an extension of somebody who knows what they’re doing. 

memory.md holds your offer, case studies, previous campaigns, previous copy, etc..

decisions.md holds the fit rules, the offers you’ve tested, claims you can make, and the shit you’ve already decided not to say. 

Otherwise you’re asking it to start from scratch every time.

4. Point the writing agent at the completed row and the offer. 

Have it find the connective tissue between what we can bring them and their services, clients, transactions, case studies, anything we can latch onto in order to create RELEVANCE. 

That’s what makes the email feel 1 to 1. 

It writes the opener and the offer line from that, then fills the variables in the lead sheet.

5. Flip through the finished emails next to the source pages. 

I want it to look like we went to their site, got their email, and wrote to them while driving and texting with one hand. It can sound a little rough. 

That’s where most of our effort goes. 

Pulling the right companies, scoring them, filling out those rows, and figuring out what offer actually belongs in front of each group.

I said, “Sir, if I give this away, I genuinely don't know what I'll eat next week.”

He told me I needed to trust God.

I understood what he was saying, but honestly, I couldn't do it.

I told him I wasn't going to give away the little money I had left when I didn't even know where my next meal was coming from.

He looked disappointed.

“You need more faith.”

I went home feeling terrible.

For days, that conversation kept playing in my head.

Then, completely out of nowhere, I got a call about a job.

The offer?

$15,000 every week for five years.

I genuinely thought they had made a mistake.

I called back to confirm.

They hadn't.

I just sat there staring at my phone, thinking about that conversation with my pastor.

text:
Agentic AI at Scale: The Economics of Control, Compute and Enterprise Autonomy- Agentic AI at Scale: Why the Next Corporate Crisis May Be the Cost of Autonomy
The race to deploy artificial intelligence inside corporations is approaching a financial contradiction that few technology budgets are designed to absorb. Gartner projects that the average global Fortune 500 company could move from fewer than 15 AI agents in 2025 to more than 150,000 by 2028, yet only 13% of organisations believe they possess adequate governance over these systems. Meanwhile, global data-centre electricity consumption is expected to approach 950 TWh by 2030, and memory prices are rising under pressure from AI infrastructure demand. The central question is no longer how many autonomous systems companies can deploy, but whether their economic contribution will exceed the combined cost of computation, infrastructure, supervision and control. The next competitive divide will separate enterprises capable of converting machine autonomy into measurable financial returns from those accumulating expensive digital activity without corresponding productivity.

The 150,000-Agent Forecast Conceals a Much Larger Management Problem
Gartner’s April 28, 2026 projection represents a potential increase exceeding 10,000-fold in enterprise agent populations within three years. Yet the headline number obscures a distinction that will determine the economics of adoption: a registered agent is not necessarily an active agent, and an active agent is not necessarily producing useful work. A corporation with 150,000 largely dormant agents could generate less inference expenditure than one operating 5,000 continuously active systems. At the same time, its inventory of machine identities, permissions and operational dependencies could be vastly more difficult to administer. Counting agents without measuring activity and accepted outcomes risks creating a new corporate performance indicator disconnected from productivity.

The warning is already visible in Gartner’s forecasts. In June 2025, the research firm predicted that more than 40% of agentic AI projects would be cancelled by the end of 2027 because of escalating costs, uncertain business value or inadequate risk controls. In May 2026, it separately anticipated that 40% of enterprises would demote or decommission autonomous agents because of governance shortcomings. These forecasts measure different phenomena and cannot be combined into a single failure rate. Their common implication, however, is unmistakable: enterprises are acquiring autonomous capabilities faster than they are developing the managerial systems required to operate them economically.

The difficulty is structural. Conventional business software largely executes predefined functions. Autonomous agents can interpret objectives, select tools, retrieve information, delegate work and repeat operations until a task is completed or abandoned. Each additional execution path introduces potential expenditure and operational consequences. When machine actors can generate further machine activity, the relevant financial exposure is no longer determined exclusively by the original human request.

Cheaper Intelligence Is Not the Same as Cheaper Operations
Stanford University’s 2025 AI Index documented a remarkable reduction in the price of model capability: the cost of querying a system achieving a specified GPT-3.5-equivalent benchmark level fell from approximately $20 to $0.07 per million tokens between November 2022 and October 2024. The same report identified annual improvements of approximately 43% in hardware performance, a 30% reduction in hardware cost per unit of performance and a 40% improvement in energy efficiency. These figures contradict the assumption that computational intelligence must inevitably become more expensive. They do not, however, establish that the total cost of autonomous corporate operations will decline.

The distinction becomes clear when model consumption is translated into enterprise expenditure. An illustrative estate of 150,000 agents making ten model calls daily would generate approximately 547.5 million calls annually. At an assumed price of $0.01 per call, inference alone would cost $5.475 million per year, before orchestration, retrieval, security, monitoring, human review and infrastructure commitments. Increasing execution intensity to 100 calls daily would raise that direct expenditure to $54.75 million under otherwise unchanged assumptions. These are financial sensitivities, not forecasts, but they expose the central weakness of investment plans based on declining token prices: consumption can expand considerably faster than the price of individual operations falls.

The physical supply chain adds another source of uncertainty. On September 30, 2026, TrendForce projected fourth-quarter increases of 10–15% in conventional DRAM contract prices and 15–20% in NAND Flash prices. These movements cannot be applied directly to GPU costs or inference-service tariffs, but they demonstrate that semiconductor inputs are not following a uniformly deflationary trajectory. NVIDIA’s published accelerator specifications illustrate the growing importance of memory: the H100 SXM provides 80 GB of high-bandwidth memory, the H200 provides 141 GB and the B200 provides 180 GB, with substantially greater memory bandwidth in successive generations. For autonomous systems maintaining long contexts and numerous concurrent requests, memory availability can constrain throughput even when arithmetic processing capacity is sufficient.

The real economic unit is consequently neither the GPU-hour nor the million tokens. It is the fully loaded cost of a correctly completed business task, including failed attempts, duplicated operations, infrastructure consumption and human correction. A more expensive model completing a workflow reliably in fewer steps may be cheaper than a nominally inexpensive model requiring repeated execution.

The Infrastructure Boom Creates a Capital-Allocation Test
The International Energy Agency’s April 2026 assessment projected global data-centre electricity consumption increasing from approximately 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030. The IEA also reported that capital expenditure by the largest technology companies exceeded $400 billion in 2025 and was expected to increase by another 75% during 2026. These figures concern the wider AI and data-centre infrastructure expansion, not enterprise agents alone. Nevertheless, they reveal the industrial consequences of making computation a continuously available production resource.

Electricity is only one component of the investment. Advanced inference infrastructure requires accelerators, high-bandwidth memory, network equipment, cooling, grid connections and financing. The Uptime Institute’s 2025 Global Data Center Survey reported an average power usage effectiveness of 1.54, illustrating the additional facility electricity required beyond the IT equipment itself. A hypothetical installation sustaining 1 MW of IT load throughout the year would consume approximately 13.49 GWh at that efficiency level. At $0.10 per kWh, its annual electricity bill would approach $1.35 million, excluding hardware acquisition, maintenance and capital recovery.

The financial consequences differ sharply between cloud customers and infrastructure owners. Consumption-based APIs transfer much of the hardware and utilisation risk to providers but expose enterprises to fluctuating demand, supplier pricing and contractual dependence. Dedicated accelerators offer greater operating control but can become expensive when capacity remains idle. Owned infrastructure adds depreciation, financing, equipment replacement and facility obligations. The IEA’s identification of memory shortages, electrical-equipment constraints and delayed grid connections makes the distinction more consequential: purchasing computing hardware does not guarantee that commissioned, economically productive capacity will be available when required.

For directors, the investment question is whether demand is sufficiently predictable to justify fixed capacity or whether flexible procurement remains preferable. Infrastructure ownership is not evidence of technological maturity if the resulting assets cannot achieve an acceptable rate of productive utilisation.

Governance Is Becoming Part of the Production Cost
The security of autonomous systems cannot rest on instructions telling a model to behave appropriately. On October 27, 2026, the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology published design tenets for agent identity management, emphasising identifiable machine actors, traceable delegation, restricted permissions and independently enforceable authorisation. The implications extend beyond cybersecurity. If an agent can initiate transactions, access confidential information or delegate operations to other agents, the corporation must determine not merely whether it is authenticated, but whether each consequential action falls within the authority originally granted.

The economics of this requirement are substantial. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 identifies threats involving tool misuse, privilege abuse, poisoned context, insecure inter-agent communications and cascading failures. Controls against these mechanisms require execution isolation, monitoring, revocation, audit trails and, for consequential operations, human approval. Yet universal manual supervision can destroy the productivity gains that justified automation. Under an illustrative workload of one million annual agent actions, reviewing 10% of them for two minutes each at a loaded labour cost of $60 per hour produces $200,000 in review expenditure; reviewing every action would cost $2 million.

The appropriate response is differentiated authority. Gartner’s May 2026 framework distinguishes agents that Observe, Advise, Act with Approval and Act Autonomously. A system preparing internal summaries does not justify the same operating restrictions as one modifying production infrastructure or initiating financial transactions. Equally, an agent capable of acting autonomously should not be permitted to determine the limits of its own authority. The financial advantage lies in automating routine enforcement while reserving intensive human oversight for operations whose consequences justify the additional cost.

Europe Is Building Capacity, but Industrial Adoption Will Determine the Return
The European Commission’s AI Continent Action Plan seeks to mobilise €200 billion in investment, including a €20 billion facility intended to support up to five AI gigafactories. The EuroHPC network identifies 19 AI Factories and 13 associated antennas. These programmes demonstrate Europe’s effort to expand access to computing infrastructure and technological expertise, but investment mobilisation, procurement decisions and commissioned computing capacity are different stages of implementation. None establishes that industrial users have already achieved corresponding improvements in productivity.

The national differences matter. Italy’s IT4LIA initiative, linked to CINECA and the Bologna Tecnopolo, offers a route toward AI capability for manufacturing, engineering and specialised enterprises. A EuroHPC procurement notice identified an estimated €290 million value for an associated AI-optimised supercomputer; that procurement figure is not evidence of completed expenditure. Germany’s HammerHAI and JUPITER initiatives target applications including manufacturing, mobility and industrial research. EuroHPC’s March 16, 2026 announcement of the HammerHAI contract described more than 15 exaflops of peak AI inference performance, a technical specification rather than a measure of commercial productivity.

France’s AI2F initiative, led by GENCI with research partners including CEA, CNRS and Inria, connects computing infrastructure with sectors ranging from aerospace and energy to healthcare and finance. On July 30, 2026, the French government confirmed its interest in hosting a European AI gigafactory, linking computing investment with energy, supply-chain and data-security considerations. The United Kingdom’s January 2025 AI Opportunities Action Plan and its AI Growth Zones programme pursue a different combination of infrastructure development, business adoption and public-service transformation.

These national approaches will compete on their capacity to translate investment into accepted industrial output. For Italian and German manufacturers, the return may appear in reduced downtime, better engineering documentation or shorter production cycles. For French strategic industries, controlled infrastructure and data governance may carry additional value. For British financial and professional services, the decisive variable may be the quality and cost of completed analytical work. The European risk is that infrastructure spending advances more rapidly than companies’ ability to integrate AI into productive processes.

The regulatory timetable adds a further constraint. The EU AI Act’s amended implementation schedule establishes December 2, 2027 for relevant standalone high-risk AI systems and August 2, 2028 for high-risk systems embedded in products. Not every enterprise agent falls into those categories, but affected organisations must incorporate the applicable obligations into system design and investment planning. Compliance introduced after production deployment can require expensive reconstruction of processes whose technical architecture has already become embedded in daily operations.

The Next 24 Months Will Expose the Difference Between Adoption and Return
The evidence from 2025–2026 points toward a decisive test during 2027–2028. Gartner’s projected project cancellations and agent decommissioning will test whether organisations can distinguish commercially useful autonomy from uncontrolled proliferation. The revised European regulatory dates will test whether compliance has been incorporated into deployment rather than treated as a subsequent administrative exercise. The expansion of data-centre infrastructure will test whether committed capital can achieve productive utilisation as hardware generations, memory markets and electricity constraints evolve.

The workforce dimension reinforces the uncertainty. The International Labour Organization estimated in May 2025 that approximately one quarter of global employment was exposed to generative AI to some degree, but exposure does not imply equivalent job displacement or realised savings. METR’s July 2025 experiment found that experienced open-source developers took approximately 19% longer on selected tasks when using early-2025 AI tools. Its February 2026 update suggested possible improvements with newer systems but identified methodological limitations preventing a reliable general estimate. Faster generation of code and documents cannot be booked as productivity until testing, correction, supervision and maintenance have been included.

Boards should therefore require every material agentic investment to demonstrate its cost per accepted outcome, first-pass completion rate, human intervention burden, utilisation, financial contribution and tested ability to terminate unauthorised execution. A deployment that repeatedly exceeds the cost of its established alternative without delivering compensating quality or risk benefits should lose its entitlement to further scaling capital, regardless of the sophistication of the underlying model.

Over the next 12–24 months, the cost of inaction will fall on shareholders financing underutilised infrastructure, employees absorbing additional verification work, customers exposed to unreliable automation and public institutions committing resources without measurable service improvements. The penalty for indiscriminate adoption will be equally concrete: higher operating expenditure, greater supplier dependence and increasingly expensive remediation of poorly integrated systems.

The central divide by 2028 will not be between corporations with artificial intelligence and those without it. It will be between enterprises that can demonstrate a financial return on autonomous execution and those that can measure only how much autonomy they have purchased.

text:
Moonshot AI launches Kimi 3D Make

It’s time to dive into something that could shake up the world of 3D modeling. Moonshot AI has just launched a new tool called Kimi 3D Make, which promises to revolutionize how we create complex 3D models and scenes.

So, what exactly is Kimi 3D Make? Is it just another image-to-3D model generator, or something more substantial?
Bridging the Gap Between AI and Professional Modeling

Kimi 3D Make isn’t your run-of-the-mill design tool. It’s an AI agent that integrates seamlessly with professional-grade software like Blender. This means you can give it instructions in plain language or through visual sketches, and it will generate detailed 3D models for you.

But wait a minute—aren’t there already plenty of AI-driven tools out there? What makes Kimi 3D Make stand out?
A Hands-On Approach to Design

The key differentiator is the hands-on approach. While other tools might focus on generating ready-made models, Kimi 3D Make aims to be an intelligent assistant that lives within your favorite software. It can write and execute scripts, create geometry, assemble scenes, and even modify existing projects based on your input.

This isn’t just about creating objects; it’s about building interactive websites, game prototypes, and 3D prints—all through a user-friendly AI interface. For instance, if you’re working on a complex architectural model or an intricate character design for a video game, Kimi 3D Make can help automate repetitive tasks and speed up the creative process.
How Does Kimi 3D Make Work?

Under the hood, Kimi 3D Make uses large language models (LLMs) to understand natural language commands. You can describe your vision in text or sketch it out quickly, and the tool will translate those instructions into detailed 3D models within Blender or other CAD systems.

Imagine describing a futuristic cityscape in plain English, and having Kimi 3D Make generate that scene for you. It’s like having an AI assistant that speaks your design language fluently. For example, if you say "Create a Gothic cathedral with flying buttresses," the tool will interpret this command and start building the model based on architectural principles.
What Is Stored and Excluded

When you use Kimi 3D Make, the tool stores your input data such as text descriptions and sketches to generate models accurately. However, it does not store any personal information or sensitive data about users unless explicitly provided through user settings. The generated models are stored in your project files within Blender or other CAD systems.

What is excluded from storage includes any private notes or comments you might make during the design process that aren’t directly related to generating 3D content. Additionally, Kimi 3D Make does not retain any data about users unless they opt-in through specific settings. This ensures that your creative work remains confidential and under your control.
User Controls

Users have control over their data and can manage privacy settings within the tool’s interface. You can choose whether or not to share your project files with Moonshot AI for improvement purposes. This ensures that you maintain full ownership of your creative work while benefiting from potential advancements in AI technology.

For instance, if you’re working on a highly confidential design project, you can disable data sharing and keep all your work private within the tool’s environment. Conversely, if you want to contribute to the development of Kimi 3D Make by providing feedback or sample projects, you can opt-in for data sharing with Moonshot AI.
Availability and Accessibility

Kimi 3D Make is currently available as a plugin for Blender, making it accessible to users who already have the software installed. The tool can be downloaded directly from Moonshot AI’s website or through their dedicated app store. Future updates may include compatibility with other CAD systems like AutoCAD and SketchUp.

This means that if you’re an experienced Blender user, you can start using Kimi 3D Make right away without any additional setup. However, for users who work primarily in other CAD software, the future compatibility plans offer a promising outlook on how this tool could integrate into their workflow.
What This Does Not Prove

While Kimi 3D Make promises significant improvements in efficiency and creativity, it does not prove that all complex 3D modeling tasks can be fully automated without human oversight. The tool relies on clear user input to generate accurate models, which means the quality of output depends heavily on how well you communicate your vision.

For example, if you’re trying to create a highly detailed mechanical part with specific dimensions and materials, Kimi 3D Make will need precise instructions to produce an accurate model. This highlights that while AI can handle many aspects of design, human expertise remains crucial for complex projects.
Practical Takeaway

If you’re a designer or artist working in the realm of 3D modeling, this could be your chance to explore new possibilities. Give Kimi 3D Make a try and see if it can streamline your workflow and help bring your ideas to life faster than ever before.

So, what do you think about Kimi 3D Make? Is this something that will change the game for 3D modeling, or is it just another tech demo?

text:
He said the fourth thing is updating the firmware — because routers are computers, and computers need security patches.

Most people never update their router's firmware. They set it up once and forget it exists. The firmware is the operating system running on the router. It has vulnerabilities. It gets patched.

"Router firmware updates are usually made to improve a router's security. Even if you have purchased a new router, it may not be up to date on the latest firmware. Some routers automatically check for firmware updates, but not all. Check the admin panel under Administration or System. Turn on automatic updates if your router offers them" .

text:
He said the third thing — and the one that makes the biggest speed difference — is manually setting your Wi-Fi channel instead of leaving it on auto.

Most routers pick a channel at setup and never change it. In a densely populated area, you're sharing that channel with every neighbor.

"The 2.4 GHz band only offers three non-overlapping channels: 1, 6, and 11. If you live in a densely populated area, you might be sharing the same channel with other routers, which causes signal interference that slows down your connection. Use a Wi-Fi analyzer app to see which channels are crowded, then set your router to a clear channel manually. For 2.4 GHz, stick to 1, 6, or 11. On 5 GHz, you have more flexibility" .

Of course. I'd met Congressman Huffman a few times and had been to many town hall meetings that are well attended, informative, mostly respectful, and polite. Our district is huge, north of the Golden Gate, Redwoods, wine country, and the Farallons National Marine Sanctuary which can bring in over a $1B a year (fishing and tourism mostly) He lives in Marin County, where if you make less that $105k, you qualify for food stamps no kidding.  Hot tubs and Teslas and $12 coffees...

31 miles out from GG bridge are the Farallon Islands, once a world-class seabird rookery which are now infested with mice. Many years ago it was decided that an eradication program was in order but of course we had to have a public comment period. Here we are 15 years or so and those damn mice are still there. I had just gotten back from Palmyra Atoll working for TNC (The Nature Conservancy) 1000 miles south of Hawaii.

We had rats there. Lots of them. One of the last best reefs on Earth... and rats were killing the whole place, including the reef (long complex story) Nuclear is my think global issue and Farallons House Mouse Eradication Project my act local issue. Palmyra rats are gone, TNC spent millions spreading 5x (iirc) the amount of poison on Palmyra (second attempt). It worked. The place thrives now.

So what's the hold-up on the Farallones? NRDC, Mothers for Peace, Greenpeace, chemophobia, salmon and fishing interests, and most significantly animal activists (I am one of those) But here I was making the case for birds and for killing the mice with poison (super complex story, too long for here) I make my case for putting 2 tons of poison BAIT on 125 acres at a public comment meeting... may 100 people there, packed! Only 3 speakers out of maybe 20 where in favor of it... me being far and away most prepared... I had pictures of bloody birds being eaten alive etc.

I explained that the poison brodifacoum/25 was mostly bait, the 25 was ppm, a metric ton has a million grams and so only 25 of those grams were the poison and 2 tons is like a sugar cube per acre of poison and the rest is corn. I was re-explaining this to some people at break time in the parking lot... when I was done a lady came up to me and said "wow Tim I think you just changed my mind" I looked at her and said

"Great, now care to try for nuclear?" The look on her face has been a highlight of my nuclear advocacy life!

So I thought I'll try that on Huffman. "Yes, we can talk in my office but no nuclear Tim!" It tured out that he was well aware of the issues "Oh I know Richard (my main antagonist) and I got the impression that Richard had been in there peddling his chemophobia bs more than once etc. This is when I brought up NRDC and the gross hypocrisy of not wanting offshore oil wells but oh 155MW of offshore wind was just fine, the gross hypocrisy of wanting to save a bunch of mice (most but not all starve to death every year) wanting to save those but to hell with the birds, wanting to save Gulls but not Ashy Storm Petrels (same Gulls that ride the garbage trucks to dump), don't kill the cats on the channel islands, airlift the goats off, 1000 saucers of liquid rodent birth control (actual suggestion)

ALL instead of 50grams of poison...

After all that Huffman the ex NRDC lawyer, popular, tall, super good looking, nice, smart guy... says to me:

"I'm not gonna die on that (political) hill"

Same with nuclear: "if someone wants to build a nuke somewhere I wouldn't oppose it... but not here"

Same with Roundup: In Marin County PG&E is prohibited from spraying around their equipment (poles) even though we are all terrified of the fire risk. Yo can drink Roundup. I have offered to do so in public. On one condition; that they stfu about Roundup.

RE this permitting bill: if it makes it easier to out up more junk RE to hell with it. The bs around permitting has nothing to do with AC physics. People throw the word "transmission" around like dice.

Huffman's been high on this 155MW offshore wind project for ? years now. You'd be able to see it from the site of the old 60MW Humboldt nuclear plant. The fishermen up there need an ice plant but the people in Humboldt are scared of nuclear... so they are faced with several dilemmas: ice/no ice, 155 MWs of fugly OR a nuke (yeah right!)(Peabody wanted to spend a $1B fixing up the train tracks (no way) to ship a unit of coal there every day, ostensibly to China out of Eureka.

So in order for Huffman and the offshore wind fanboys to get this 155MW of fugly going they'd have to build roads, docks, concrete plants, bigger boats, cranes, fueling... No one wants that. But we have all this permitting reform coming up... awkward! Break out the chainsaws! Start the big Caterpillars... Peoria needs the money!

Too long? Tough. I've wasted so many hours of my life reading about unreasonable energy bs on twitter/fb mostly about money and wackadoodle projections of 60 giggle watts of sunbeams and cool breezes and that we don't need nukes. This bill is more about the fallacy that RE builds out faster than nuclear than it is about AC physics/energy. They think permitting is what holds up RE.

Vogtle was about 3.65 days per MW to build. We should have had this 155MW wind farm built in 2 years.

I wrote all this, not AI... but I'm a big fan of AI for math and physics and discussing books.

text:
Kevin Costner’s wife asked for $248,000 a month in child support. In court, she said she didn’t know how she’d afford groceries.

They had a prenup. It gave her 30 days to leave his house after she filed for divorce. A judge had to order her out.

They married in 2004 and had three children. In May 2023, after 18 years, she filed. The house was his, bought in 1988, before the marriage.

The prenup paid her $100,000 on the wedding day, $100,000 on the first anniversary, and $1 million after she filed.

He offered about $51,000 a month. A judge set $129,755 for now. She asked for more.

She moved into a $40,000 a month rental and said it wasn’t enough for the kids.

That summer, she was photographed on vacation in Hawaii with a family friend, Josh Connor.

In September 2023, the judge decided: $63,209 a month.

In the video below, Kevin arrives at court: “We’re talking about somebody I love on the other side.” Then listen for what she says is in the kids’ DNA.

She later married Josh Connor.

The case for Christine: 18 years, three kids, and a husband who made over $1 million a month on Yellowstone.
The case for Kevin: she signed the prenup, and their oldest son drives a 15 year old truck.

Was $63,209 a month for three kids fair, or did she ask for too much?

To date, Israel has returned territories larger than its entire present-day territory in exchange for peace.

Moreover, Israel has repeatedly offered the Palestinians a state.

In 2000, President Clinton proposed a Palestinian state encompassing 96% of the West Bank, with territorial swaps to compensate for the remaining percentage. The proposal also included Gaza and East Jerusalem as the Palestinian capital.

Israel's then-prime minister, Ehud Barak, accepted the framework. Yasser Arafat rejected it without presenting a counterproposal, and the Second Intifada followed, during which hundreds of Israelis were murdered.

In the early 1990s, Yitzhak Rabin, and later Ehud Barak around the turn of the millennium, explored offering Syria a withdrawal from the Golan Heights and a return to the June 1967 lines. Assad rejected the proposals.

In 2005, Israel unilaterally withdrew from Gaza, leaving behind desalination facilities, a power station, and greenhouses. Israel also began seeking moderate Palestinian partners in Gaza to establish a free-trade zone at the Karni crossing.

text:
The longest running booth in NFL TV history is cracking in public.

What happened: before ESPN's Bills vs Rams Monday Night Football game on Oct. 12, Troy Aikman and Joe Buck got into an expletive-filled argument in the booth, according to a new report from The Athletic, summarized Friday by the New York Post. Buck reportedly said: "You are not going to f-ing talk to me? I'm not the reason you don't have a contract." Aikman reportedly answered: "I just never thought you'd do it to me." The report says Aikman also got into it with ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro that same night.

The money: Buck signed a six-year extension in September, reported at $108 million and running through the 2032 season. That's close to a 20 percent raise on the 2022 deal that brought both men over from Fox as a package. Aikman's five-year, $90 million deal runs out after this season, and ESPN has not negotiated with him. Per the report, Aikman's camp offered a return at a raise similar to Buck's and ESPN declined.

Both sides: Aikman's camp sees Buck as a "master of manipulating" who kept his own talks secret. Buck's camp says Aikman was "barking orders" for replays and made life hard for production staff. ESPN has sided with Buck and is in cost-cutting mode. Greg Olsen, now at Fox, is widely considered the favorite to replace Aikman.

On air, it still works. Monday's Cowboys win in Philadelphia sounded as smooth as ever, and Aikman got emotional honoring longtime spotter David Moulton.

What we still don't know: whether ESPN changes course, where Aikman lands as a free agent, and whether the pair finishes the season through the Super Bowl ESPN carries in February. They've worked together since 2002.

ZB30 standing by in the booth.

A graphic circulating online accuses Gov. Wes Moore of failing across nine major policy areas, including education, employment, housing, energy, transportation and taxes.

Some claims are overstated. Maryland has recorded reductions in violent crime and fatal overdoses. But the state’s fiscal and economic challenges provide substantial grounds for scrutiny.

▪️ BUDGET CRISIS: Legislative analysts project a $2.57 billion structural deficit in FY2028, growing to $3.43 billion by FY2030.

▪️ JOBS: Maryland lost an estimated 20,100 payroll jobs in August and September combined, even as unemployment declined to 3.9%.

▪️ EDUCATION: Despite improving school ratings, 22.8% of students remain chronically absent, and half of Maryland schools earned three stars or fewer.

▪️ AFFORDABILITY: Maryland ranks fourth nationally for grocery costs, while residents contend with expensive electricity, housing, insurance and taxes.

▪️ TRANSPORTATION: Moore revived Baltimore’s Red Line in 2023, but construction has not begun, funding remains unresolved, and there is no firm opening date.

▪️ ENERGY: The administration’s new $200 million generation program offers no immediate household bill reductions.

Moore can point to genuine progress in public safety. That doesn’t resolve Maryland’s financial problems.

The question isn’t whether every promise has failed. It’s whether the administration is delivering measurable results proportional to its spending commitments.

Where are the balanced budgets, affordable utilities, stronger job numbers and completed infrastructure projects Marylanders were promised?
