AN OPEN LETTER TO KAMALA HARRIS
@KamalaHarris
YOUR PRESIDENTIAL DREAM IS NOT OVER

The Next Stop Is a New Frontier for American Democracy

Dear Vice President Kamala Harris,

As you may have noticed, I often speak about political party bosses—or perhaps I should call them arrogant delegates—who believe they control the bus carrying the hopes and dreams of Americans who want to become president. They tell candidates, “Get on the bus. We will take you to the next stop.” But sometimes they take you only halfway, and at the final stop, they make decisions that leave you with no time to prepare. You have been on that bus long enough to understand how the system works. But I am telling you that your presidential dreams should never be stopped by wealthy candidates, powerful donors, Democratic Party machinery, Republican Party machinery, or any political system that undermines your opportunity to lead. A new frontier is coming, where ordinary Americans, through their blogs, artificial intelligence, and independent participation, can evaluate candidates and offer their own endorsements. Your future should not be decided by the people driving the party bus. It should be decided by the American people.

You must never give up on your dreams, especially because of the young girls and women who look to you as proof that the presidency is within their reach. Hillary Clinton inspired generations of girls to imagine a woman becoming president, but after her defeat, that particular presidential journey came to an end. I do not want you to abandon yours. Do not be a quitter. Your next campaign should not be built around who can raise the most money or purchase the most advertisements. It should be built around the future of American women, young people, and citizens who will participate in politics through AI, independent websites, blogs, and new democratic institutions. Artificial intelligence will play a central role in the next presidential election, and I want you to understand that your opportunity to lead is not over. Your experience, your ambitions, and your willingness to continue participating can help shape a better political history for the generations that follow.

I intend to begin a new endorsement process, and I want you to be among the first to hear about it. But the first endorsement will not be yours. It will go to the Governor of California, and it will come with something unusual: complaints. Because an endorsement should never be a blank check. It should be an opportunity for citizens to examine leadership, identify problems, demand answers, and offer solutions. We may not have as many complaints about you today, but I am certain Americans across the country will have questions, concerns, and ideas they want you to address. That is how a meaningful endorsement should work: citizens participate, leaders listen, and together they build a public record of accountability. So I invite you to continue fighting for your dreams and to participate in creating this New Frontier. Before we endorse our next president, we must begin rebuilding the system that produces our presidential candidates.

The American dream belongs to every American—including the women and girls who are still waiting to see one of their own become president.

Omar Arizona
The Super User Party — A New Frontier for American Democracy

text:
hey bud what do you think you got there? 

This is an unsent State Department draft from May 4, 1948—ten days before Israel declared independence. It argues that Jewish military successes and determination to establish a state could lead to a wider war, and that the United States should seek a negotiated territorial settlement rather than become involved militarily against the Arab states.

The crucial context is in the footnotes and the documents immediately around it.

1. It was a policy argument, not an official finding about who started the war.

The heading identifies it as a draft memorandum from Dean Rusk to Under Secretary Robert Lovett, but the editorial footnote says:
“Drafted by Mr. McClintock; a marginal notation states it was not sent.”

That makes it evidence of thinking within the State Department. It does not establish that Rusk approved it, Lovett received it, or the United States adopted its conclusions. Original document, footnote 1

2. Fighting was already underway, but the main intervention by neighboring Arab armies was still ahead.

The document falls between the November 1947 UN partition resolution and the end of British rule in May 1948. By early May, Jewish forces were gaining the upper hand against Palestinian Arab forces and Arab volunteers.

The military report that this draft explicitly relies upon—Consul General Thomas Wasson’s May 3 telegram—describes collapsing Arab morale, refugees fleeing, and expectations of further Jewish advances. But it also says:
“Jewish operations at beginning were defensive against Arab attacks.”

It describes the subsequent shift to offensive operations intended to improve defensive positions and communications. The draft’s own supporting report therefore does not describe the conflict as Jewish aggression from its beginning. Wasson’s report

3. The accusation that the Jewish Agency rejected peace needs qualification.

The immediate trigger was rejection of a particular American diplomatic proposal. That proposal included a ten-day ceasefire, an extension of the British Mandate, and flying representatives to Palestine for negotiations. American proposal

In the immediately preceding document, Jewish Agency representative Moshe Shertok explains his position: he rejects extending the Mandate and accepting responsibility for the American proposals, but explicitly offers an immediate ceasefire if the Arabs also agree, using the existing UN truce machinery.

That does not prove that Jewish leaders had no military ambitions. It does mean rejecting this negotiating package cannot simply be equated with rejecting any ceasefire. Shertok’s response

4. “The Jews will be the actual aggressors” is a prediction about the next phase.

The preceding words matter:
“If these predictions come true…”

The draft anticipates Jewish attacks on Arab communities, followed by intervention from neighboring Arab states, followed by Jewish appeals for UN protection. Its author argues that American military action against those Arab states would then be unjustified and strategically disastrous.

That is a forceful contemporary interpretation of an anticipated sequence—not a retrospective investigation establishing responsibility for everything that happened in 1947–1948. Original document

5. Its practical objective was a different partition settlement.

The draft proposes a deal with King Abdullah of Transjordan: a Jewish coastal state from Tel Aviv to Haifa, with other territory allocated through arrangements involving Abdullah, Saudi Arabia, and Syria. Its overriding concerns include American relations with Arab governments and the danger of American or Soviet military involvement.

There was disagreement even within the State Department: two days earlier, Loy Henderson had argued that an invasion by Arab armies, before or after May 15, would be difficult to regard as anything other than a violation of UN Charter principles. Henderson memorandum

The document is genuine evidence that some American officials sharply criticized Jewish military policy and anticipated Arab intervention as a response. Calling it an official American determination that “Israel started the 1948 war,” however, would misrepresent its status, timing, and surrounding evidence.

text:
On May 4, 1944, Mildred “Micky” Axton was sitting in the rear of a B-29 Superfortress when the chief test pilot’s voice came over the intercom. He asked if she would like to fly the aircraft. Micky put on her parachute, crawled through a narrow passage and made her way to the cockpit. The pilot gave her the left seat and she took control of one of America’s most powerful bombers. In that moment she became the first woman to fly a B-29. The aircraft was so secret that Micky later said she could tell only her husband about the experience.

Her love of flying began in Coffeyville, Kansas. She earned her pilot’s license in 1940 and became the only woman in her civilian pilot training class. In 1943 she joined the Women Airforce Service Pilots. She left her infant daughter in her mother’s care and traveled to Sweetwater, Texas, for training.

After completing her training Micky was assigned to Pecos Army Air Field where she tested repaired aircraft before they returned to service. Eventually her mother became ill and Micky had to leave the WASPs to care for her daughter. She returned to Kansas and found work with Boeing’s flight-test operation in Wichita. That job brought her aboard the B-29 nicknamed “Sweet Sixteen.” When the chief test pilot offered her the chance to fly it she later recalled being “absolutely in hog heaven.”

The chief pilot wrote a letter confirming her historic flight. During the war the WASPs were not granted military veteran status. They finally received that recognition in 1977. Micky lived long enough to see the women’s service formally recognized. She died in 2010 at the age of 91. In her honor a restored training aircraft was named “Miss Micky.

text:
DISGRACE: Almost £10 billion of Britain’s £14.9 billion bill for pandemic protective equipment was wasted while frontline staff went without adequate protection.

On 14 July 2026, the UK Covid-19 Inquiry set out how failures in government buying and distribution left health and care workers poorly protected during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Personal protective equipment, or PPE, includes the masks, gloves and other kit used to protect staff and patients from infection.

The government’s job involved more than finding somebody willing to sell it.

Officials needed to know what workers required, check what suppliers could deliver and get the right equipment to the people who needed it.

The UK entered the emergency without a properly prepared system for doing that.

Its emergency stockpile held too little vital equipment, alongside large quantities that had expired.

Plans for rapidly expanding buying and distribution had not been properly tested.

Ministers and officials then had to build emergency systems within days, just as countries around the world were competing for the same supplies.

Demand shot up, prices rose and supply chains came under enormous pressure.

That left decision-makers choosing between risking public money on urgent purchases and slowing down while other countries secured the available equipment.

Baroness Heather Hallett, who chairs the inquiry, concluded that buying at risk was the right decision in those circumstances.

Waiting would have exposed frontline workers and the public to unacceptable danger.

The failure started before that choice: better preparation would have made it less desperate.

Nor did securing a purchase mean the government had solved the problem.

Buying and distribution were not sufficiently joined up, and the technology behind them was outdated.

Officials struggled to establish what was needed, what suppliers were providing and what was being transported.

Without that connected picture, spending money and getting useful protection to a worker became two separate problems.

Then there was the government’s High Priority Lane, better known as the VIP lane.

Officials established it under pressure from ministers to manage offers of help.

It gave some suppliers favourable treatment because of their connections to government.

Hallett found that this built unfairness into a system handling billions of pounds of public money.

The inquiry did not identify cronyism or corruption by ministers or officials in the final decisions to award contracts.

Hallett concluded that the lane should never have been established and must not be repeated.

The inquiry also identified practical strengths that the emergency plans had failed to organise in advance.

Manufacturers changed their production to make equipment, businesses used overseas contacts to secure supplies and the Army brought experience in moving them.

Those efforts helped obtain equipment at the speed and scale the crisis demanded.

But the UK’s overseas supplier base was too concentrated in China, while the potential of domestic manufacturers had not been adequately considered before the emergency.

The recommendations therefore reach beyond choosing different suppliers.

They include better-managed stockpiles, trained buying staff, stronger domestic manufacturing and more varied overseas supply routes.

Hallett also called for buying and distribution systems to be digitalised within three years, so officials could share information as supplies were ordered and moved.

The missing capability was basic: knowing what protection workers needed, what the government had bought and whether it was reaching them.

text:
Stoked to say that I am wrapping up the editing on Chapter 9 of 10 of my 7th book, Chasing Dexterity in American Football (to be released in early 2027)! 

Like snowflakes in the Minnesota winter, no two movement problems in football are ever the same, and no two movement solutions will be the same either.

Well, Chapter 9 of Chasing Dexterity in American Football takes that idea to the film. Across 20 of the game’s most skillful movers, from Gale Sayers and Jim Brown to Jerry Rice, Lawrence Taylor, Ed Reed, Lamar Jackson, and Myles Garrett, we look at what these players do in situ, within and across the solving of the most challenging problems found on the field.

For each one, I break down plays from different situations and conditions to show the movement problem-solving process (MPSP) at work: the what is of the problem, the information it offers and the affordances that information specifies, and how perception, cognition, and action flow into each other as one integrated movement solution that becomes functionally fit to the peculiar problem at hand.

How do they functionally become one with the problems they face? What does it look like to be attuned, intentional, adaptable, and authentic, again and again, across situations and conditions?

That is what chasing dexterity looks like!

Next up in Chapter 10: none other than a FULL chapter on the movement skill of Barry Sanders.

text:
Peter Obi will crash dollar to N500, slash bread to N800, rice to N27,500 if elected — Pat Utomi vows

Political economist Pat Utomi has said the presidential campaign of Peter Obi and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is proposing to strengthen the naira to N500 against the dollar if elected in 2027. 

Utomi disclosed this in a post on X, explaining that the exchange-rate target forms part of the party’s economic blueprint aimed at tackling inflation, reducing poverty and restoring Nigerians’ purchasing power. 

According to him, the proposed naira appreciation would be supported by investments in security, electricity and road infrastructure, as well as structural reforms designed to make the economy more competitive. 

He projected that the plan could trigger significant reductions in the prices of essential commodities. 

Under the proposed programme, a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for about N1,750 could fall to N800, while a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500. 

A medium-sized yam, he said, could reduce from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could decline from N75,000 to N37,500. Plantain could fall from N2,500 to N1,250, while a whole chicken could drop from N7,000 to N3,500. 

Utomi also projected that a dozen eggs could sell for N1,150 instead of N2,300, while a painter of garri could drop from N1,300 to N650. He added that petrol and cement would also become cheaper. 

“We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he said. 

“It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.” 

Utomi added that the proposal represents the party’s “concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty.” 

However, he did not state when the N500/$ target would be achieved or provide details of the monetary and fiscal measures required to sustain such an appreciation.

It’s a civil war Russian alligator Ukraine log

US leaders had a clear shot after 1991 to lock in a stable Europe that included Russia as a legitimate power. They chose permanent primacy instead. The failure was arrogance, broken verbal assurances, and refusal to treat a nuclear state that had just dismantled its empire as a peer rather than a defeated supplicant.

The Ukraine war is the direct, predictable bill for that choice.
T
he core failure was treating the end of the Cold War as total victory rather than an opportunity for a negotiated order.

In February 1990, Secretary of State James Baker told Gorbachev that if a unified Germany stayed in NATO there would be “no extension of NATO’s jurisdiction for forces of NATO one inch to the east.” Soviet transcripts show Baker agreeing that a broadening of the NATO zone was unacceptable. Similar language came from Helmut Kohl, Hans-Dietrich Genscher, and others. These were not idle remarks; declassified records from the National Security Archive document a cascade of assurances across Western leaders during German reunification talks. No broad formal treaty locked the entire future expansion, and the formal two-plus-four agreement was limited to Germany. The US and NATO later treated the verbal record as non-binding once Russia was weak. That is the factual record of what was said and what was not written down.

George Kennan, the architect of containment, called NATO expansion in 1997 “the most fateful error of American policy in the entire post-Cold War era.” He predicted it would inflame Russian nationalism, undermine democracy in Russia, restore Cold War conditions, and push Moscow toward hostile policies. He was correct. Clinton proceeded with the 1999 round (Poland, Hungary, Czech Republic); later rounds added the Baltics and others. The 2008 Bucharest summit explicitly promised Ukraine and Georgia eventual membership. Russia’s red lines on a buffer and its near abroad were treated as irrelevant. Shock therapy under Yeltsin produced economic collapse and oligarch looting while Western advisers cheered; the subsequent recovery under Putin coincided with the completed expansion. Partnership for Peace was offered as a half-measure and then.

Common ground was available: a European security system that treated Russia as a stakeholder rather than a permanent outsider, neutrality or non-alignment for Ukraine as a buffer, economic integration without military encirclement, and genuine demilitarization of the post-Soviet space. US leaders (Bush Sr. through Clinton and successors) rejected that path for unipolar primacy. The verbal assurances of 1990 were convenient while Soviet forces were withdrawing and inconvenient once the Warsaw Pact was gone. The result is not “Russian aggression out of nowhere”; it is the predictable reaction of a great power whose core security interests were overridden after it had already conceded the empire. The Cold War’s trillions and millions of veterans bought a chance. Post-1991 policy spent it on expansion that Kennan and others warned would restart the contest. That is the point-blank failure.  https://t.co/mVdZBOXEuo

text:
THE ENEMY DOESN'T ATTACK WHAT IT DOESN'T FEAR. 🙏🤍🔥

Remember this.

To every soul who has spent a lifetime suffering yet continues to choose kindness.

To those who have been struck down time and time again, face spiritual warfare, yet somehow find the strength to rise.

To those who have endured betrayal, heartbreak, loss and suffering, yet refuse to allow the cruelty of this world to corrupt the goodness within their hearts.

To those who feel they are constantly fighting battles against their health, their minds, their emotions and their peace.

I want you to consider something.

The very thing you perceive as your greatest burden is also a testament to the strength of the spirit you carry?

There is a reason the enemy seeks to extinguish the light.

THIEVES DON'T BREAK INTO EMPTY HOUSES.

DOGS DON'T BARK AT PARKED CARS.

The enemy doesn't waste its energy fighting what it does not perceive as a threat.

You see, darkness has no need to challenge darkness.

It is the light that exposes what darkness desperately seeks to conceal.

And I believe there are many souls walking this earth who carry something far more valuable than anything this material world could ever offer.

A heart that refuses to hate.
A spirit that refuses to surrender.
A love that suffering has never managed to destroy.

You have been tested in ways others may never comprehend.

You have walked through fires that were meant to consume you, yet somehow you emerged still possessing the capacity to love.

That is not weakness.

THAT IS SPIRITUAL STRENGTH.

I believe the greatest victory over darkness is refusing to become a reflection of it.

So the next time life brings you to your knees, remember that even there, you can rise.

Not because you are untouchable.
Not because you will never suffer again.

But because your spirit is worth more than the suffering you have endured.

THE DEVIL DOESN'T NEED TO DESTROY THOSE WHO HAVE ALREADY SURRENDERED THEIR LIGHT.

And you, my friends, are still shining.

THE DARKNESS HAS FOUGHT YOU YOUR ENTIRE LIFE, YET HERE YOU ARE, STILL CARRYING THE VERY LIGHT IT COULD NEVER EXTINGUISH.

Walk in faith. Walk in love.

AND NEVER FORGET WHO WALKS BESIDE YOU.

God. 🙏🤍🔥

text:
If Zelensky Is So Corrupt, Why Can’t Anyone Buy Him? 🇺🇦

I just realized something almost hilarious if it wasn’t very obvious and also real about the whole anti-Zelensky narrative.

For years we have been told that Zelensky is corrupt, illegitimate, a puppet, a billionaire thief, some CIA creation, whatever version happens to be useful that day. And yet somehow Putin, Trump, oligarchs, billionaires and the entire anti-Ukraine political machine still cannot control him.

Think about that contradiction.

Zelensky was elected in 2019 with about 73% of the runoff vote. Ukraine has not held another presidential election because elections are suspended under martial law during Russia’s invasion, something Zelensky has said could change if conditions allow a safe and legal vote. Meanwhile Trump, Elon and others are now openly calling for Ukraine to replace him after Zelensky refused demands to stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure and bend over to them. 

And this is where their own propaganda stops making sense. If Zelensky were really as spectacularly corrupt as they claim, why wouldn’t somebody have bought him years ago?

Putin has all the money. Russian oligarchs have money. Western billionaires have money. Elon has more money than all of them. Trump has political power. There are people with enormous financial and geopolitical interests who would benefit from a Ukrainian president willing to make the right deal for them.

If Zelensky were really nothing but a corrupt opportunist, the easiest path imaginable would have been to take the money, make peace with Putin on Putin’s terms, protect himself, become insanely wealthy, powerful and live comfortably ruling the Ukraine and the area as a probably richest dictator on earth. 

Instead, Russia invaded, Zelensky stayed, Ukraine kept fighting, and years later these people are still trying to pressure him, discredit him, replace him and convince everyone that he is somehow the problem.

Trump and Elon has now publicly called for Ukraine to get a new president after Zelensky resisted pressure over Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. Their relationship has deteriorated sharply precisely because Zelensky has continued pursuing policies Washington told him to stop. 

So maybe the reason so many powerful men seem absolutely fucking obsessed with Zelensky is much simpler than all the conspiracy theories.

Maybe they hate him because they cannot break him.

Maybe they hate him because they cannot buy him.

Maybe they are simply jealous of him and his amazing courage and integrity.?

And maybe nothing drives men obsessed with power more insane than another man they cannot control.

text:
Elizabeth Ann Hanks is a writer and journalist who shares her life story in her memoir, The 10: A Memoir of Family and the Open Road...

She is the only daughter of actor Tom Hanks and his first wife, Susan Dillingham (actor Samantha Lewes), and the sister of actor Colin Hanks. Her parents divorced in 1987. She and her brother primarily lived with their mother in Sacramento, California. Her mother suffered from severe mental illness, paranoia, and addiction. Ann Hanks described growing up amid emotional instability, physical abuse, neglect and domestic deprivation. 

. . . 

While her father’s career was skyrocketing, her daily life was filled with profound uncertainty, struggles, and a frequently empty refrigerator.

Every time Tom Hanks appeared on screen or held up an Oscar statue, millions of fans smiled and cheered.

The world saw him as America's ultimate nice guy, a reliable father figure on film and a beloved global superstar.

But back home in Sacramento during the early nineteen-eighties, his daughter Elizabeth Ann Hanks was living in a completely different reality.

Elizabeth was born in 1982 to Tom Hanks and his first wife, actress Susan Dillingham, whose professional name was Samantha Lewes.

As Tom transitioned from a working television actor into a massive box-office icon, the original family home began to fracture under the heavy weight of untreated mental illness.

Her mother struggled deeply with emotional instability, leaving Elizabeth and her older brother Colin feeling isolated, neglected, and unsafe in their own house.

The contrast between her father's multi-millionaire status and her chaotic domestic routine was deeply confusing for a young child.

In one world, her dad was greeted by cheering crowds and glittering spotlights.

In her daily world, she was just a little girl trying to navigate a turbulent household where basic stability felt entirely out of reach.

The tension eventually escalated to a breaking point, culminating in a frightening physical altercation with her mother that forced Elizabeth to pack her bags and flee in the middle of the night.

Seeking safety and permanence, she moved to Los Angeles to live with her father and her stepmother, Rita Wilson.

Stepping into the bustling Hanks household brought a dramatic shift in custody and a brand-new family dynamic alongside her younger half-brothers, Chet and Truman.

Adjusting wasn't simple, especially as she balanced her quiet nature with her brother Chet’s turbulent adolescent years and very public rebellious phases.

Yet, that move provided the grounding safety she needed to grow and heal.

Instead of leveraging her famous last name to launch an acting career in Hollywood, Elizabeth chose a quieter, more grounded path.

She dedicated herself to her passion for reading and writing, building an independent identity as a respected journalist and author based entirely on her own intellect and hard work.

When she eventually decided to share portions of her family story, she did not do it to generate cheap tabloid gossip.

"I didn't write this to tear anyone down or settle old scores," Elizabeth once reflected when discussing her journey with writing and healing.

"I wrote it because surviving the chaos of your childhood demands that you eventually look the truth straight in the eye."

Her journey also highlighted the vital role played by Rita Wilson, whom Elizabeth has frequently praised as a steady second mother who offered a true safe haven during her darkest moments.

Even Tom Hanks has openly acknowledged that no family is entirely flawless and that every household carries its own hidden scars.

The world spent decades falling in love with Tom Hanks, crowning him as ultimate gold standard of American fatherhood. But behind that warm, carefully crafted image lay a cold truth that no award could cover up.

YOUR STOCKS CAN DO MORE THAN JUST SIT IN YOUR PORTFOLIO. 

For most people investing in U.S. stocks, the usual approach is to buy shares of companies they believe in, hold them for several years, and eventually sell when the price reaches a level where they are comfortable taking profits.

There's nothing wrong with that approach, and I still think long-term investing makes sense for people who prefer building their portfolios rather than constantly trading every market movement.

But I have also been looking into how investors can make additional use of the assets they already own without necessarily selling their existing positions.

Traditional brokers like @IBKR, @RobinhoodApp, and @moomoo already offer investment services, including margin accounts and borrowing against eligible securities, so using stocks as collateral isn't exactly new.

However, those services generally operate within their respective brokerage environments, and managing investments across traditional stocks, crypto, and other markets can still require investors to maintain several accounts.

That is where @Bitget's rToken ecosystem offers a different setup, particularly for people who already trade crypto while maintaining long-term exposure to U.S. stocks and ETFs.

I have discussed rTokens several times in my previous posts, especially the stock transfer service, but I want to highlight three features that show how eligible tokenized holdings can be used beyond simply waiting for their prices to appreciate.

1️⃣ EARN ADDITIONAL RETURNS THROUGH STOCK DUAL INVESTMENT

Bitget supports Stock Dual Investment for selected rTokens, letting users choose between Buy Low and Sell High strategies based on how they plan to manage their positions.

For example, suppose I have been following $NVDA for a while and would want to accumulate at a lower price instead of buying immediately.

I could explore a Buy Low product, subscribe using USDT, and choose an available target price and settlement date. Under the product's conditions, I would receive the applicable interest, and if the settlement price triggers conversion, the USDT would be exchanged for the corresponding rToken at the agreed target.

For someone who already holds an eligible tokenized stock and has a price where they would be comfortable taking profits, Sell High offers another approach, as they can subscribe using their rTokens while earning interest under the selected terms.

I mentioned this in my previous content, but it is important to understand that Dual Investment is not the same as receiving guaranteed passive income just because you hold a stock.

So while the additional interest might be attractive, I would still consider whether I am comfortable with the target price and possible conversion before subscribing.

You can explore the available Stock Dual Investment products here: https://t.co/mQ4wrxO3tB

2️⃣ USE ELIGIBLE rTOKENS AS FUTURES MARGIN

Another feature lets you use selected rTokens as margin through Bitget's Unified Trading Account (UTA).

Instead of selling a tokenized stock position to free up USDT for another trade, eligible holdings can contribute collateral value toward supported futures or margin positions.

For someone who follows several markets at once, this could provide more flexibility when managing capital because the original stock-linked exposure can remain in the account while its eligible collateral value contributes toward another position.

However, Bitget does not necessarily count every rToken at its full market value. The platform applies collateral ratios, meaning only a portion of an eligible asset's value may count toward available margin.

Using an existing holding as margin adds another layer of risk because a sharp decline in the collateral asset, combined with losses on the leveraged trade, could quickly reduce the account's available margin.

That is something I would be particularly cautious about during earnings announcements or periods of high market volatility, when even stocks with strong fundamentals can experience significant price movements.

3️⃣ BORROW AGAINST YOUR STOCK HOLDINGS WITHOUT SELLING THEM

You can also use supported rTokens as collateral for crypto loans, allowing eligible users to borrow assets such as USDT while maintaining their original tokenized stock exposure.

This may be useful for investors who need additional liquidity but would rather avoid selling an investment they intend to hold long term.

The amount that can be borrowed depends on the asset's collateral requirements, loan-to-value ratio, and the platform's current borrowing limits.

It is also worth remembering that borrowing against stocks does not eliminate the risks of selling or trading; it just adds other considerations, including interest payments and the possibility of liquidation if the collateral value falls too far.

Personally, I would be careful about borrowing against an asset just to increase market exposure because the added flexibility can also amplify losses when several positions move against you.

WHAT ABOUT STOCKS STILL HELD THROUGH TRADITIONAL BROKERS?

For investors already using platforms like Robinhood, Moomoo, or Interactive Brokers, Bitget's stock transfer service lets you move eligible U.S. stock and ETF holdings into its rToken ecosystem.

I have covered the transfer process in previous posts, but it connects to this discussion because supported holdings can be used with Bitget's additional trading, lending, and Earn products once transferred and converted into rTokens.

There is also an ongoing transfer campaign offering 200 USDT worth of rSPCX for a first eligible stock transfer of at least $5,000, with higher reward tiers available for larger amounts.

You can check which stocks qualify, how the transfer process works, and the complete reward conditions here: https://t.co/EY3GMxq5aV

For someone who already manages both stocks and crypto, it's appealing to have more options for using eligible assets within the same trading ecosystem.

At the end of the day, buying and holding stocks is still a perfectly reasonable strategy, and I do not think every long-term investor needs to use margin, take out a loan, or subscribe to structured products just to make their portfolio more productive.

Sometimes holding an asset without doing anything else is already the right decision.

What matters is understanding which additional features actually fit your investment goals, rather than feeling pressured to use every available product simply because it promises greater capital efficiency.

text:
Little Office of the Blessed Virgin Mary

FRIDAY

Morning Prayer
God, come to my assistance.
- Lord, make haste to help me

Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit
as it was in the beginning, is now, and will be forever.  Amen.

Virgin of virgins,
I choose you today
as my sovereign, my queen, my empress,
and I declare myself, as I am in fact,
your servant and your slave.
I invoke your royal name of Mary,
that is, sovereign Lady,
and beg of you with all my heart
to admit me into the privileged circle¡
of your family
as one of your servants,
to do your will
as a humble slave and a loving child.
As a sign of your acceptance
engrave on my heart
with the fire of your love,
not the brand of an unwilling slave,
but those two gracious words of the angel:
Ave Maria.
As long as I draw breath
may your burning love ensure
that I bear these words
in my heart and in my memory,
and that until my dying breath
my will may be always on fire
with my great desire to serve you,
my sovereign and my queen,
glorious in your majesty.
Though I am in every way unworthy
of so honorable a title,
I resolve sincerely to be your slave,
to serve you wholeheartedly,
to protect your name,
and that of your Son,
against every insult,
as far as it may rest with me,
and never to allow anyone in my charge
to offend your Son in any way.
By your tender love for your Son,
by the glories you have received
from the Most Holy Trinity,
do not reject me from your service
but as my sovereign and my queen
preside over all my actions,
command whatever you will,
direct all my work,
remedy all its defects.
During my whole life
rule over me
as your servant and slave.
At the hour of my death,
as I hope for
at the end of my loving servitude
among the privileged members of your family,
receive my soul and escort it
into the presence of God.

St Bartolome de Los Rios(1580-1652)

PSALMODY

Ant.1 My soul clings to you, Lord Jesus Christ.

Psalm 51
O God, have mercy on me
Your inmost being must be renewed, and you must put on the new man. (Eph 4:23-24)
Have mercy on me, God, in your kindness.
In your compassion blot out my offense.
O wash me more and more from my guilt
and cleanse me from my sin.
My offenses truly I know them;
my sin is always before me
Against you, you alone, have I sinned;
what is evil in your sight I have done.
That you may be justified when you give sentence
and be without reproach when you judge,
O see, in guilt I was born,
a sinner was I conceived.
Indeed you love truth in the heart;
then in the secret of my heart teach me wisdom.
O purify me, then I shall be clean;
O wash me, I shall be whiter than snow.
Make me hear rejoicing and gladness,
that the bones you have crushed may thrill.
From my sins turn away your face
and blot out all my guilt.
A pure heart create for me, O God,
put a steadfast spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from your presence,
nor deprive me of your holy spirit.
Give me again the joy of your help;
with a spirit of fervor sustain me,
that I may teach transgressors your ways
and sinners may return to you.
O rescue me, God, my helper,
and my tongue shall ring out your goodness.
O Lord, open my lips
and my mouth shall declare your praise.
For in sacrifice you take no delight,
burnt offering from me you would refuse,
my sacrifice, a contrite spirit,
a humbled, contrite heart you will not spurn.
In your goodness, show favor to Zion:
rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will be pleased with lawful sacrifice,
(burnt offerings wholly consumed),
then you will be offered young bulls on your altar.

Exxon earned more from making fuel than from producing oil, while its oil and gas output kept falling. A global shortage of diesel took its refining margin marker to a record $50 a barrel, and profit per share excluding one-offs reached $4.23, more than double a year ago. Chief executive Darren Woods said the shortage will last well through next year.

• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟰.𝟮𝟯 ($3.52 last quarter; about $1.84 a year ago by our math)
• Refining profit, excluding one-offs: $𝟵.𝟭 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 ($4.1 billion last quarter)
• Oil and gas production: 𝟰.𝟱𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝘆 (−5.7% from a year ago)
• 2027 share buybacks: $𝟮𝟬 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 (new; same pace as 2026)

⚖️ 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the windfall is lasting longer than one quarter and Exxon put it into debt repayment and next year's buyback; net debt is 7.5% of capital, from 13% in March. One caution: prices and margins explain all of this year's profit growth, so the case still rests on a shortage that ends when Middle East and Russian refineries return.

The question now is how much refining profit survives a reopened Strait of Hormuz. Either lost Middle East, Russian and Chinese supply keeps markets short into 2027, or the $50 marker falls back within a quarter. The marker in the January report will tell.

🐂 𝗕𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗖𝗮𝘀𝗲

🟢🟢 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗗𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿
Energy Products, the segment that turns crude into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, has become Exxon's biggest earner. Refineries in Russia and the Middle East stayed shut, with "roughly 10 percent of global capacity offline", so the company's own refining margin marker reached a record $50.3 a barrel.

Exxon's refineries answered by running flat out. Its US Gulf Coast crude units ran at 100%, and the group posted its second-highest Gulf Coast diesel volume on record. The segment earned $9.1 billion excluding one-offs, up from $4.1 billion last quarter.

• Refining margin marker: $50.3 a barrel, from $29.0 last quarter and $17.5 a year ago
• Profit per barrel processed: about $26, against about $4 for all of 2025
• Capture: by our math each extra dollar of margin added $233 million in the quarter, above the $200 million the company's own sensitivity implies
• Traded volumes: about four times the 2019 level, Exxon says

This matters because the quarter tests a claim Exxon has made for years: that $17 billion of refining investment since 2019 and $3 billion of structural savings built a business that earns more at any margin. The capture rate says yes. Production and manufacturing expenses fell to 9.9% of revenue from 11.8% a year ago. The reason was higher revenue, not lower spending, because that expense line itself rose 11%.

What to watch: the refining margin marker in the fourth-quarter report, against $50.3 now. A reading that stays above $30 while the Strait of Hormuz remains shut would show that the shortage, not one quarter's trading, sets the margin.

🟢🟢 𝗡𝗲𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝗯𝘁 𝗙𝗲𝗹𝗹 $𝟵.𝟳 𝗕𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀
Exxon pays a dividend it has raised for 44 straight years and buys back about $20 billion of stock a year, and it keeps both going when prices fall. Chief executive Darren Woods told analysts "we're not going to ever cut our dividends", so the balance sheet has to carry that pledge through the bottom of the cycle.

This quarter the cash arrived: free cash flow reached $19.1 billion, twice the $9.4 billion paid out in dividends and buybacks. The rest went to debt. Net debt fell by $9.7 billion in the quarter by our math. It now equals 7.5% of capital, down from 11% in June, which the company calls the lowest ratio among the large oil majors.

• Net debt: $22.1 billion, from $31.8 billion in June and $32.9 billion at year end
• Shareholder returns: $28.0 billion so far this year, $15.1 billion of it buybacks
• Dividend: raised 4% to $1.07 a share
• 2027 buybacks: $20 billion, the same pace as this year

The 2027 buyback decision matters more than the debt paydown, because Exxon set it before knowing where refining margins settle, and it warned that purchases may not fall evenly across the four quarters. So the balance sheet, not the margin, now stands behind the promise.

What to watch: the 2027 planning metrics Exxon promised in a press release before year end, in particular where cash capital spending lands inside the $28–32 billion range. A figure at the top, alongside $20 billion of buybacks, would mean the balance sheet rather than the shortage is funding both.

🟢 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗛𝗼𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝟭.𝟴 𝗠𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗕𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝘀
The Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico is Exxon's largest growth asset, and the company plans to lift it from about 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels a day this year to 2.5 million by 2030. Production "remained just above 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels per day" in the quarter, so Exxon has met this year's target.

Woods told analysts that Exxon alone runs automated drilling rigs in the Permian and will expand them to about half of its fleet by 2028. Finance chief Neil Hansen said synergies from the Pioneer acquisition have doubled to $4 billion a year.

This matters because the 2030 plan needs the basin to grow about 9% a year, and Woods says the volume target is not the point: the test is whether new technology lifts recovery per well. He conceded the benefit "just takes time for that to manifest itself in the portfolio" in a field this size.

What to watch: the 2027 Permian figure in the planning press release due before year end. The 2030 path needs about 1.96 million barrels a day next year by our math, so a lower number would mean the rigs are cutting cost rather than adding barrels.

🐻 𝗕𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗖𝗮𝘀𝗲

🔴🔴 𝗢𝘂𝘁𝗽𝘂𝘁 𝗙𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘀 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝗦𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗦𝗮𝘆𝘀 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵
Exxon produced 4.50 million oil-equivalent barrels a day, 5.7% less than a year ago and the lowest figure in seven quarters. The decline came from three places: the Middle East, where war keeps about 350,000 barrels a day offline; Guyana, where the contract now gives the group a smaller share of each barrel; and asset sales.

Guyana is the part Exxon warned about. Once partners recovered their $55 billion of investment, the share of output that repays costs fell, and management flagged a step of about 100,000 barrels a day this quarter. It arrived: entitlement effects took 87,000 barrels a day off from the previous quarter, which the company labels "Lower advantaged volumes with accelerated Guyana entitlement impacts".

Woods says that, excluding the Middle East, production rose from a year ago, and the fifth Guyana development, Uaru, starts in the fourth quarter. But Exxon's own slide still shows a full-year plan of about 4.9 million barrels a day, against 4.53 million so far this year. By our math the fourth quarter would need 6.0 million to get there, and the group has not given a figure adjusted for the disruption.

What to watch: the 2026 production figure in the planning press release Exxon promised before year end, and whether it replaces 4.9 million with a disruption-adjusted number. A figure near 4.5 million would mean this year's growth story runs on Permian and Guyana cash, not on barrels.

🔴🔴 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗔𝗹𝗹 𝗼𝗳 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗬𝗲𝗮𝗿'𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵
"These are lasting improvements, not simply the result of favorable prices and margins," Woods said of the results. Exxon's own earnings bridge tests the claim. Through nine months, profit excluding one-offs rose $18.5 billion from a year ago, and higher prices and margins added $22.7 billion.

• Prices and margins: +$22.7 billion year to date, 123% of the profit increase by our math
• New projects in the Permian, Guyana, Golden Pass, Singapore and the UK: +$2.7 billion
• Structural cost savings: +$1.4 billion year to date, and zero in the quarter against the previous one
• Higher expenses, lower base volumes and Middle East losses: −$7.4 billion combined

So the lasting part is real but small, and this quarter it shrank: against the second quarter, prices and margins added $3.6 billion while volumes from new projects took away $640 million, because Guyana's entitlement fell. The company's own sensitivity shows the exposure the other way. Each dollar off the refining margin marker costs about $200 million a quarter. A return to last December's $18 marker would therefore remove about $6.4 billion a quarter by our math.

That is not a forecast, because Woods expects the shortage to run "well through next year". But one timing item already moved against Exxon: mark-to-market effects on unsettled trades swung from a $2.5 billion gain last quarter to a $2.5 billion loss, the unwind Exxon itself flagged in July.

What to watch: the price and margin line of the earnings bridge in the fourth-quarter report, due in late January. The first quarter in which that line turns negative will show how much profit the investments and cost savings can hold on their own.

🔴 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁 𝗙𝗲𝗹𝗹 𝟰𝟬% 𝗮𝘀 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻𝘀 𝗦𝗹𝗶𝗱
Chemical Products, which makes polyethylene and other plastics, earned $725 million excluding one-offs, down from $1.2 billion last quarter. The company blamed margins that "declined on higher regional product availability and higher feed costs in Europe and Asia Pacific", meaning more supply came back while Exxon's European and Asian plants paid more for raw material.

The North American polyethylene marker fell 31% from last quarter, to $998 a ton. Volumes helped a little, because sales rose on Asian seasonal demand, but they remain 11% below a year ago. This matters because unit profit, about $148 a ton this quarter, sits below the $210 Exxon reports for 2025, so the second-quarter rebound was a price spike inside the same oversupply.

What to watch: the North American polyethylene marker in the fourth-quarter report, now $998 a ton. A second quarterly decline would put chemical earnings back near the level of early 2026, when the segment earned $110 million.

🔴 𝗥𝗶𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗗𝗶𝗱𝗻'𝘁 𝗔𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿
Six standing concerns got no new numbers in the release, the slides or the call, so each one carries over unchanged into the next quarter.

• Second-quarter reserve additions: Exxon has still not itemised the $1.4 billion booked in June, which includes the Louisiana coastal settlement.
• Qatar LNG repairs: Woods said he does "not have much of an update"; the terms of Exxon's share of the rebuild stay unknown.
• European windfall taxes: nobody raised them; the EU methane rule delay helps, but a levy on refining profits remains possible.
• Guyana: the force-majeure acreage awaiting the ICJ ruling and the 2027 licence expiry went unmentioned.
• Papua LNG: Exxon took operatorship and a 34% stake but gave no investment-decision date; Rovuma is still due "as we get through the back end of this year".
• New ventures: carbon capture gained Nucor and the Rose approval; hydrogen, lithium and data centres went unmentioned, and Kazakhstan and Venezuela remain talks without terms.

👓 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗲𝘀

𝗪𝗼𝗼𝗱𝘀 𝗦𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝘂𝗲𝗹 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗟𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳
Asked when refining margins return to normal, Woods named three variables: Middle East exports, "a third of the shortage out there, roughly"; Russia, where "roughly about half of Russia's refining capacity's been taken offline"; and spare Chinese capacity. His guess is that "it will take certainly well through next year before we see things getting back closer to normal". Separately, the European Parliament delayed the EU methane rule by three years, removing a threat to Exxon's European imports.

💲 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗞𝗣𝗜𝘀

𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆 𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀 (𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀, 𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): $𝟲𝟲.𝟱 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇗ accelerating
Rising faster than sales: up 47% from a year ago, against quarterly sales up 33%. Receivables are bills customers have not yet paid, and higher fuel prices lift them. Payables rose too, so working capital released $2.2 billion of cash in the quarter rather than absorbing it.

𝗗𝗶𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 (𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): 𝟰,𝟭𝟰𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇘ decelerating
Falling, but more slowly: down 3.4% from a year ago, after 4.0% a year earlier. The annual $20 billion of buybacks now retires a smaller share of the company each year, so the per-share lift from repurchases is shrinking even as the dollar amount holds.

𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝗽𝘂𝘁 (𝟮𝟲𝗤𝟯): 𝟯.𝟳 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝘆  ⇄ reversing
Turned up after two quarters of decline: 3,735 thousand barrels a day, up 4.9% from last quarter as Asia Pacific units came back, but 9.0% below the record a year ago. Europe ran 754 thousand barrels a day, down 29% from a year ago, which caps how much of the margin Exxon can capture.

🔮 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲

𝗤𝟰 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲𝘀: $𝟱𝟬𝟬–𝟳𝟬𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇘ decelerating
New. Exxon expects the corporate cost line, mainly interest and head-office expense, to fall to between $500 million and $700 million. The middle of that range sits about a third below this quarter's $864 million, consistent with the lower debt. This quarter landed inside its range after two quarters above it on a reported basis.

𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗰𝗮𝘀𝗵 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲: $𝟮𝟳–𝟮𝟵 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from $27–29 billion
Unchanged. Spending so far this year is $20.0 billion. By our math that leaves a range of $7.0–9.0 billion for the fourth quarter, so the pace would at least match this quarter. Last year the December quarter was the heaviest. From 2027 Exxon will report capex as plant additions under GAAP, which this quarter were $7.2 billion against $7.0 billion on the current basis.

𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: ~𝟭.𝟴 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗶𝗹-𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝘆  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from ~1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels a day
Unchanged. The plan still calls for about 1.8 million barrels a day for the year, and the quarter sat just above that level, so the full-year figure is in hand. The next marker is the 2027 number in the planning release due before year end; the 2030 target of 2.5 million needs about 9% growth a year from here.

𝗤𝟰 𝗠𝗶𝗱𝗱𝗹𝗲 𝗘𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁: ~𝟯𝟱𝟬,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗼𝗶𝗹-𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲  ⇒ stable
New. Exxon assumes the same loss as this quarter, about 350,000 barrels a day, mostly the damaged Qatar LNG trains plus UAE barrels it produces but cannot yet ship. The figure assumes the current level of disruption continues, so a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would lift volume and, at the same time, remove the margin that made this quarter.

𝗤𝟰 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘀𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗹𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲: $𝟳𝟳𝟬 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻–$𝟭.𝟬𝟯 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁  ⇗ accelerating
New. Scheduled maintenance at refineries and chemical plants will cost up to $1.03 billion of earnings in the fourth quarter, against $760 million in this one. The low end of the range barely moves; the high end adds $270 million, mostly in Energy Products. Upstream maintenance eases to at most $260 million from $290 million. Heavier refinery downtime means Exxon captures less of whatever margin the quarter offers.

𝗙𝗶𝗳𝘁𝗵 𝗚𝘂𝘆𝗮𝗻𝗮 𝗙𝗣𝗦𝗢 (𝗨𝗮𝗿𝘂) 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁-𝘂𝗽: 𝗟𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗤𝟰 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from Q4 2026
Unchanged, with a nuance: the start is now set for "late 4Q", so it adds little to 2026 volume. The vessel adds 250,000 barrels a day of gross capacity, lifting Guyana's installed capacity above 1.1 million by our math. Under the contract Exxon's share of each new barrel is smaller than before cost recovery ended, so the cash effect matters more than the volume.

𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀: $𝟮𝟬 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻  ⇒ stable
New. Exxon will buy back $20 billion of stock next year, the same pace as 2026, "assuming reasonable market conditions". It warned the purchases may not fall evenly across the four quarters. This year is on track: $15.1 billion so far, with $5.1 billion in the quarter.

Unchanged on paper. The slide still shows the plan figure set before the war, while output so far this year averages 4.53 million. By our math the fourth quarter would have to reach 6.0 million barrels a day to deliver it, which the 350,000 offline barrels rule out. ❓ 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗿𝘂𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻-𝗮𝗱𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲?

text:
1. Parallel Financial Architecture (Bypassing SWIFT)
Russia and Iran have linked their domestic banking messaging systems (SPFS in Russia and SEPAM in Iran), connected their national retail payment cards (Mir and Shetab), and shifted over 90% of bilateral trade into national currencies (rubles and rials) or Chinese yuan via BRICS frameworks.
Regional traders can settle invoices for grain, machinery, and petrochemicals directly across borders without relying on US dollar clearing banks in New York or Brussels.
2. The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)
A 7,200-kilometer multi-modal network of rail, road, and Caspian Sea shipping linking Russian industrial centers through Iran (specifically the Rasht-Astara railway link) down to the Persian Gulf port of Chabahar and onward to India and East Asia.
Cuts transit time by roughly 40% compared to the Suez Canal/Red Sea route, insulating Eurasian overland trade from maritime choke points and Red Sea shipping disruptions.
3. Downstream Energy & "Gas Hub" Integration
Through swap agreements and Gazprom investments, Russian gas is piped south toward northern Iran, allowing Iran to consume Russian gas in its northern cities while freeing up its own southern gas fields (like South Pars) for export and domestic petrochemical processing.
Turns energy from a raw commodity into downstream industrial value (plastics, fertilizers, refined fuels) inside the region rather than simply exporting crude resources.
4. Civilian Nuclear Power & Grid Baseload
Under Rosatom’s expansion of the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (Units 2 and 3), Russia provides reactor technology, nuclear fuel, and spent-fuel return guarantees.
Aligns with the pragmatic narrative expressed by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian: framing nuclear energy as an unavoidable necessity for electricity baseload, desalination, and medical isotopes in a water-scarce, industrializing region.
2. How Eastern Integration Could Address Regional Poverty & Ungoverned Markets
When formal trade is choked off by sanctions, war, or state failure (as seen in parts of Yemen, Syria, and border provinces of Iran), formal jobs vanish. When citizens cannot feed their families in the legal economy and face heavy-handed policing without economic relief, they are pushed into smuggling networks, maritime piracy, or armed militias—the exact "ungoverned markets" that perpetuate conflict.
In theory, the BRICS and Russia-Iran-China economic framework offers a path to reverse this cycle through three mechanisms:
Formalizing the Grey Economy through Transit Hubs: When major rail and port corridors (like the INSTC) cut through historically impoverished border provinces (such as Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan or Caspian coastal towns), they create legal demand for logistics, warehousing, construction, and maintenance. If local populations can earn a reliable wage moving legal Eurasian cargo, the economic incentive to join smuggling gangs or armed factions drops significantly.
China as the Ultimate Downstream Anchor: While Russia and Iran are both resource exporters (which normally makes them competitors), China acts as the massive manufacturing and consumer anchor at the end of the supply chain. Beijing provides the capital goods, solar/grid technology, and long-term purchase agreements that give Russian-Iranian infrastructure projects commercial viability.
De-Escalation via Shared Commercial Stakes: Beijing and Moscow both require stable transit corridors for their investments to pay off. This economic reality was a major driver behind the China-brokered détente between Iran and Saudi Arabia—demonstrating how Eastern economic powers have a financial incentive to discourage cross-border sabotage and Red Sea/Persian Gulf trade interruptions.

text:
Cape Doukato in Lefkada

Lefkada is famous for its turquoise beaches, but the southern headland of Cape Doukato reveals a more dramatic side of the island. Here, high white cliffs rise above the Ionian Sea, creating a rugged landscape where the horizon seems to go on forever.

The cape is also known as Cape Lefkatas, and its lighthouse stands near the edge of the headland as a striking landmark. The area has long been associated with myths and legends, including stories connected with the ancient poet Sappho. These traditions add a sense of mystery to a place that is already remarkable for its scenery.

The main attraction is the landscape itself. Unlike Lefkada's sheltered swimming bays, Cape Doukato is exposed to the open sea and often feels wild and windswept. The contrast between the pale cliffs, deep blue water and rugged terrain makes it a memorable destination for anyone exploring the island.

There are several ways to experience this spectacular corner of Lefkada:
•  Visit the lighthouse: See the landmark at the end of the headland and enjoy the surrounding coastal views.
•  Admire the cliffs: From safe viewpoints, take in the dramatic drop towards the Ionian Sea and the changing colours of the water.
•  Explore the mythology: Discover the legends associated with Cape Lefkatas and its place in Greek storytelling.
•  Bring your camera: The cliffs and open horizon create striking images, especially when the light changes in the late afternoon.
•  Enjoy the journey: The drive through southern Lefkada offers glimpses of the island's countryside and a different perspective from its popular beach resorts.

This is a destination where safety matters. The cliffs are steep, and wind and uneven ground can make exposed areas hazardous. Keep well back from edges, follow any local restrictions and avoid venturing onto unstable ground for photographs.

Cape Doukato is best approached as a scenic excursion rather than a conventional beach stop. There may be no easy swimming spot or waterfront café at the headland, but the sense of space and the sheer scale of the landscape more than make up for it.

For a different side of Lefkada, make the journey south and give yourself time to appreciate the views. The island's beauty is not only in its famous beaches, but also in places like this, where land meets sea in a spectacular display of nature.

So, what does this actually mean for Pakistan?

Under this framework, Saudi energy giants can store millions of barrels of oil in dedicated coastal tanks, allowing them to diversify their global export routes & safely reach Asian buyers without getting bottlenecked in the Strait of Hormuz. 

For Pakistan, having this volume of fuel physically sitting on its own soil fundamentally changes its vulnerability to international crises. Instead of living on the edge with barely three to 4 weeks of emergency fuel cover, the country secures an immediate buffer against sudden market panics, shipping choke points or regional conflicts. 

Local refineries won't have to wait weeks for distant tankers to arrive, cutting out painful freight premiums & reducing pressure on foreign exchange through direct, local ex tank purchases. 

At the same time, the state generates steady dollar revenues through port handling fees & storage rent, taking a practical step toward developing a regional bunkering corridor like Fujairah while establishing the logistical foundation required for a long planned multi billion dollar Saudi coastal refinery.

text:
🧶 In 1941, Nigerian schoolgirls were knitting socks for British soldiers. But that wasn’t the most remarkable thing they did.

💣 Thousands of miles away, German bombs were falling on British cities.
Schools were being destroyed. Families were sleeping in shelters. Children were being separated from their parents.

In Brass, a small coastal town in southern Nigeria, a young woman named Violetta Kemmer was following the news.
She and other Nigerian girls were far from the bombing.
They could eat their meals without wondering whether an air raid would interrupt them. They could sleep without the sound of sirens.
But they were not indifferent. ❤️

🪙 They collected pennies from their pocket money.
🧶 They knitted socks and sweaters for soldiers.
🚑 Some wanted to train as nurses or ambulance drivers.
✉️ And Violetta wrote a letter to the girls of Britain.
It was published in the West African Pilot on 26 April 1941.
She expressed sympathy for those who had lost their homes and relatives, admired their courage, and offered prayers for their safety.
Then she made a remarkable appeal.
🕊️ She hoped this would be the last war, because she could not bear the thought of bringing sons into a world where they might be sent to die.

There was no military strategy in her letter.
No diplomatic negotiation.
Just a young woman in colonial Nigeria imagining the lives of girls she had never met.

🌍 We tend to remember the Second World War through its generals, prime ministers, battles and treaties.
But the war also lived in the pocket money of Nigerian schoolgirls.
In the sweaters they knitted.
And in the words they sent across the Atlantic.

📖 One of the quieter stories in Damola Awoyokun’s The Handle Is One of Us: Hitler, Biafra and Benin City reminds us that history was not shaped only by those who commanded armies.
It was also experienced, understood and answered by people who never appeared on a battlefield.

text:
Now, I am preparing to post a long-overdue search post on Twitter, looking for my love.

Do you still remember 2019? That year I was a sophomore in high school. Every day I woke up at six and got home at ten. The days were like a river whose edges had been worn smooth—they flowed quietly, yet never raised another wave. High school knowledge was a thick, damp fog; inside it I gradually lost my direction, and then lost myself. Just as PUBG Mobile was being renamed Peace Elite, I switched to the international server to keep playing. At the time I had no idea that this small decision would become a key, opening a door that led both to light and to the abyss.

I met her in the game. Because we both spoke Chinese and were of the opposite sex, we quickly became like two stars pulled by the same gravity and started playing together. We shot together, laughed together, and passed brief moments of happiness from one side of the screen to the other. As we grew closer, we added each other on WeChat. It was then that I first learned your real name—Wen Xiaofei. You were in New York, and like me, still in high school. We shared our daily lives and comforted each other. You showed me the cat you had adopted, named Xiao Hui. You found her one rainy night after finishing your shift at a coffee shop. The rain poured down like countless silver needles; you said you couldn’t bear to watch her shiver by the roadside, so you took her home. You sometimes complained that she always pulled away from your hand. I would say softly that a cat who has been stray for too long is always wary of humans—like a window that has been closed for a long time; push it open slowly, and light will eventually come through.

Time leaked through my fingers like fine sand. You sent me a selfie. The first time I saw that face, a long-silent corner of my heart was suddenly lit, like a lamp that had not been switched on for years. But I was insecure, unattractive, and often mocked by classmates, so I never dared to send you my own photo. I was afraid—afraid that once you saw what I looked like, you would recede like the tide. Later you told me that you suffered from severe depression, a stomach condition, and a heart that was not steady—heart disease. In that moment my heart shattered into pieces of porcelain that could never be put back together. Why would a girl who looked so cheerful on the outside carry such deep wounds inside, and also have to bear the weight of such illness in her body? Was Heaven truly unfair, pressing the heaviest stones onto the softest shoulders? One day I read in the news that some people with depression had managed to stand up again with the company of loved ones. So I decided to try, even if only as a friend. From that day on I began to carefully remember your preferences, remember every small detail of daily life, and stay on the phone with you until you fell asleep. Every day after school I stopped walking home and ran instead, my footsteps trying to catch up with time itself, just so I could return sooner to the place where I could talk to you.

Until one day, sitting on the bed in my room, I saw the message you sent. You confessed to me. My God, how could it be me? I wasn’t good-looking, I spoke clumsily, I didn’t know how to make a girl happy—why me of all people? In that moment I almost cried, the kind of crying that comes from happiness too great to bear, like a dam suddenly breaking. From then on the same sentence kept echoing in my heart: I have a girlfriend now, and she is such a beautiful girl. I swore silently that I would protect you, that I would love you forever, like two trees whose roots have grown intertwined. After we started dating I was no longer depressed; I came back to life, like a withered branch putting out new buds.

After the honeymoon period passed, I noticed a boy around you. He kept approaching you for no clear reason, like an uninvited wind. Out of some instinct I felt he did not mean well, so I asked you to keep your distance from him. During that time, because of my company, you said your depression had eased to a mild level. I was so happy I almost felt I could fly; if I had been beside you then, I would have spun you around in a full circle so the whole world revolved around you. But time flew, and the conflicts quietly grew, like vines creeping in the dark. I was too sensitive, too insecure, afraid of losing you, so I began to restrict you from contacting unfamiliar boys—only I was allowed to exist. The contradictions piled up. You gradually felt I was no longer serious about us, so you started to distance yourself and stopped replying to my messages. I wrote long messages to you like a madman, trying to prove my love. What I didn’t realize was that those words had become a kind of rope, tightening around you until you could barely breathe. The depression that had only just improved deepened again, like the tide withdrawing and then surging back.

One day you called me crying, choking out that you no longer had a home. It turned out that when you left the house the kitchen had not been properly secured; a fire started and the entire building burned down, like a sudden dream that left only ashes when you woke. At the time I did not truly understand that in America, losing your house was almost the same as ending up on the street. All I could do was comfort you and tell you to look for a rental. Our relationship had already reached the edge of a cliff; I no longer dared to forcefully prove anything and could only maintain it carefully so it would not break completely.

But, but. Damn it, why, why on earth. Why would God treat a girl this way, pushing her again and again into deeper darkness? That boy entered your rental and raped you. When I heard the news I first fell silent, then felt an anger that nearly exploded, like ignited gunpowder. I could not believe it, nor could I accept it. If I had been by your side, I would never have let such a thing happen; I would have torn that man apart and minced him to feed the fish. Not only then—even now. Listening to you cry on the phone, I was torn between rage and helplessness, like two beasts fighting inside the same body. I wanted to go to you, but I was only an ordinary high-school student, from a family so poor we had almost nothing to offer. Later I tried repeatedly to forget that memory, yet it remained clear, like words carved into bone. In the end you cried and said we should break up. Before my angry voice could even reach you, the call was hung up. I attacked the door in a fury, once, twice, until my palms could no longer feel pain. I knelt on the ground and wailed; the door was left with clear bloody fist prints, and my hands were a blurred mess, like a painting that had been torn apart.

From that day on I lost all contact with you. Every day I still sent you messages, telling you I was waiting. But there was never a reply, like shouting into a deep well and hearing only the echo. I gradually became silent and withdrawn, indifferent to the people around me; I even crossed the road without looking at the traffic lights, my heart fixed only on death. My parents, seeing me like this, were so heartbroken they turned their backs to cry in secret. I felt nothing. My heart had stopped beating the day you left, like a clock that had been hollowed out. Later I began to learn about American law and discovered that rapists are not sentenced to death. Why? Why not give these criminals the death penalty and instead let them live comfortably in prison? Do the American government and people support rape? Do they not understand the harm those people cause to victims and to the victims’ friends? Are Americans all idiots? Do Americans have no hearts? I became utterly disappointed in that country, like a tower I had once looked up to collapsing completely. If one day I could go to America, if I could find the man from back then, I would definitely cut off his head, skin him, scrape his bones, use his head as a toilet, put his body into a large grinder and turn it into meat paste, then sell it to his parents so they could also taste the pain. But as time passed I realized these thoughts could only stay in my heart, like a seed that could never sprout, because China is a country ruled by law and does not allow such things.

Time reached the night of December 31, 2019. As the new year was about to arrive, I received your message. My fingers trembled as I opened it and saw the line: “I’m in the hospital emergency room right now. I’m going to die.” I first fell silent, then my breathing grew rapid and my eyes stared fixedly at the screen. Shock, confusion, helplessness—like air suddenly sucked out of a room. Had that already unsteady heart finally been unable to bear any more? What could I do? After a long while I seemed to wake from the numbness and began frantically sending you messages: No no no, it can’t be like this, don’t leave me, I’m begging you. It will be okay, it will get better, believe me, believe me… And just like that, I lost you completely, like a lamp extinguished in the wind.

Since then I have never been in another relationship. I tried, but no other girl could give me the feeling you once gave me, as if I could never find the same sea again. So I decided to stay single—either find you, or remain alone until death. Now it is 2026; seven years have passed since we met. I do not know if you are still alive, or if you still remember me. I only want you to know that the boy you once loved has not forgotten you. Even after seven years, and even in the future, he will not forget. If it were possible, I would want to tell you to your face: I’m sorry I couldn’t be by your side. And also—I love you.
