SEATTLE — After spending decades scouting college football programs, evaluating NFL free agents, and investing millions of dollars in wide receivers who occasionally struggle to catch a perfectly thrown football, the Seattle Seahawks have discovered an extraordinary alternative: a dog.

Seahawks president of football operations and general manager John Schneider has announced the signing of Ashley Whippet IV, a Frisbee-catching whippet, to a three-year, $18 million contract featuring $12 million guaranteed, unlimited Milk-Bones, and an exclusive endorsement agreement with a national pet-food company.

The signing was inspired by the legendary Ashley Whippet, the three-time world Frisbee champion whose spectacular airborne catches captivated national television audiences during the 1970s. The original Ashley became famous for extraordinary leaps, reportedly reaching heights of nine feet, and even performed during Super Bowl XII.

Schneider reportedly discovered the footage while reviewing unconventional sources for wide receiver prospects.

"I watched this dog launch himself into the air and catch a Frisbee that was practically in another ZIP code," Schneider explained during the team's fictional press conference. "Then I started thinking about the money we're paying professional athletes to accomplish essentially the same thing. The economics were impossible to ignore."

Head coach Mike Macdonald was equally enthusiastic.

"John called me into his office and showed me the video. My first reaction was that the dog had better ball-tracking skills than half the receivers I've coached. My second reaction was to ask whether he could learn the playbook."

EXHIBIT A — AN UNCONVENTIONAL SCOUTING REPORT

According to Seattle's personnel department, Ashley Whippet IV possesses exceptional acceleration, extraordinary leaping ability, and an almost supernatural capacity to track objects moving through the air.

His unofficial 40-yard dash time of 3.2 seconds initially stunned the coaching staff, although observers acknowledged that an assistant coach had released a squirrel near the finish line.

Macdonald immediately recognized the competitive implications.

"We're talking about a receiver who doesn't need to be reminded to watch the ball into his hands. He doesn't turn his head to see who's about to hit him, and he doesn't start celebrating before completing the catch. Those are fundamentals we've been trying to teach professional football players for generations."

Schneider offered a more financial assessment.

"At $6 million a year, he's an absolute bargain. I've seen receivers making four times that amount drop passes my grandmother's poodle could catch."

EXHIBIT B — THE CONTRACT NEGOTIATIONS

Negotiations reportedly became contentious when Ashley's agent demanded a private kennel, personal veterinarian, lifetime supply of premium dog food, and a contractual prohibition against mandatory participation in team meetings exceeding 15 minutes.

Schneider rejected the original proposal.

"Look, we're running a professional football organization, not a luxury dog resort. We had to draw the line somewhere."

The parties eventually settled on $18 million over three seasons, with incentives for receptions, touchdowns, Pro Bowl appearances, and refraining from biting opposing defensive backs.

Macdonald was reportedly concerned about one provision granting Ashley permission to leave practice whenever he hears an ice-cream truck.

"That's going to create some scheduling challenges," the coach admitted. "But we've had players leave practice for considerably less compelling reasons."

The NFL Players Association has requested clarification concerning whether Milk-Bones constitute reportable compensation under the league's salary-cap rules.

EXHIBIT C — THE FIRST PRACTICE

Ashley immediately justified Seattle's investment by catching 49 consecutive passes during his first workout.

His lone incompletion occurred when he abandoned a crossing route to investigate a fire hydrant.

Macdonald dismissed the incident.

"That's a concentration issue. We've dealt with those before. Frankly, I've seen receivers become distracted by a cheerleader in the third row. At least the fire hydrant was on the field."

Coaches discovered that Ashley had little difficulty learning conventional pass routes, although comeback patterns proved troublesome. The dog repeatedly refused to return to the quarterback until someone shouted, "HERE, BOY!"

Macdonald responded by revising Seattle's offensive terminology.

"FETCH!" now signals a deep passing route. "STAY!" indicates maximum pass protection. "ROLL OVER!" has been assigned to the offensive line, while "PLAY DEAD!" remains available for third-and-long situations.

Schneider defended the changes.

"Every successful organization adapts its systems to the talents of its personnel. If we have to replace a 300-page playbook with a dog-training manual, that's what we'll do."

EXHIBIT D — THE NFC WEST RESPONDS

News of Seattle's acquisition reportedly sent shock waves throughout the division.

The San Francisco 49ers are investigating whether defensive backs can legally carry tennis balls onto the field. The Los Angeles Rams have questioned whether a dog should be permitted to compete against a franchise represented by another animal, while Arizona is reportedly considering hiring a professional obedience instructor as its defensive coordinator.

Macdonald remains unconcerned.

"Defensive coordinators spend their careers studying route combinations, coverages, and receiver tendencies. Now they're going to have to learn canine psychology. I'd like to see somebody explain Cover 2 to a border collie."

Schneider believes Seattle has established a competitive advantage that other franchises will struggle to duplicate.

"We're already scouting the Westminster Dog Show. There's some outstanding talent out there that nobody in the NFL has even considered."

EXHIBIT E — A NEW OFFENSIVE PHILOSOPHY

Seattle's offensive staff has developed a special formation designated the K-9 Spread, featuring Ashley in the slot and several conventional receivers positioned outside.

The strategy is straightforward: release Ashley downfield, throw the football as far as possible, and allow instinct to take over.

Macdonald explained the concept.

"We've spent years designing sophisticated offensive systems. Sometimes football is simpler than we make it. You throw something, the dog runs after it, and he catches it. The beautiful part is that he actually brings it back."

There is, however, one complication.

During practice, Ashley repeatedly retrieved the football after making a touchdown catch and returned it directly to the quarterback, occasionally crossing the goal line in the wrong direction.

Macdonald acknowledged that the coaching staff is working on correcting the behavior.

"We've explained that once he reaches the end zone, he's supposed to stop. Unfortunately, every time we throw his ball, he assumes we want it returned."

Schneider has reportedly authorized an additional $250,000 for specialized training.

EXHIBIT F — THE PRESS CONFERENCE TURNS UGLY

The introductory press conference took an unexpected turn when a reporter asked whether signing a dog represented an admission that Seattle had exhausted its conventional personnel options.

Schneider appeared offended.

"Absolutely not. We're identifying talent wherever it exists. Some teams scout the Southeastern Conference. Some scout the Big Ten. We're expanding our evaluation process to include the American Kennel Club."

Another reporter questioned whether Ashley possessed sufficient football intelligence to understand NFL defensive schemes.

Macdonald responded immediately.

"He understands when someone is throwing an object, where it's going, and how to get there before it hits the ground. That's more than I can say for some receivers I've watched."

A third reporter asked whether Ashley would be permitted to participate in touchdown celebrations.

"Within reason," Macdonald replied. "We're trying to discourage him from burying the football in the end zone. Groundskeeping has already complained."

The press conference ended abruptly when Schneider attempted to demonstrate Ashley's catching ability by tossing a Frisbee across the room.

Ashley cleared the conference table, intercepted the Frisbee approximately eight feet above the floor, and landed directly in the lap of an ESPN correspondent.

Schneider smiled.

"Now tell me that wasn't worth eighteen million dollars."

EXHIBIT G — THE HALL OF FAME QUESTION

NFL historians have begun debating whether a successful canine receiver could eventually qualify for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Supporters point to the extraordinary accomplishments of the original Ashley Whippet, whose national fame helped popularize competitive canine Frisbee exhibitions.

Critics argue that dogs cannot reasonably be compared with professional football players.

Macdonald disagrees.

"Speed is speed. Athleticism is athleticism. Catching ability is catching ability. If he gets open and catches touchdowns, I don't care whether he has two legs or four."

Schneider was considerably more emphatic.

"If Ashley catches 100 passes, gains 1,500 yards, and scores 15 touchdowns, somebody's going to have to explain why he shouldn't be considered for the Pro Bowl."

The Hall of Fame has declined comment, although an unidentified official reportedly suggested that urinating on a bust in Canton would constitute automatic disqualification.

THE VERDICT

For decades, NFL franchises have invested enormous sums searching for wide receivers with superior speed, exceptional leaping ability, reliable hands, and the instinctive capacity to track airborne footballs.

The legendary Ashley Whippet demonstrated those abilities before national television audiences more than half a century ago.

John Schneider's fictional acquisition represents the logical conclusion of applying modern personnel economics to an old problem: Why spend $25 million annually on a receiver who drops catchable passes when a dog will retrieve virtually anything thrown in his direction?

Mike Macdonald now possesses an athlete who arrives enthusiastically for practice, never questions the coaching staff, doesn't demand additional targets, and considers catching the football the most enjoyable activity imaginable.

He doesn't complain about his contract, criticize his quarterback, or threaten to hold out during training camp.

He just wants somebody to throw him the ball.

Seattle may finally have discovered the perfect wide receiver.

There remains, however, one potentially catastrophic flaw in the entire experiment.

If somebody throws a Frisbee from the upper deck during the fourth quarter, the Seahawks could find themselves playing with ten men.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

text:
Much fucking better month. September VS October. 

447 trades VS 253 trades so nearly a 200 trade difference. 

September was a choppy mother fucker as in my performance. Got my head out of my ass and started doing more review work in October. 

September ended with a big fuck you loss. Today rolled out a fat little +$12,792.20 session.

I'll put it on youtube. Some good theory on why the CVD inverted today. 

Basically it's end of moth which we all know is the higher volume options contracts that trade. Unlike retail who loves their 0DTE - They're also too poor to afford the premiums of a monthly, otherwise they're just too much risk trading that shit.

Why the fuck do I need to be directionality right and deal with time decay? Ah but the premiums on spreads!? Yeah spreads have horrible RR when it comes to their high win rates.

So typically Fridays have higher volume and more so end of month. 

And I know this will make some people mad. But I think GEX doesn't matter. The theory has holes.

Does SPX options traders hedge futures? Yes.

But you got to understand most people get caught up on market makers trying to stay delta neutral.

Will hedge funds and institutions all ways have inventory on. And a lot at that. 

They have so much inventory that goes into the markets - they aint playing spreads. They work huge tranches of inventory. They might need to cut in 10K ES lots so they hide it, and work it in little chunks at a time through some sort of algo or whatever. Therefore in order to prevent price from moving they must cut up that 10K position and campaign it. They can't get that all in on one price one tick.

So they spread it out over several points. There aint enough liquidity. And as books get thinner, but we see the same volume we would seen on thicker books - now they spend more time cutting in smaller chunks therefore taking more trades which creates long drawn-out ranges and chop.

So they work bigger spreads of price. They can't work as tight as a market maker. Funds, and institutions can't sit cash billions. The shit always needs to be working somewhere at all times, otherwise why would anyone give them investment capital if it's not all being worked? Sure there's some cash right. But why would someone give me 10 million dollar trading account if I only can make a few thousand a session on that?

They wouldn't. They could make more returns on T-notes and NOT split with me - for no risk VS investing with me.

The big boys are always rolling inventory. Therefore they can kind of be looked at like market makers but they run larger spreads or massive areas of inventory that can span 10 points which is necessary to get all their size in or out - therefore they just let the market go a lot fucking further before any profits are locked in.

Also when you hedge like that. You don't go long ES short SPX and make profits. The SPX will expire. You still need to close ES on ES book. You can't open and close different products in different order books.

So at some point the inventory gets SOOO off side in ES, that ES is imbalanced. Doesn't matter if there's hedging in SPX and all that shit. You don't need to watch SPX to know when ES is imbalanced. Each individual book by itself still has it's own inventory. And that granular line of thinking is a way to understand how ES - it's own inventory - can get offside and imbalanced.

More so when SPX contracts just expire. But the futures while they do every quarter, they ain't like options with a more aggressive expiration cycle - therefore when they expire - the ES inventory has to do something!? You going to just keep hedging more and more SPX?! At some point you got too fucking much ES inventory that can get out of control and that HAS TO COME OUT AT SOME POINT IN IT'S OWN BOOK!

Hence delta inversions on the CVD. 

At some point the masses just have to adjust. If I'm not mistaken I have some PDFs on how the indices work and there's specific days just for re-balancing that - don't quote me - are calendar events. Like every quarter.

Lance Breitstein has a video where he mentioned some Trilliom or however the fuck you spell his old firms name? - He mentioned in a 2 year period a few traders made a billion in following these indices institutional rebalances. 

Mean while every other fucking influencer strat is like finger painting done by a child compared to understanding this shit.

When the CVD inverts we can get these steam roller plays. Pockets of bids today sit and transact causing crazy ranges, but then it just pushes down to the next areas then the next area. 

On a really HTF chart you can see we're kind of in a massive fucking range.

So today's trend down can be nothing for institutions with billions in inventory. They have to work massive areas anyways as they could never compete on lower time frames.

Once you understand this and can identify these steam rollers, and fuck me time it. The market direction is per-destined to a degree.

Usually it's much later in the day to figure this out after the morning noise settles in. 

Now below I point out where I exited the last chunk of contracts today. There was a volume leg of 229K lots. Probably the next biggest resting spot if not the biggest of today on the down side. 

That's going to speed bump price. 

Plus someone is resting a long quote on 7600

Resting quotes that sit forever are large traders advertising where they want to trade in the hopes another larger trader will interact.

They work all around that resting quote not just the resting quote so they cut and hide and sweep. It's called campaigning.

Sometimes when you see a sweep around these areas up or whatever it's the same guy just cutting up his tempo. Can't work the same pattern of cutting in all your size. The more random you are with the finesse the more hidden you are.

Now obviously other larger traders see this. So they dance. 

The reason for this is to throw algos off that front run. In the book Flash Crash a Royal Canadian banker named Brad Katsuyama - mentioned how every time he posted a large order he would get front ran. Didn't know it was HFT algos, until deeper investigations. This was skunk works level of secrecy here. 

The author Michael Lewis mentions that large traders want to trader with other large traders. They need to. 

So they went into dark pools which those providers just ended up selling that data to HFT firms.

But now it's more hidden. This is why the bid offer or level 2 depth almost always looks the same. They iceberg in. But doing pure iceberging like say 10K lots - we as retail would see that and front run it. So.... 

They mask themselves more by smaller cutting of orders and random sweeps and shit.

They need to stay off the front running algos radar and fuck with their signals.

Everyone stays hidden until the last moment.

Now yes. Big traders can trade off the book with other banks or private liquidity providers - BUT! At some point someone needs to adjust and take inventory off the public book or put some back in.

See when they trade off the books that inventory is already open interest. At some point after they hot potato that shit to each other off the books someone will be left with "the bag" and need to go on the books and cut in.

CBOE exchange will gladly make magic inventory appear on SPX FLEX options and take the other side of your hundred million dollar bet in one transaction.

However they're going to cut in with their own market maker algos or other types of algos. Because on the other side of a large block of trades like that is another large traders, and it's zero sum. One of them will get fucked.

So these private liquidity providers will campaign their side where as Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund may not have the tech knowledge or can't be fucked with campaigning in.

But those transactions are late reported on the tape. So now everyone can see your hundred million dollar one shot trade with a liquidity provider and someone like Ken Griffin can squeeze you then acquire your firm at a discount.

So campaigning is much better in some ways then doing a huge block trade with another rival competitor.

This is why advertising in the order book by laying up one resting larger order to stick out from the "average size" can act as advertising. 

Other large traders see it and if they need to move inventory they will trade around here. So this is where it gets all choppy and sweepy and smaller little pockets of icebergs come in.

They're cutting. And yes two big traders transact, but now it's more anonymous. You still can't fucking figure who's on the other side and by how much inventory and if it's open or closed interests. There's much more anonymity to doing this even though they advertised - Unlike say Leopold Aschenbrenner who just goes open interest NVDA 50 million or whatever. The other guy who traded with him knows... He knows and finance is a dirty game. And he knows if the position is open or closed, and who he traded with exactly. 

Had someone like this just cut in. Will - no one will really know who, nor if it's all open or closed interest - nor the actual size of the position.

However it's a better method to allow larger traders advertise they're looking for liquidity, but keeping it way more anonymous, and prevents retail and HFT algos from front running or fucking with them.

See. You just learned something new. You really can't find everything on the internet for free and packaged this well without Easter egg hunting hundreds of pockets of information.

That's why you should like and share this. Because now you too - will see resting liquidity differently, and then realize how a lot of other retail traders don't understand why they do that. 

Sure sometimes they advertise and no one plays with them. That's real risk.

text:
BIG TECH HOLDS $3 TRILLION IN SPENDING COMMITMENTS FOR THE AI BOOM 

Wall Street’s AI selloff intensified Friday, sending the $QQQ Nasdaq 100 down 4% toward a technical correction and the S&P 500 down 2.5%. Investors are questioning whether roughly $750B in annual AI spending can deliver sufficient returns as major technology companies’ core businesses show signs of slowing, Bloomberg reports.

•Tech Rout:  
$INTC Intel plunged 31%, its largest decline in over four decades, following weak guidance. $AMZN Amazon fell 2.3% amid rising capital spending. The Nasdaq 100 has erased over $1.2T in market value during October, heading for its worst month since March 2025.

•AI Profitability:  
Slowing advertising, consumer and retail businesses are raising concerns about AI investment returns. Analysts say investors increasingly want evidence that strong demand translates into earnings and cash flow.

•Financing Pressure:  
Amazon established an $80B hardware-backed financing facility, while Blackstone warned Anthropic may initially receive a below-investment-grade rating after its IPO.

•Broader Markets:  
Bitcoin fell below $77K following Binance’s record $6.3B hack. Oil climbed amid fears of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran, while Treasuries headed for their best month since February 2025.

•Market Risks:  
UBS warned of a potential midcycle AI spending slowdown. Miller Tabak’s Matt Maley cautioned that broader market weakness could shift investors from defensive sectors into cash, undermining the rotation supporting equities.

•Earnings Trends:  
Q3 S&P 500 profits are projected to grow 30% YoY, but earnings beats average just 1.4% versus historical averages of 7.5%–8%, weighed down by Meta and Alphabet.

•Downside Risk:  
BTIG’s Jonathan Krinsky sees a potential S&P 500 test of its 200-day moving average near 7,306, more than 5% below Thursday’s close.

•Historical Trends:  
November has averaged a 3.5% Nasdaq gain in midterm election years, while the S&P 500 and Dow averaged 2.7% and 2.6%, respectively. Historical patterns offer no guarantee.

text:
Raises are coming in January for minimum-wage workers in 16 states, including Colorado.

Here in Colorado, the statewide minimum wage rises 55 cents on January 1, from $15.16 to $15.71 an hour. That’s about $32,700 a year for full-time work. Denver’s goes up 55 cents too, to $19.84. Both rise automatically with inflation each year.

Across the country, the 2027 minimum wage will range from $7.25 an hour to $18.40 in Washington, D.C. For a full-time worker, that’s a difference of more than $23,000 a year.

Washington state will have the highest statewide minimum on January 1, at $17.73, followed by Connecticut at $17.48 and California at $17.40. A few more places adjust later in the year, including Alaska, which goes to $15 on July 1, and D.C., Oregon and Florida, which adjust for inflation.

Meanwhile, 20 states still use the federal minimum of $7.25, which hasn’t changed since July 2009. Five of those have no state minimum wage law at all: Alabama, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina and Tennessee.

A few things to know before comparing job offers:
~These are floors for most adult workers who don’t earn tips. Many cities, like Denver, set higher ones.
~Some states allow lower rates for very small businesses or teenage workers.
~Tipped workers often have a lower base wage, though employers generally have to make up the difference if tips fall short.

As a childcare center owner, I watch these numbers closely. Every January raise is real money for workers, and it’s also a real cost for small businesses that run on thin margins. Both things are true, and I think it’s worth talking about honestly.

If you’re an hourly worker, check your first January paycheck to make sure the new rate shows up. If it doesn’t, ask your employer, and if that doesn’t fix it, contact the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment.

I’m not a financial advisor.

Sources: U.S. Department of Labor, Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, Bloomberg Tax, ColoradoBi

text:
introducer: “please welcome the secretary of the treasury, scott bessent.”

scott bessent: “good afternoon and thank you all for being here today. i’m pleased to be joined by fbi director kash patel, cms administrator mehmet oz, ftc chairman andrew ferguson, and assistant attorney general colin mcdonald. as we bring new force to the fight against fraud, president trump has made clear that the war on fraud is not the work of one department, but a mandate that we must carry across the entire administration. i am proud to stand alongside so many dedicated colleagues who are delivering on that mandate every day. america is a generous country and the compassion of our people imposes a corresponding duty on our government. that is why i visited minnesota in january to make clear that the u.s. treasury is deploying every tool to bring an end to this egregious unchecked fraud and hold perpetrators to account. over the past year, treasury returned $175 million in payments that would have gone to deceased individuals and expanded the do not pay access from 4 to 99 percent of federal programs. further, we have stopped almost $190 million and returned over $100 million in funds to u.s. victims of overseas fraud, ordered an audit of approximately $9 billion in treasury contracts, and together with our partners at the irs proposed stronger eligibility checks for health insurance tax credits. these actions form one front of a whole-of-government effort led by vice president vance. the vice president’s task force first convened in march, and he has worked tirelessly to restore vigilance and responsible stewardship in the management of public money. since january 2025, the trump administration has uncovered more than $260 billion in fraud, prevented $72 billion in taxpayer funds from going out the door to illicit actors annually, and brought enforcement actions against nearly $60 billion. nowhere is the work more urgent than here in minnesota. in the weeks following my visit, treasury’s financial crimes enforcement network, known as fincen, issued a geographic targeting order to trace criminal networks that divert funds overseas and ensure that taxpayer dollars go to the american people, not terror groups like al-shabaab. we have ongoing investigations, at home and abroad, into al-shabaab, its networks, and its enablers. since the start of the trump administration, fincen data have also supported the law enforcement effort that led to the arrest and charging of 115 fraudsters, as well as 75 convictions and nearly 3,000 subpoenas across minnesota. but just yesterday, irs-ci assisted with investigative activity at several sites suspected of fraud. i want to give a shout out to our great officers at irs-ci. they don’t get much press, but they are quietly one of the most effective groups in the united states government for fighting fraud. today, fincen released additional information to help refer new leads to law enforcement and provide support to ongoing investigations. we issued a notice to help financial institutions identify, report suspicious activity, especially those involving charities and nonprofits. the notice highlights how criminals exploit fundraising capabilities to facilitate terrorist financing, fraud, and other illicit activity. fincen also issued an alert on the risk associated with cross-border transactions originated by money service businesses known as msbs. the alert details how bad actors can exploit msbs to move funds overseas. fincen identified over $8 billion in potentially suspicious foreign agent-directed payments between 2021 and 2025 alone. and today’s alert urges financial institutions to be vigilant in detecting, identifying, and reporting suspicious activity arising from certain cross-border payments, including u.s.-based msbs. the next phase of this fight, meanwhile, will make it easier than ever for whistleblowers who know where the fraud is to help lead us to it. until now, any citizen who detected fraud was forced to navigate a maze of tip lines scattered across law enforcement agencies. no more. for the first time, we’ve created a single centralized portal at https://t.co/Kiw3reJlOk. treasury is proud to seed this new $25 million fraud whistleblower incentive program. anyone who submits information that leads to a conviction or enforcement action may be eligible for a $30,000 reward. speaking up has long carried a cost for whistleblowers. under president trump, it can offer a reward. now the industrial-scale fraud that tim walz shamefully and perhaps knowingly allowed to fester is the defining legacy of his administration. but with president trump back in office, washington is no longer content to watch minnesota’s fraud epidemic spiral from a distance. the days of indifference are over, and under this president’s leadership, wherever the money leads, the full weight of government will follow. now i’m pleased to turn it over to someone who has helped give the fight against fraud both its discipline and its force, fbi director kash patel.”

kash patel: “thank you, scott. this fbi follows the money. this fbi will put in prison anyone who commits fraud anywhere in the world against any american citizen. thanks to president trump, we finally have a commander in chief who prioritized the initiative to go after the fraudsters with the full force of government. thanks to the vice president for leading the anti-fraud task force with our department of justice partners and the assistant attorney general, colin mcdonald. and thanks to this great team here with chairman ferguson, with dr. oz, with our state and local partners. it is an interagency lift. as the secretary said, it is a whole-of-government approach, and the results we are delivering are truly historic. we’re here today to announce that just yesterday, fbi minneapolis and our partners executed 17 search warrants in a single day to combine into a 26-count indictment. three of those search warrants were at a child care center, two of those search warrants were at the residences of the owners of those centers, and two more of those search warrants were on the early intensive development and behavioral intervention unit here in minnesota. fbi minneapolis and our interagency partners arrested four of the alleged fraudsters. aspen associates, 11 counts of health care fraud, $8 million in intended loss. jama mohammed, american home health care, six counts of health care fraud, $3.27 million in intended loss. home sweet home, eight counts of health care fraud, $10 million in intended fraud. and habiba mohammed, smart therapy, one count of conspiracy to defraud the united states, totaling nearly $20 million in intended fraud and loss. the subjects intended to defraud thousands of victims of over $41 million, money that was supposed to go to those in need with our precious taxpayer dollars funding that bill. instead, they thought they could get away with their crimes. they did not succeed because of this team and the president and vice president’s anti-fraud task force. we are going to continue working with our state and local partners and the interagency to dismantle, disrupt, and take down fraud networks wherever they are, in minnesota, right here in st. cloud, and everywhere else in the country. the fbi’s initiative under the vice president’s fbi’s most wanted fraudsters list has also seen historic achievements. in just four months after launching the list, we captured four of the most wanted fraudsters on four separate continents who were on the run for nearly 5,000 days, who defrauded americans of $2 billion. there is no other administration in u.s. history that has set out in such an initiative. we set out on it, we delivered for the american people, and we’re going to continue manhunting fraudsters in every corner of the earth. right here in minnesota, the feeding our futures program has achieved historic success in terms of our investigation. we have charged, thanks to our department of justice partners, 81 subjects, 70 have already been convicted, and their fraud value is over one half billion dollars. these communities will no longer be ravaged by these fraudsters who come here to siphon away our precious dollars from our most needy, our senior citizens, and our children. this fbi is proud to stand with the trump administration and vice president vance’s leadership and our interagency partners, and know this to any fraudsters who continue or think they will continue to defraud americans. this fbi will continue to follow the money, we will continue to work with our interagency partners, and we will put every last one of you in prison. i’m truly thankful of fbi minneapolis, our sac, and the entire fbi squad in minneapolis for me as your director. thank you for working tirelessly to this effort, and most importantly, thank you for being a partner in this team. it is truly an interagency lift, and we are here to deliver these historic results. it’s a great day to be here in minnesota. it’s a great day for america because the world knows we are not just watching fraud. we’re taking action and we’re kicking butt. and now it’s my honor to introduce my dear friend and one of the champions of the anti-fraud movement, dr. oz.”

mehmet oz: “in many ways, the war on fraud, our nation’s war on fraud, started right here in minnesota. it’s not an issue to be proud about, it’s just a reality. and we have been doing a lot of work in minnesota, as we have in many other states, because the problems we identified here are not unique to minnesota, but they’re particularly evident in minnesota. since the inauguration of these programs that the president, again, assigned the vice president to run this anti-fraud task force, we’ve embarked on an unprecedented quest to crush fraud and corruption here and nationwide. the network of crime, the river of criminal activities, runs deeper than we ever thought possible. and today, we’re going to put another face to the kind of bad behavior that we’re detecting and preventing. director patel has agreed to help me. this is charmaine meadows. we want to put a name and a face to some of the things we’re talking about. earlier this month, charmaine was not just indicted, she was convicted by a federal jury for stealing over three and a half million dollars for the now-defunct minnesota medicaid housing stabilization services program. there’s many cautionary tales here, so i’m going to spend a few moments to bring alive what we are doing at the national level with one individual here in minnesota. this program, the medicaid housing program, was designed to keep homeless and disabled seniors who were suffering serious conditions, the exact kind of people you want to put your hand out and help back up again. it was designed to help keep them out of institutions, which also saved taxpayer dollars. and by helping them get comfortable and stable housing, it was supposed to achieve that. but charmaine and fraudsters like her don’t want that to happen, and they act in ways that obscure the process that could have allowed it to occur. the program was so overrun with corruption that it ballooned from being about a two and a half million dollar program when it was first established in 2020, just six years ago, to over a hundred million dollars in 2024. that is a forty-fold increase in four years. that’s impossible to stand. if you’re even paying a slight bit of attention to what you’re doing, you would never let that happen. unfortunately, it looks like that was the norm in many instances. minnesota shut the program down. i’m going to say that again. this housing stabilization program, which everyone on this stage thinks has merit, was shut down because of fraudsters like charmaine meadows. now she billed more hours than possible. she hired untrained individuals overseas. she did unspeakable things that broke the very integrity of this valuable program, leading to it being completely removed. it was no longer offering those services to worthy folks living in minnesota who could benefit from them. that is the price we pay for allowing charmaine meadows to not only say, this is her website, by the way. i couldn’t photoshop this. this is exactly what you see at proven, personalized, profitable. that last word, of course, being the operative one. now, no one’s getting housing services. let’s get back to charmaine. she billed a program for housing services that were never provided to vulnerable medicaid beneficiaries who could have desperately used them. she billed for services across multiple states and countries at a time. at the same time, that is physically impossible to provide services all at once. her employees were doing more than 20 hours per day of work. again, she claims, not really happening. that unfortunately led to people, even in a hospital, being offered services, which again, not legal and physically impossible, a telltale sign of fraud. that’s how we shut down people like charmaine and her colleagues like hers. we go after them. folks like kash patel, treasury secretary bessent, and the law enforcement team here in minnesota and elsewhere went after her, and she’s going to jail. that’s the face of this problem. let’s talk about how we actually deal with the issues. thank you. the first major issue we have to do at accomplish nationwide is being able to revalidate providers. that means, specifically, are you really allowed to do the service that you’re being told you can do? many of these programs got out of kilter because unlicensed individuals and unmonitored settings did unmeasured tasks, and that led to huge increases in taxes. so revalidation asks, are you able and eligible to provide the services? to be eligible, by the way, you can’t have been convicted as a felon. you must be licensed in the state, here in minnesota, in this case, to own a business. you’ve got to pass inspections. you have to avoid being fired from medicare or medicaid in the past. you cannot have been excluded from the programs. we asked minnesota to revalidate all of the high-risk providers here in minnesota, 14 categories. 30 percent, almost one in three, of all the people providing services in minnesota could not be revalidated. i’ll say that again. one in three people, roughly, who are providing services were not allowed to provide services. that degree of fraud, again, you have to purposely be averting your glance to allow that to happen. that is similar to what we’re seeing in places like new york around social adult daycare, and here in minnesota, 50 percent of people in social adult daycare were not allowed to provide that service. i have to ask the bigger question, should we be using federal tax dollars to pay people to play mahjong and card games as they hang out in clubhouses for crooks? an issue for a separate day, perhaps, but one that comes to mind here. the second big thing we did was to start working closely with treasury, and i want to applaud secretary bessent for being open to thoughts and, in fact, proactively helping us identify the real issue here, which is we are catching the charmaines of the world. they’re low-level street operators. they’re real capos. the real people at the top of the pyramid, they keep getting away with this. we need to go upstream to capture those folks. we don’t want the foot soldiers. we want the people who hired the foot soldiers, the ones who hired them. the department of treasury is the raft that will take us there. i’m excited to announce that earlier this month, cms signed a memorandum of understanding with treasury that will help figure out who the real villains are to help us track where the money is going. it’s a formal cooperation between our agencies. again, the president and vice president have insisted on this. it’s an all-government effort, and this will allow us, for the first time, to collaborate in ways never before possible, at least at scale. secretary bessent’s team of forensic accountants are going to help us follow the money, and they were using the fincen program that he mentioned earlier, the financial crimes enforcement network, and they’re allowing us to use cross-referencing of enrollment records, of banking details, of oig, office of inspector general, hotline tips, and the fraud prevention system in general. so think of the godfather. the godfather, you’ve got all these street operators doing all kinds of illicit activities, but the don, don corleone, he’s actually taking the money at the top of the pyramid and siphoning it off. that’s how the multinational criminal organizations get their money. that’s why they’re in america, because during covid, we introduced the possibility of defrauding the federal government at scale, especially in healthcare services, and they have taken advantage of it. so we’re moving on to the big boys, and the secretary, just yesterday, inaugurated a closer relationship with the irs, which is going to be a very valuable asset, because if people are lowly enough to steal from the poor, if criminals take from the poor, they’re almost certainly not paying their taxes. and so by passing that information to the irs, and the irs, i have learned, has 2,900 gun-carrying accountants, but they have a lot of accountants as well as the gun-carrying ones. they have an enforcement arm, the criminal investigation arm, that they are working closely with us to identify individuals, because remember, these criminals, they don’t steal the money without putting it somewhere. they don’t declare that money, because if you steal the money, you’re not paying your taxes, but you do sign your tax return. so we don’t have to wait for all the things that normally we have to fulfill in order to take action. the irs has a separate ability to enforce the law to prevent these financial scams, as well as the tax evasion that takes place. this connects all the different points together that allows us to help figure out exactly how the money is being stolen from the poor, and just recently, this month, we connected the dots in california with hospice. we have several hospices that we knew were sending the same money that they were stealing to one bank account. we found that bank account had many other hospices that were pushing money into it as well. it turned out it was one big web, one network of criminals, and we took the whole thing down by no longer paying, and as soon as these criminals stopped making money, they run away. this all-government approach works because we have close personal relationships as well as working relationships. secretary bessent, thank you very much for standing up for the needs for us to work together as a team and breaking down siloed barriers historically that have held us apart. now, let me introduce another good friend, colin mcdonald. he’s the assistant attorney general for fraud enforcement, who’s done a yeoman’s job pulling together so many disparate pieces in the quilt of law enforcement in this great nation. colin.”

colin mcdonald: “thank you, dr. oz. one hundred and sixty-two days ago, this team of public servants announced the largest fraud takedown in minnesota history, fifteen new defendants charged with federal felonies in schemes reaching more than $90 million in fraud. we said then that those charges were just the beginning of our work to root out rampant fraud in minnesota, and we meant it. today we’re announcing just a sliver of the immense work underway to restore the rule of law, safeguard taxpayer dollars, protect the vulnerable, and punish wrongdoers in minnesota. just this week alone, five defendants have been charged with health care fraud offenses in medicaid fraud schemes involving more than $48 million in intended loss, including $29 million in schemes that have been uncovered for the first time. this follows multiple defendants charged with snap benefits fraud last week. and yesterday, in separate ongoing criminal investigations, the fbi and our law enforcement partners executed numerous search warrants in a coordinated regional operation. the cases that we are prosecuting involve fraudsters targeting tax dollars meant to help the most vulnerable americans. we are also activating all enforcement tools to recover stolen money. last week, we filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking to forfeit three properties in minneapolis valued at approximately $519,000, allegedly purchased with proceeds from a fraud scheme that took money meant to feed our children. and our prosecutors and agents are not only charging new cases, they are actively proving them in court and ensuring real consequences for wrongdoers. already this month, two fraud defendants have been convicted at trial for their fraud schemes, including one for defrauding a minnesota housing program designed to help secure housing for the homeless. the state of minnesota was forced to shut down that program after costs skyrocketed from $2.5 million to $107 million in just four years. that was not supply and demand. that was fraud. and as dr. oz mentioned, that program no longer exists because the fraudsters drained it dry, and those homeless who needed that help no longer have that program because of fraudsters. as for prison sentences, two days ago, salim saeed was sentenced to 30 years imprisonment for his role in the feeding our future fraud scheme. he was responsible for more than $44 million in fraud proceeds and used the money to fund his luxury lifestyle, including vehicles and a luxury home. just this morning, today, saeed farah was sentenced to 78 months in prison for his role in a scheme to bribe a juror during his prior fraud trial, with $2,000 in cash delivered to the juror’s home. that is the fraud that we are confronting in this district, in the state of minnesota. all told, over roughly the past 115 days, 14 fraud defendants in minnesota have been sentenced to a combined total of 988 months in prison. that is over 82 years of prison time for fraud crimes in this state, and that does not count the 40-year sentence imposed for a feeding our futures defendant earlier this year. ladies and gentlemen, that is the new normal, and fraudsters here should know it. now, these results do not happen automatically. they require earnest, dedicated, experienced, talented public servants to do the work, like all of the individuals on the stage here with me. i specifically commend u.s. attorney dan rosen, first assistant u.s. attorney joe, the prosecutors in the minnesota u.s. attorney’s office, and the prosecutors from the fraud division who have come from all over the country to do this important work here in minnesota. they’ve come from michigan, missouri, new jersey, north carolina, virginia, texas, and other places from america to confront the fraud epidemic here in minnesota. they are sacrificing time with their families and children back home to do the work of justice here in minnesota. we are not doing this work alone. we are working hand-in-hand with the talented and dedicated agents and analysts with the fbi, irs-ci, hsi, hhs-oig, the postal inspection service, usda-oig, va-oig, and other law enforcement partners to do this work, and i thank them all. let me be clear. this is still the beginning of our work in minnesota. we will be here for as long as it takes to punish the wrongdoers in minnesota, to deter additional criminal conduct, and restore the public’s confidence in the rule of law. and now it’s my honor to welcome chairman andrew ferguson to the podium.”

text:
ROUND IX
SUCH SUBSIDIARY BODIES
A CITIZEN'S DAMNATION OF THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION AND THE EUROPEAN UNION, FOR THE ABUSE OF AMERICAN GOOD FAITH, TRUST AND SACRIFICE; AND A PLEA TO THE NATIONS OF EUROPE

Raised by a citizen of the United States under the Constitution and the Declaration of Independence, and laid before the President and the Congress in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances"

AGAINST the North Atlantic Treaty Organization as it stands in 2026: its Council, commands, agencies and offshoots. AGAINST the European Union: its Commission, Council, Parliament, Court and banks.

Not against the nations of Europe, save France and England, damned already in Rounds III and VII. The rest are our oldest allies. This falls on the machinery they built over them.

I. WHAT WE SIGNED

Washington, 4 April 1949. Fourteen articles. Article 3: each Party, "by means of continuous and effective self-help and mutual aid," will "maintain and develop" its own strength. Article 5: each answers an attack with "such action as it deems necessary." Article 7: the Security Council keeps "the primary responsibility." Article 9: "such subsidiary bodies as may be necessary." Article 10: membership for "any other European state." Article 12: after ten years, any Party may call the rest to "consult together for the purpose of reviewing the Treaty."

No article names a commander, an agency, a budget, a partner, or a member that is not a state. The text was changed once, in 1951, for Turkey and the Mediterranean. Everything since came by communique.

Monroe's bargain ran both ways: Europe out of our hemisphere; America out of "the wars of the European powers in matters relating to themselves." Washington told us "to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world," and to trust only "temporary alliances for extraordinary emergencies."

We set that warning aside for you. We kept faith. This is what was done with it.

II. THE ALLIANCE

It has amended itself without amending its treaty. 1991: "Alliance security must also take account of the global context." 1999: "non-Article 5 crisis response operations." 2010: "Crises and conflicts beyond NATO's borders." 2022: crisis management "at strategic distance"; "The Indo-Pacific is important for NATO." Cyberspace, "a domain of operations," 2016. Space, "an operational domain," 2019. None went to our Senate.

It has made war on a state that attacked no member. In April 1998 our Senate wrote that "the core purpose of NATO must remain the collective defense of the territory of all Alliance members." Within a year: Belgrade. 78 days. More than 38,000 sorties. No Security Council resolution cited in NATO's own account. On 28 April 1999 our House split 213 to 213 on authorizing it: "So the Senate concurrent resolution was not concurred in." The bombing went on.

It has carried our forces far past its own map. Article 6 draws Europe, North America, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic north of the Tropic of Cancer. It led in Afghanistan eleven years, above 130,000 troops at the peak. Libya, more than 26,000 sorties. Iraq. The Horn of Africa. Partners from the Mediterranean to the Gulf to the Indo-Pacific.

It has raised a command, a trust fund and a purchase list for a state that is not a member. Wiesbaden, which it says "does not make NATO a party to the conflict." A trust fund above EUR 1.4 billion. A list under which "NATO Allies purchase critical defence equipment from the United States, which is then delivered to Ukraine," past USD 6 billion, with money from Australia and New Zealand, which are not members either. At Ankara, EUR 70 billion pledged for 2026. Sides aside: none of it is in the charter.

It has set middlemen between our forces and our purposes: channels we do not control, our military does not distribute, and the charter never approved. Its own procurement agency, given "a central role." The European Investment Bank, rewritten to fund "pure military investments," about EUR 4 billion into defence in 2025. The European Peace Facility, EUR 11.1 billion for Ukraine by 2024, EUR 6.6 billion more on 25 September 2026. The Union's EUR 150 billion in SAFE loans, at least 65 percent of each purchase's components bought from the Union, Ukraine or its European partners.

It has let us carry it. On NATO's own budgets we pay 14.9 percent, the same as Germany. That was never the bill. In 2025 the United States carried about 62 percent of all allied defence spending. Our Congress found it in 1998: "the United States already pays more than a proportionate share of the costs of the common defense of Europe." Article 3 has bound every Party to self-help since 1949. At The Hague they promised to honor it by 2035. Our State Department: "Content to free-ride on U.S. security guarantees, European nations slashed their defense spending and let their militaries atrophy."

It has given foreign courts the first claim on our soldiers, and abused the grant. Our Code "applies in all places." Our law authorizes "all means necessary and appropriate" to free our people from the Court at The Hague. Yet under its Status of Forces Agreement the host may try our soldiers first for any offence not against our own people or property and not done on duty; we may only ask for "sympathetic consideration." Our Senate consented in 1953 on condition: "The criminal jurisdiction provisions of Article VII do not constitute a precedent for future agreements." Even what the treaty reserves to us was taken. At Aviano, a NATO base, we asserted that the Air Force officer commanding its security had acted on official duty. Italy tried him in absentia, convicted him in 2009, and its highest court upheld it in 2012. Our own Manual for Courts-Martial still calls the host's claim law: "Under international law, a friendly foreign nation has jurisdiction to punish offenses committed within its borders by members of a visiting force".

It has quartered our soldiers among governments that defend the court hunting them. Afghanistan was NATO's war. In 2020 the International Criminal Court opened its investigation of it, reaching our forces. When we sanctioned that court in October 2026, the Dutch Prime Minister pledged to do "whatever we need to defend the ICC." The Union's foreign-policy chief: threats against it are "not acceptable." Our law, since 2002: "The United States will not recognize the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court over United States nationals."

It has opened every door but one. On 31 March 1954 Moscow raised Soviet membership in the Treaty. The Western powers' draft reply: "the completely unreal character of such a suggestion."

III. THE UNION

It has made itself a person in law: "The Union shall have legal personality." It is not a state. It never signed our treaty. It wrote our treaty into its own anyway: its defence commitments "shall be consistent with commitments under the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, which, for those States which are members of it, remains the foundation of their collective defence."

It has overruled its own peoples. France said no in 2005; Lisbon passed its Parliament in 2008. The Netherlands said no in 2005 and in 2016; both were ratified anyway. Ireland said no twice and was asked again twice. Denmark, once, and was asked again. Greece said no in 2015 and was handed terms a week later.

It has called a room unanimous by emptying it. On 14 December 2023 Hungary's Prime Minister was invited out "so that a unanimous decision could be taken in his absence."

It has set its Court over their constitutions, until their own courts answered. Germany's, 5 May 2020: "ultra vires." Poland's, 7 October 2021: "inconsistent" with Poland's Constitution.

It has extended its system into this hemisphere. Monroe, 1823: "any attempt on their part to extend their system to any portion of this hemisphere" is "dangerous to our peace and safety." He spared your colonies: "With the existing colonies or dependencies of any European power we have not interfered and shall not interfere." We have kept that word for 203 years. French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique and Saint-Martin are Union territory in the Americas. Greenland and eight more are associated with it. Your colonies were the carve-out. Your system is not.

Yet: 17 January 2026, Mercosur signed; when its own Parliament sent the deal to its Court, the Union applied it anyway from 1 May. 14 February, Canada signed into SAFE, "the first non-European country to join." 20 October: "The Arctic is Europe's Northern Neighbourhood." "The EU is part of the Arctic." "Arctic security is European security." Dual-use corridors for military mobility. A cable from Greenland straight to Europe. 30 October, Montreal, in writing: "an ever-closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself"; Canada in the Union's "Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP) missions and operations," "from the Arctic region to the Black Sea"; and "Ukraine's Euro-Atlantic integration." The same day, the Union's bank signed "a Framework Agreement paving the way for EIB investment in Canada."

The Arctic Council was founded on the rule that it "should not deal with matters related to military security." It has been paused since 3 March 2022. Its three binding agreements bind eight Arctic states and no Union. The Union asked to sit there in 2013. It is still waiting.

When we spoke of Greenland, European armies came to exercise on it through 2026. France offers Europe a nuclear umbrella, the decision "entre les mains du President de la Republique." The Union plans "a true European defence union."

Our State Department has "re-established absolute primacy in our hemisphere," and will "reverse the expansion of all other forms of foreign military influence," so that our neighbors "never feel that they owe political fealty to any extra-hemispheric power."

IV. WHAT WE GAVE

From 26 June 1948 to 30 September 1949 we fed a blockaded Berlin by air: more than 2.3 million tons, more than 189,000 American flights. Congress appropriated $13.3 billion to rebuild Western Europe. Twenty-one American cemeteries on your soil hold about 104,000 of our dead.

What we can give, we can withhold. In 1956 we told London and Paris to leave Suez and held back the dollars until they did. We approved the constitution in Bonn and all but dictated the one in Tokyo. We brought down the governments in Tehran in 1953 and Guatemala City in 1954.

As our troops say, we can put a Burger King anywhere in twelve hours. We fed a city by air for fifteen months. We can carry your trade bilaterally.

About 68,000 of our troops are stationed permanently in Europe, before rotations, across 31 permanent bases. Our combatant commands span the globe. Our law requires "not less than 11 operational aircraft carriers." Not a threat. A reminder: the largest military in the world is based everywhere.

We have played nice so you would look better. That ends the day the Union formally plants itself in this hemisphere: by membership, by arms, or by claim.

V. TO THE TWENTY-SEVEN

Our treaties bind us to states, not to the Union. If you are our oldest allies, our duty is to protect you from it.

Our State Department: "Submitting to the unaccountable supranational regulatory bureaucracy of the European Union, the continent deindustrialized, failed to innovate, and slipped into economic malaise." And: "It is time for European nations to wake up."

The Union built two doors and never shows you either. Article 48: amendments "may, inter alia, serve either to increase or to reduce the competences conferred on the Union in the Treaties." Use it to dissolve the bodies you never elected. Article 50: "Any Member State may decide to withdraw from the Union in accordance with its own constitutional requirements." Use it if they will not go.

Hold your constitution against the Union's law, line by line. Here is the line each of you gave away, and what was done to you after.

AUSTRIA. Accession Act 1994, Art. I: "the authorities ... shall be authorized to enter into the Treaty regarding the accession of Austria to the European Union." 2000: fourteen governments cut political contacts with Vienna over the coalition you elected.

BELGIUM. Art. 34: "The exercising of specific powers can be assigned by a treaty or by a law to institutions of public international law." October 2016: Wallonia refused CETA, 46 to 16. The signature was had within two weeks.

BULGARIA. Art. 85: Parliament ratifies treaties that "grant the European Union powers arising from this Constitution." Monitored by the Commission 2007 to 2023. Kept off Schengen's land borders until 2025.

CROATIA. Art. 143: Croatia "shall confer upon the institutions of the European Union the powers necessary" for membership. March 2005: your accession talks, postponed.

CYPRUS. Art. 1A: "No provision of the Constitution shall be deemed to annul" what becomes "necessary by reason of its obligations as a member state of the European Union." March 2013: your parliament voted 36 to 0 against the levy. Your depositors paid anyway.

CZECH REPUBLIC. Art. 10a: "Certain powers of Czech Republic authorities may be transferred by treaty to an international organization or institution." Munich, 29 September 1938: Chamberlain and Daladier signed away your land without you at the table.

DENMARK. Sec. 20: powers "may ... be delegated to international authorities." 2 June 1992: you said no to Maastricht. They asked again.

ESTONIA. Amendment Act 2003: the Constitution "applies taking account of the rights and obligations arising from the Accession Treaty." 1942: London proposed accepting "the reincorporation in the Soviet Union of the Baltic States." Washington called it a "complete repudiation." We never recognized it.

FINLAND. Sec. 94: a "transfer of competence to the European Union" significant to "Finland's sovereignty." Your seat at the Arctic table is yours, not Brussels'.

FRANCE. Art. 88-1: "States which have freely chosen to exercise some of their powers in common." 29 May 2005: 54.67 percent said no. February 2008: Lisbon, ratified without you.

GERMANY. Art. 23: "the Federation may transfer sovereign powers by a law." 2020: your Constitutional Court ruled the Union's Court "ultra vires." The Commission pursued you until Berlin bowed.

GREECE. Art. 28: "Authorities provided by the Constitution may by treaty or agreement be vested in agencies of international organizations." 5 July 2015: 61 percent said no. A week later: "consult and agree with the Institutions on all draft legislation."

HUNGARY. Art. E: competences exercised "through the institutions of the European Union." December 2022: 55 percent of three funding programmes frozen, until October 2026. December 2023: decided around you.

IRELAND. Art. 29.4.6: "No provision of this Constitution invalidates" what membership "necessitated." No to Nice, 2001. No to Lisbon, 2008. Asked again, both times.

ITALY. Art. 11: "such limitations of sovereignty as may be necessary." August 2011: the ECB sent your government a secret list of demands. By November that government had fallen.

LATVIA. Art. 68: Latvia "may delegate a part of its State institution competencies to international institutions." 1967: London sold your frozen gold and paid its own claimants under a deal with Moscow.

LITHUANIA. Constitutional Act 2004: Lithuania "shall share with or confer on the European Union the competences of its state institutions." Your nuclear plant, closed as the price of entry. Your gold, sold by London too.

LUXEMBOURG. Art. 5: the exercise of state powers "peut etre transfere a l'Union europeenne." The Commission ordered you to claw EUR 250 million in tax back from Amazon. Its own Court threw the order out.

MALTA. Art. 65: laws in conformity with "the treaty of accession to the European Union." 2025: the Union's Court struck down your own rules on who may be Maltese.

NETHERLANDS. Art. 92: "Legislative, executive and judicial powers may be conferred on international institutions." No in 2005, 61.5 percent. No in 2016. Ratified anyway.

POLAND. Art. 90: Poland "may ... delegate to an international organization or international institution the competence of organs of State authority." 2017: a rule-of-law procedure. 2021: a fine of a million euros a day.

PORTUGAL. Art. 8: the Union's treaties and norms "are applicable in Portuguese internal law in accordance with Union law." 1890: London's ultimatum, and you yielded. 2011: the troika's terms.

ROMANIA. Art. 148: the Union's founding treaties "shall take precedence over the opposite provisions of the national laws." Found ready for Schengen in 2011. Let in by land in 2025.

SLOVAKIA. Art. 7: the Union's acts "shall have precedence over laws of the Slovak Republic." 2015: outvoted on relocation. 2017: your challenge dismissed.

SLOVENIA. Art. 3a: Slovenia "may transfer the exercise of part of its sovereign rights to international organisations." 1915: London and Paris promised your land to Italy in secret.

SPAIN. Art. 93: powers "derived from the Constitution shall be vested in an international organisation or institution." Gibraltar, ceded at Utrecht "for ever." Your banks, rescued on conditions, 2012.

SWEDEN. Ch. 10, Sec. 6: "the Riksdag may transfer decision-making authority." 2003: you said no to the euro. Brussels still says you must adopt it.

VI. TO CANADA

CETA has applied to you since 2017. Nine Union states have never ratified it. At Dieppe in 1942, a raid proposed by England's Mountbatten killed 907 of your men. In February you signed into the Union's loans. In Montreal its Council President hailed your money for its Ukraine loan, "tant qu'il le faudra": for as long as it takes. You are our neighbour, our partner in NORAD, and of this hemisphere, not theirs. Associate membership is the threshold.

VII. TO THE CONGRESS, AS ALLIES

We do not agree with your recent actions, nor your failures to act. You wrote the lock: the President "shall not suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty" without two-thirds of the Senate or an Act of Congress, and defined those words by a Vienna convention your Senate never ratified. You wrote even into our own territorial law: "Nothing in this paragraph shall be deemed to supersede any treaty or international agreement with which this paragraph conflicts." In a defense bill, you barred funds to take our forces in Europe below 76,000 until it is certified that we moved "only after appropriate consultations with all North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) allies and relevant non-NATO partners." Our indictment of you stands. But each of you swore to "support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic." If ever that oath would answer your hand, the time is now.

THE TERMS I WOULD SET
I hold no office and set no terms. Terms with an alliance or a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry, and to both I defer. Within the lock Congress set, and not a piece beyond it, these would be the terms: a full American command-and-control corrective.
I. Article 12. Call the review the Treaty has allowed since 1959. A review is none of the four words Congress locked.
II. The charter's line. No commitment under Article 4 or 5 without a consensus of all members and, for us, the Senate's consent, as the Senate wrote in 1998 and again in 2022. Wind down every non-Article 5 operation and every partnership beyond Article 6's map.
III. Command. SACEUR stays American, as since Eisenhower. Every subsidiary body yields to the military order of the nation that pays, bleeds and dies for it.
IV. No middlemen. Any channel we do not directly control, our military does not distribute, or the charter does not approve, closes. Our logistics run through our own commands.
V. Non-members. The Wiesbaden command, the trust fund and the purchase list come under our direct control or close.
VI. Money. Our share of the common budgets never rises, as the Senate conditioned. Article 3 is a duty now, not a target for 2035.
VII. Rules. American forces fight under American rules of engagement. A coalition's rules bind them only if our Secretary of War authorizes it. He should not.
VIII. Status of forces. Reopen Article VII. The first right over our people is ours. The Senate said in 1953 that Article VII set no precedent. Honor it.
IX. The Court. Every nation hosting our forces commits in writing never to hand our people to the International Criminal Court.
X. Bases. Condensed and rebuilt for modern reach.
XI. The Union. No seat, no say, no claim in NATO.
XII. The hemisphere. No Union force, base or defence instrument in the Americas. The Arctic stays with the eight states that sit on it.

To Brussels: you have been told.

To the nations of Europe: read your constitutions. Then read theirs. We bled for you twice. We will not watch you signed away by committee.

The ninth. Read it with all that came before: the petition to the Holy See, for the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness"; the inquiry before the Secretaries of State; the indictments of the Congress and of the Supreme Court; the damnation of the International Criminal Court; and eight rounds: the Union, the EBRD, France, Basel, the press, Canada, the Crown, Australia.

We the People

text:
President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah has paid tribute to the late Madame Penehupifo Pohamba, describing her as a remarkable woman who dedicated her life to serving others with humility, dignity and compassion.

Delivering her tribute at the Memorial Service held at the Pohamba residence in Okanghudi Village, Ohangwena Region, President Nandi-Ndaitwah highlighted the late Madame Pohamba’s lifelong commitment to service and her contributions as First Lady, which earned her recognition at regional, continental and international levels.

The President recalled that, nationally, the late Madame Pohamba was honoured with the Most Brilliant Order of the Sun in 2014.

She further noted that Madame Pohamba was recognised as an Ambassador of Peace by the Universal Peace Federation in Washington, D.C., received the Global Inspirational Leadership Award in Dubai and served as Chairperson of the Forum of African First Ladies for the Fight Against Breast, Cervical and Prostate Cancers in Africa.

President Nandi-Ndaitwah emphasised the importance of continued attention to these forms of cancer in Namibia. Against this background, she observed that the memorial service was not only an occasion to reflect on the offices and positions held by the late Madame Pohamba, but also to honour the remarkable woman behind them: a freedom fighter, a healer, a mother and a servant leader who made an enduring contribution to the nation.

The President described the late Madame Pohamba’s commitment to service as a calling, an act of love and a profound expression of her humanity. 

President Nandi-Ndaitwah recalled that, like many of her generation, Comrade Penehupifo answered the call to join the liberation struggle for Namibia’s independence.

“Having received medical and military training in exile, Madame Pohamba put her knowledge and skills to use in providing primary healthcare to Namibians in refugee camps, making a meaningful contribution to the struggle for freedom,” the President stated. 

Reflecting on her role in the liberation struggle, President Nandi-Ndaitwah underscored that the late Madame Pohamba fought to safeguard the lives and dignity of the Namibian people. She noted that her hands were trained both to defend freedom and to heal the wounded.

The President further highlighted that, even under the difficult conditions of exile, Madame Pohamba demonstrated that the liberation struggle was fought on many fronts, and that every life saved was an act of resistance.

Turning to her contributions as First Lady, President Nandi-Ndaitwah recalled that the late Madame Pohamba dedicated herself to advancing awareness and interventions in tuberculosis, maternal healthcare and HIV/AIDS.

She also highlighted Madame Pohamba’s patronage and support for the Maternal and Child Health National Agenda and the Namibia Pharmaceutical Foundation, which assisted children requiring facial reconstruction surgery.

She stressed that Madam Pohamba’s legacy serves as a reminder that public service must ultimately be measured by the lives we touch and the burdens we help others carry.

Extending her condolences to His Excellency Dr Hifikepunye Pohamba, the bereaved children and grandchildren, President Nandi-Ndaitwah acknowledged that words may offer little comfort in the face of such a profound loss. 

On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Namibia, her family and herself, the President conveyed her deepest condolences to the Pohamba family during this difficult time.

In conclusion, President Nandi-Ndaitwah reflected that Meme Penehupifo Pohamba had completed her earthly journey, having devoted her years to serving others, her courage to the struggle for freedom, her knowledge to healing the Namibian people, and her heart to her family and nation.

The President called on mourners to honour her memory by carrying forward her enduring legacy of compassion, courage, service and love.

text:
Holding 1500 shares of a favorite tech platform at a $175 average while option premiums get completely demolished creates a very specific kind of portfolio vertigo.

When forward guidance turns ice cold and the macro backdrop offers zero cover, bagholding stops being a passive waiting game and starts feeling like an unhedged penalty. You used to be able to sell covered calls to pad the bleed, but when volatility collapses and premiums dry up, that cushion vanishes entirely.

Down in the trenches, the community is split right down the middle. Half the room is buying the dip under $100 because the app is part of their daily routine and they remember how people wrote off Meta at $90 before it ripped. The other half is convinced the platform is rotting from the inside out and that long-term AI disruption is going to eat any hope of a fundamental turnaround.

When your cost basis is miles above the current tape and the hedging tools are gone, deleting the app for a year starts looking less like a joke and more like the only position left that doesn't cost you sleep.

text:
In this new era, I believe we must continuously create more stable social ladders and avenues for upward mobility. 

Whenever productivity makes a technological leap, history shows that—if managed wisely—every major shift can unleash explosive economic growth and generate countless unimagined job opportunities, far outweighing the old jobs that fade away. 

Every industrial revolution in history has created unprecedented wealth in precisely this way. That is why it is vital to formulate forward-looking policies that align both with historical trends and the demands of this new industrial wave.

Steve Hilton's campaign offers us a pathway toward just such a blueprint. So long as new progress gathers momentum, that momentum alone is powerful enough to drive an entire era forward—a rising tide capable of carrying everyone toward success. 

In the wake of these newfound opportunities, wouldn't ordinary citizens gain vastly expanded horizons for growth? 

The prerequisite, of course, lies in electing the right leaders—those who can open doors to rare, transformative opportunities for social mobility.
