government. that means americans wake up, go to work, and spend hours of their day working for the government. money that never enters their hands goes to the federal government to fund these programs. and we have all agreed, all american citizens have agreed amongst each other, that we’re going to fund these programs to help our families, our friends, and our neighbors in need. how can we look american citizens in the eye and ask them to keep paying for these programs when for four years these programs were laid bare for pirates to rob to the tunes of hundreds of billions of dollars, to take the money out of the pockets of american citizens, to take food out of the mouths of american children, to live a life of luxury. we can’t. this system won’t survive. the only way it survives is by pursuing the vision that president trump laid out when he founded this task force and the vice president has pursued with unbelievable vigor, which is the fraud stops. money stays in the agencies so that it goes to the people we’ve agreed we are actually going to help. and when it does get out, colin and kash and the teams of prosecutors and law enforcement officers from every part of the federal government chase them to the ends of the earth and bring them to justice. if we don’t do this, if we don’t win this fight, social trust will continue to degrade in this country. trust in government will continue to degrade and these programs won’t survive. this fight is about saving the american system from the worst types of actors, fraudsters, pirates, and gangsters, and restoring america for americans. for four years, minnesota was laid bare to fraud and the federal government looked the other way. pirates and gangsters and thugs funded luxury lifestyles by taking money out of the pockets of hardworking american citizens. president trump, vice president vance, and secretary bessent have a very clear message for all of them. enough is enough. we are putting american citizens first just as the president promised in his election and just as we have tried to do every single day. with that, i’ll turn it back over to secretary bessent.”

scott bessent: “good, and i want to thank all of you. i think we can see that the results, while incomplete, have been rapid, fulsome, and in many cases the consequences severe. so i’d be happy to answer any questions.”

reporter: “thank you, mr. secretary.”

moderator: “the very important question we’ll go to is online.”

reporter: “throughout the last year or so, president trump has mentioned that there were billions and billions of dollars of fraud here. but the fraud that’s been uncovered so far is well under that figure. i think $19 billion was the total. when are we going to see that really high figures that’s been mentioned before?”

scott bessent: “as we can see, it’s accelerating every day, and whether it’s the $500,000, several million, it will continue to add up. as we heard today, the real tragedy is that these programs are being shut down. i was at a roundtable here in january, and i heard from two parents who the program for autistic children, their children needed and attended, had been shut down. so i think that as we work on this every day, that we are uncovering more, and as we heard earlier, we are getting the street level capos, and we expect over the coming weeks and months to secure arrests, verdicts, and recoveries from the kingpins.”

moderator: “thank you. the next question, we’ll go to cbs, francis.”

francis: “yep, yep. i’m curious if you were able to touch on why you all picked st. cloud as the location today. we’re aware of two raids down in the twin cities, if you can touch on that.”

scott bessent: “we were invited here. the local assistant u.s. attorney suggested that we come here. the government here is doing their best, and again, this is the center of the fraudulent activity, minneapolis-st. paul, but this is all over the entire state. the walz administration has been woefully negligent and turned a blind eye. so every citizen of minnesota is a victim, every town and city, the people are being defrauded.”

all, npr: “thank you. that was also my question. are any of these defendants specifically in st. cloud, or any of these businesses that you’re targeting? can you talk about any investigations that are specifically related to st. cloud?”

kash patel: “we’re not going to talk about ongoing investigations, but the fact that we are here should make you think that the greater region and the greater area here, that the task force is very interested in what’s going on in this area.”

reporter: “thank you. if the administration has declared war on waste and fraud, could you explain the $420 million overpayment for a prison in appleton, minnesota, when the company offered it to the state of minnesota for $75 million?”

kash patel: “yeah, i don’t know anything about that. what we are here to do is to prosecute criminal fraud, and any question like that that deflects away from it, i think is a waste of our time. thanks.”

reporter: “so yesterday, senate democrats put out a report that accused cms of targeting blue states with this task force. they pointed out some $12.4 billion in fraud in florida, significant fraud, $5 to $10 billion a year in texas. so i’m wondering if cms feels like they’re holding other states, red states, purple states, to the same standards as they’re holding minnesota.”

scott bessent: “when i speak to dr. oz, he tells me that what’s going on in his home state of florida, that there is substantial fraud going on there, many of it offshore, much of it in the medical equipment industry. so again, the democrats, having let this happen on their watch, whether it’s here or in their states, they are trying to deflect, and it’s going on everywhere, and we’re going to track them down. but i can tell you that the guardrails tend to be loosest in the democratic states.”

reporter: “this kind of goes along the same lines as maybe some of the other questions about why you came to st. cloud or minnesota, but per capita, i was wondering, because we can throw big numbers out, texas, big state, florida, big state. minnesota doesn’t have the same population. per capita, has it been that much worse here than other states? is that maybe why we’re here? can you talk a little bit about per capita, where it’s been the worst?”

scott bessent: “well, i would say that we are at ground zero for per capita, given the population of minnesota and this fraud that we’ve seen. and it’s ongoing, and the kind of egregious nature of this and the lack of oversight from the ag’s office and from the walz administration is shocking. so it is substantial. it is heartbreaking in many ways because, as we were talking about, whether it’s a program for the homeless, the one where i saw the parents for autistic children, and it is prevalent. so i would say that minnesota, unfortunately, because of the lack of oversight, likely has, as a percent of the dollars, one of the largest in the country.”

reporter: “you mentioned earlier that there was offshore accounts being redistributing money. could you give us a list of some of those countries?”

scott bessent: “well, i can’t give a list of the countries. i will tell you that there is a nexus around somalia and terrorist organizations associated there. but unfortunately, we at treasury follow the money, and we can see that many other countries are offshore laundries, and what we do at treasury is we follow the money, and we are attempting to recover it for the u.s. government, but more importantly, to break this recycling that seems to go on, that leaves minneapolis, ends up offshore, and then some of it finds its way back here.”

moderator: “and the last question will go to jenny, star tribune.”

jenny: “hi. just wondering if the fbi is planning any more search warrant executions ahead of the election, or any other activity?”

scott bessent: “i’ll leave that to the director.”

kash patel: “thanks, secretary. and the fbi will, with our partners at the department of justice, execute search warrants based on facts and the law in a timely fashion upon proper adjudication by the attorney general’s office. thank you.”

scott bessent: “okay. well, i want to thank you all for coming here today. we can see the magnitude of the problem. we can see that this task force is working on a solution. i was with vice president vance this morning. he was unable to make it today. and he and i were going through each of the departments, and i will tell you that this task force is the most fulsome cross-government agency that i have seen at my time in government. so thank you all.”

text:
How to get your clients to give you a no brainer offer so you can run successful cold-email campaigns for them:

{{firstName}},

If we increased one of your {{service_line}} field-reps conversion rate on visits by 10-15 percent in under 2 weeks, with no expenses to you, would that be worth a meeting?

-

the cost + time to realized value for the prospect is:

$0 + under 2 weeks

That's when you know you have a no-brainer cold-traffic offer.

----------

I’m going all in on cold email copy and offer building because most of what I’m seeing right now is bad. 

People are writing emails before they’ve made an offer a stranger can understand. 

The person reading it should be able to ask, “Do I have this problem?” If they do, it should be easy to reply.

Here’s how to build the whole thing for an AI SaaS selling to service companies with field sales reps.

-------

1. Make the offer with the client first.

If a SaaS or AI company hired me for outbound, most of our early work would be on the cold-traffic offer. 

I’d ask what problem the buyer already knows they have, what result they want, and what the company is willing to let a stranger try before a full rollout.

Take Rilla, which lets managers review and coach conversations from field visits. 

I’d ask them to let an interested service company put any one rep on the app for two weeks, on the house. 

The manager hears what happens on real visits and sees where to coach.

That’s what we’re taking to cold traffic: one rep, two weeks, no expense to the service company, and a way for the manager to coach from what the rep actually says.

Now we have an offer for cold-traffic:

Increase anyone of your sales reps closing % in under 2 weeks, for free.

If the product really works, then the client should be willing to run it to acquire pipeline.

-------

2. Build a list that fits the offer.

We need service companies with people who sell in the field: 

HVAC comfort advisors, plumbing salespeople, electrical reps, and similar roles. 

A company doing repairs with no field sales motion doesn’t belong just because its website says HVAC. 

The contact should be the person responsible for the reps or the business owner.

The goal would be map their entire TAM and then score it based on fit, simple.

-------

3. Scrape for just two fields the copy needs. (KEEP IT SIMPLE):

For this first test campaigns, I need {{service_lines}} and {{service_region}} from each company’s own site, scraped by an agent via harness or something like Loopster via HTTP:

{{service_lines}} = hvac, plumbing or electrical
{{service_region}} = Atlanta or Georgia

I don’t need a paragraph pretending we know how their team operates.

 I need two facts that make the offer relevant to the company receiving it.

This is with an "OR", not "AND" framework so the agent would know this that creates the variables in the CSV.

-------

4. Write 3 angles.

Angle A with variables):

{{firstName}},

If we helped one of your {{service_line}} reps in {{service_region}} increase their conversion percentage on visits by 10-15 percent, would that be worth a meeting?

We can do this in under 2 weeks, completely on the house - pick any rep and we’ll put them on the app before their next visit.

You’ll hear how they handle pushback so you know what to coach them on.

-

Angle A with parsed variables)

Jordan,

If we helped one of your hvac, plumbing or electrical reps in Atlanta or Georgia increase their conversion rate on visits by 10-15 percent, would that be worth a meeting?

We can do this in under 2 weeks, completely on the house - pick any rep and we’ll put them on the app before their next visit.

You’ll hear how they handle pushback so you know what to coach them on.

-

Angle B with variables)

{{firstName}},

If we increased one of your {{service_line}} field-reps conversion rate on visits by 10-15 percent in under 2 weeks, with no expenses to you, would that be worth a meeting?

Pick any rep and we’ll put them on our app before their next visit.

-------

5. Turn the lines into a repeatable workflow.

If the website doesn’t support one of the fields, that row goes to review. 

The agent doesn’t make up a territory or write a completely different email for every company.

I’d do this with my agent harness, OpenAI and Cloudflare Browser Run, or use Loopster’s HTTP column to call the APIs. 

That gives me the same process across a list of 5,000 companies while keeping the facts in each message tied to that company’s site.

-------

6. Test the copy.

I know the offer is good.

It's free, there's an outcome claim that can be realized in as little as two weeks, they get to have AI in their business that actually can be attributed directly to revenue which might be an angle I try later on, and overall the cost + time to value is $0 + under 2 weeks.

It's a solid cold-traffic offer, I wouldn't change it until I launch 5-10 angles at least.

It's just a matter of conveying it until we strike a nerve in the market and scale up that angle OF THE OFFER.

Most of the work here is getting the client to agree to an offer a cold prospect can understand. 

Once that’s done, the copy and the two website fields do all the heavy lifting.

Is there any way to hold the #perpetrators of #crimes against #humanity accountable?

Today, at the beginning of my International Human Rights Law class with women students inside Afghanistan, I asked how they were doing.

One student from #Badghis province, in northwestern #Afghanistan, told us: “Women have completely disappeared from our village. You hardly see any women in the city.”

Another student from Herat described how Taliban members confronted women in public despite their efforts to comply with the dress restrictions. She recounted reports of women being #detained in #containers, separated by age, threatened, and held until their families paid money who barely bring food at the table and promised they would follow the imposed dress rules.

These are not distant stories. These are the everyday experiences shared by my students.

I teach international human rights law, and one question repeatedly comes up in our discussions: Is there any way to hold them accountable?

This question is at the heart of my recent article published by IntLawGrrls, where I examine accountability through the International Criminal Court’s Afghanistan investigation and the role of universal jurisdiction when states fail to cooperate with arrest warrants.

If Taliban leaders accused of international crimes travel freely through the United States and Europe, while women inside Afghanistan face abduction, detention, and systematic persecution, what does accountability mean?

My question to every state is simple:

We have evidence. Survivors have spoken. Will you act on that evidence, or will you continue to offer political engagement and safe passage to those accused of international crimes?

Justice requires action, not statements.

Read my article 👇

Thinking about living in Midtown Sacramento? Imagine beautiful Victorian homes, tree-lined streets, sidewalk cafés, art galleries, lively nightlife, and some of Sacramento's best restaurants—all within walking or biking distance!

Midtown is one of Sacramento's most exciting places to live, combining historic architecture, creative energy, and an incredible sense of community.

Let's discover the best neighborhoods in Midtown Sacramento!

🏡 MIDTOWN HISTORIC DISTRICT

Love classic Sacramento architecture? Midtown's historic residential streets feature beautiful Victorians, Craftsman bungalows, charming apartments, and mature shade trees. It's a wonderful choice for people who appreciate character, walkability, and neighborhood cafés.

🌳 BOULEVARD PARK

One of Midtown's most beautiful residential areas! Boulevard Park is known for its grand historic homes, tree-lined streets, architectural details, and peaceful atmosphere. Residents enjoy easy access to restaurants, coffee shops, and downtown attractions.

🎨 R STREET CORRIDOR

Looking for a creative, energetic neighborhood? The R Street Corridor features converted industrial buildings, contemporary apartments, restaurants, galleries, breweries, and entertainment venues. It's especially appealing to people who enjoy an urban lifestyle.

🍽️ HANDLE DISTRICT

If you love dining out, this is your kind of neighborhood! Centered around 18th and L streets, the Handle District is packed with restaurants, cocktail bars, cafés, and nightlife. It's a lively destination for food lovers and city enthusiasts.

🌸 SUTTER DISTRICT

Located around Sutter's Fort and the surrounding Midtown streets, this area combines historic character with local restaurants, neighborhood businesses, and convenient access to parks and cultural attractions.

🎉 FUN THINGS TO DO IN MIDTOWN SACRAMENTO

🎨 Second Saturday Art Walk – Discover local galleries, art exhibitions, music, and creative businesses throughout Midtown.

🥕 Midtown Farmers Market – Spend Saturday morning shopping for fresh produce, flowers, artisan foods, and handmade goods.

🍽️ Enjoy Sacramento's Dining Scene – Try favorites like Mulvaney's B&L, The Waterboy, Zócalo, and Paragary's.

🌳 Relax at Fremont Park – A lovely neighborhood gathering place surrounded by cafés and restaurants.

🏛️ Visit Sutter's Fort State Historic Park – Discover an important piece of Sacramento's early California history.

🎭 Catch a Show at B Street Theatre at The Sofia – Enjoy live performances just outside Midtown's traditional boundaries.

🚴 Bike the Tree-Lined Streets – Midtown's compact grid makes it easy to discover cafés, boutiques, historic homes, and public art.

🍸 Experience Midtown Nightlife – From cozy wine bars to lively restaurants and cocktail lounges, there's always somewhere interesting to spend an evening.

❤️ WHY PEOPLE LOVE MIDTOWN SACRAMENTO

Midtown offers a lifestyle that's hard to beat: historic homes, vibrant culture, walkable streets, excellent restaurants, and the excitement of California's capital city.

Whether you're looking for a charming Victorian, a modern loft, or a stylish apartment, Midtown has plenty of personality!

Unfortunately E-Verify is toothless. If an unauthorized worker presents a genuine identity that belongs to someone else — stolen, borrowed, or purchased — E-Verify will confirm them as authorized.

Staffing agencies and subcontractors create a layer. In one Texas meatpacking case, a staffing agency (Archer Services) actively provided stolen identities to workers so they would pass E-Verify.

Finally, E-Verify usage is voluntary. Roughly 14% of U.S. employers participate.

California says "you can use E-Verify but only in narrow circumstances and don't use it to re-check existing workers or on applicants who haven't yet received a job offer", while Illinois says "you basically can't use it unless the federal government forces you to, and if you do, here are extra hoops."

🎺🌎✝️📖🕊 The story of Florence Chadwick is used by Pastor Vlad Savchuk in the video to illustrate the importance of Perseverance and keeping the right perspective during difficult times. 

Florence Chadwick was an accomplished long-distance swimmer, famous for being the first woman to swim the English Channel in both directions. In 1952, she took on a new challenge: attempting to swim from Catalina Island to the California coastline.

🌿 The Story:

The Challenge: While attempting the 26-mile swim, a thick, heavy fog settled over the water. 

The Struggle: Despite her incredible skill, the lack of visibility caused her to lose sight of the shoreline. Exhausted and unable to see her goal, she eventually requested to be pulled from the water. 

The Lesson: She was devastated to learn afterward that she had stopped less than a mile away from her destination. 

Pastor Vlad emphasizes that we often quit not because the task is impossible or because we lack strength, but because we lose hope when our circumstances create a "fog" that obscures our vision of the finish line. 

However, when Chadwick returned two months later, mentally prepared for the conditions, she pushed through that same fog and successfully completed the swim.🏆 

✝️📖🕊🌿 To maintain hope during tough times, Pastor Vlad Savchuk offers several principles based on his message about navigating difficult situations:

Shift Your Focus: Hope is often lost when we focus on the "fog" of our circumstances (financial struggles, health issues, or relational strain). Instead, intentionally fix your eyes on the "cloud"—God's presence, promises, and character—rather than the challenges themselves. 

Stop Complaining: Discouragement can turn into a habit of "stinking thinking." Choose to remove the complaining attitude and replace it with praise, even when the breakthrough hasn't arrived yet. 

✝️📖👑 Remember God's Track Record: Remind yourself that the God who brought you to your current situation did not bring you this far to abandon you. If He led you there, He plans to bring you through it. 

Persevere Through the Fog: Drawing from the story of swimmer Florence Chadwick, who quit because she couldn't see the shore through the fog, Pastor Vlad emphasizes that we often quit right before the finish line. Don't lose hope just because your vision of the outcome is obscured; keep moving forward. 

✝️🛡⚓️👑 Recognize Internal Development: Understand that God may be using the squeezed moments not just to change your circumstances, but to work on your character and build your Faith. 
👉 View the challenge as a time of being developed into a Person of Mature Faith . 

📲 SHARE ✝️📖🌎❤️🙏

text:
**Patterns of Resistance to Verification in California**

In 2026 the Department of Justice compiled lists of registered voters flagged as possible non-citizens and sought cooperation from states for matching against federal databases. Approximately thirty states, including California, refused full unredacted voter files and were sued; courts frequently sided with the states on privacy and federalism grounds. In California, federal authorities identified roughly 20,000 registered voters as likely non-citizens and requested that officials review the names, confirm citizenship where possible, or segregate associated mail ballots pending verification. Letters went to nearly every county. San Diego County received both earlier grand-jury subpoenas seeking registration applications, voting histories, and supporting documents for specific individuals and a later demand concerning 1,709 names. County counsel responded that the request constituted “a thinly veiled voter purge,” that the Registrar was legally prohibited from releasing non-public identifiers such as Social Security numbers or copies of identification documents, and that the office would not segregate ballots or participate in the review. Similar refusals occurred at the state level and in other counties.

County-level reviews of the lists themselves raised questions about their reliability. San Diego County’s examination of a sample found that approximately 59 percent of the names already had canceled registrations and approximately 74 percent had no recorded history of voting in the county. Los Angeles County reported comparable issues in its preliminary review, including a substantial share of U.S.-born individuals and inactive or canceled records. These spot-checks do not establish that the residual is zero, but they illustrate the high false-positive rates that have characterized similar bulk matching efforts. In other states, large initial flags of potential non-citizen registrants have typically contracted sharply upon independent review, often to a few hundred cases or fewer, with criminal convictions remaining rare. The refusal to share the data needed for rigorous local confirmation nonetheless leaves the residual volume of ineligible registrations unmeasured under current California methods.

These responses form a pattern of incomplete verification: rejection of federal matching offers, incomplete documentation under public-records requests, and litigation that delays checks until after ballots have been cast and counted. The combination of self-attestation, expanded mail and automatic registration, and structural barriers to external verification means any substantial volume of ineligible registrations would remain undetected until or after it affected outcomes. Historical data collected under different administrative conditions therefore cannot be treated as a reliable upper bound on the problem under current methods. Under §18002, the question is whether such sustained refusal to perform verification duties that fall within the registrar’s responsibilities constitutes willful neglect.

text:
Joe Flacco of the Cincinnati Bengals just offered to pay Caleb Williams fine out of his own pocket.

Here is what the fine is for.

Caleb Williams has been wearing cleats made by a company called Caddix. The NFL fined him 11,941 dollars for it after the Bears won at Atlanta in Week 6.

Not for anything he did in the game. For the logo on the side of his shoe.

NFL uniform rules let three brands appear on a player's feet. Nike, Adidas and Under Armour. Those are the three with league partnerships. Anything else has to be taped over.

Caddix was founded in 2015. The thing it sells is a stud design meant to cut down the rotational stress that shredded knees and ankles take every time a man plants his foot and turns.

Williams says he had been trying to get out of Nike and into these for about a year.

"They're smart cleats, they're science cleats, and they've been working for me."

He says he is focused on his health. He says they have helped his joints. He estimates about 40 NFL players already wear the brand.

And here is the part that changes how this reads. Williams has no contract with Caddix. Nobody is paying him to wear them. He is eating an 11,941 dollar fine for a shoe he bought into on his own.

That is when Flacco said this.

"If Caleb gets fined again for wearing Caddix, I'll pay the fine myself."

Jack Rasmussen, who founded the company, said he would cover it too.

Be straight about who is talking. Flacco is one of four athlete advisors to Caddix and has worn the cleats for years. He was the first NFL player to put them on, back in 2024. CBS has described him as an investor in it. He is not a neutral bystander here, the company went and put a billboard up in Chicago about all this, and every bit of this is good for Caddix.

So take the sales pitch out and look at what is left.

Flacco is in his 19th NFL season. Nineteen years of getting hit, getting up, and finding out in his forties what all of it costs. A man with that many miles on him has opinions about what is under his feet, and he is willing to spend his own money backing a 24 year old on another team who reached the same conclusion.

Williams has appealed the fine. Caddix has a hearing with the league on November 10. The Bears play at Seattle on Monday and he says he is not taping anything over.

Strip out the brands and the billboard and the sentence underneath it is this.

A quarterback is being fined for wearing something he believes protects his knees.

One hundred and thirty miles off the American coast of Alaska, five hundred and nineteen people, most of them elderly passengers in thin coats, were bobbing in open lifeboats in twenty-five-foot freezing waves.

On October 4, 1980, an engine room fire crippled the luxury cruise ship Prinsendam in the Gulf of Alaska. As the ship listed heavily in forty-degree rain and fifty-knot gale winds, hundreds of senior citizens had to be lowered into pitching wooden and fiberglass boats in the dark.

It had every ingredient to become a modern Titanic. The nearest airstrip was nearly two hundred miles away, and no helicopter could carry five hundred people across the ocean to land.

Instead, the United States Coast Guard, U.S. Air Force Pararescuemen from the 71st Aerospace Rescue and Recovery Squadron, and Canadian aircrews improvised an aerial bridge in the middle of a storm.

The massive American supertanker Williamsburgh steamed to the scene and offered its small stern helipad as a floating landing platform.

When violent waves made hoisting elderly passengers from the last lifeboat almost impossible, two U.S. Air Force Pararescuemen jumped straight out of their helicopter into the freezing sea, climbed into the lifeboat, treated dying hypothermia victims, and strapped each senior into the rescue basket by hand.

Every single one of the five hundred and nineteen souls came home alive.

🚨 Amazing CCP propaganda! The German president praised "freedom of thought" at Peking University. CCP state media quietly cut it out.

On Oct 29, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, on a state visit to China, received an honorary professorship at Peking University and gave a speech there.

According to the official text published by his office, he began with Cai Yuanpei, the legendary president of Peking University a century ago, who had studied in Leipzig. Then he quoted Cai's famous motto for the university:

"Freedom of thought and embracing of diversity. Let us adhere to this spirit!"

( Cai's motto, 思想自由，兼容并包, is to Peking University roughly what "Veritas" is to Harvard. Every Beida student knows it by heart.)

In the same speech, Steinmeier also:

1. cited the Universal Declaration of Human Rights;

2. called Russia's war against Ukraine an attack on the international order, and asked China, which "has close ties with Russia," to help persuade Moscow to stop;

3. complained about state-subsidised Chinese exports flowing into Europe, tightly controlled (or no) access to China's market for European companies, and Beijing's restrictions on important raw materials.

Now look at how China News Service, the CCP's second state news agency after Xinhua, reported the same speech on Oct 30.

The headline was about trade: "win-win must never become a zero-sum game." The lead: Europe "does not want to decouple from China." They also found room for his ping-pong match on campus (with photos and video) and his trip to the Huangshan mountains.

Freedom of thought? Gone.

Human rights? Gone.

Russia and Ukraine? Gone.

The trade complaints? Gone.

(I compared his office's official text with the China News Service report. I haven't checked every Chinese outlet, so if you find a Chinese state media report that kept those lines, please share it in the comments.)

The next day, Xi Jinping briefed Steinmeier on the CCP's Fifth Plenum, the meeting that just expelled a record 33 senior figures, and, according to the CCP's own Foreign Ministry readout, offered to "carry out governance experience exchanges" with German political parties.

What experience would that be? How to make a quarter of your Central Committee disappear?

I studied at Peking University from 1984 to 1991, where I earned a Master of Science degree. In 2000, the CCP sent me to a forced labor camp simply because I practiced Falun Gong. That is what "freedom of thought" means under the CCP.

Thank you, Mr. Steinmeier, for saying it at Beida. Too bad most Chinese people will never get to read it, unless we tell them.

text:
An urgent call for sustainable waste management solutions for City of Bulawayo

The waste management system in the City of Bulawayo is in a state of serious decline and requires urgent intervention. The situation at Richmond Landfill, commonly known as Ngozi Mine, is particularly concerning, with reports of toxic emissions raising serious health and environmental concerns among residents of Cowdray Park and surrounding communities. There is an urgent need for a comprehensive and sustainable waste management strategy to address the crisis and safeguard the health and well-being of Bulawayo residents. In light of these challenges, the Bulawayo City Council should seriously consider engaging Geo Pomona Waste Management company, taking inspiration from the partnership established with the Harare City Council. Geo Pomona is an established waste management operator whose technological capabilities, operational experience and resource recovery initiatives could potentially offer Bulawayo an effective solution to its waste management challenges.

Note:

· Service delivery above everything else

It is important that the Bulawayo City Council, under the leadership of Citizens Coalition for Change (CCC) Mayor David Coltart, approaches this matter objectively and puts the interests of residents above political considerations. Waste management is a fundamental municipal responsibility that should never become a political battleground. What matters most is ensuring that residents receive reliable, efficient and consistent waste collection and disposal services, irrespective of political affiliations.

· Benefits of contracting Geo Pomona Waste Management

Engaging Geo Pomona could also present significant economic and environmental benefits for the City of Bulawayo. Through modern waste processing and resource recovery systems, the city could benefit from valuable by-products, including compost produced from organic waste, recyclable materials such as plastics and metals, and landfill gas, primarily methane, which can potentially be harnessed for energy generation. These initiatives would not only reduce the volume of waste destined for landfills but also promote a circular economy, create economic opportunities and support environmental sustainability.

· Geo Pomona is an internationally reputable company

Geo Pomona's technological capabilities and waste separation and sorting systems have attracted interest from regional and international stakeholders. Delegations from South Africa, Namibia, Malawi and Angola have visited its facility to assess its operations, with a view to exploring the potential adoption of similar waste management models in their respective countries. Furthermore, the Government of Botswana recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Geo Pomona to explore opportunities for sustainable waste management. Bulawayo should not be left behind when opportunities for modernising municipal services are available. The city deserves a waste management system that reflects its status as one of Zimbabwe's major urban centres

Sam Amadi: When intellectualism surrenders to partisanship

By Dan Nwomeh

Given his well-known status as a public intellectual, I was taken aback to read Dr. Sam Amadi's article, Peter Mbah Is Failing, and Failing Unnecessarily. It was filled with intellectual dishonesty, extreme partisanship, unsubstantiated allegations, emotionally charged and incendiary rhetoric, spurious statistical interpretations, and a disturbing disregard for research and scholarship. What purported to be objective political analysis was, in reality, an exercise in partisan rabble-rousing, emotion-stirring and pandering to his well-known political constituency. @SamAmadi is no longer the intellectual we used to know.

Consider his preposterous claim that somebody is shot dead at a political rally in Enugu every week. What a reckless and irresponsible assertion! Where are the names of the victims, dates, locations and police records? How did he arrive at this conclusion? This is a state that security experts have consistently identified as having one of the lowest crime rates in Nigeria, with independent assessments indicating a reduction of more than 80 per cent in violent crime since Mbah assumed office in 2023.Regular attacks and violent incidents occur in other states, including Imo and Abia, yet Amadi conveniently applies an entirely different standard to Enugu.

Indeed, Enugu has invested in one of Nigeria's most sophisticated security architectures, featuring thousands of AI-enabled surveillance cameras, drones, nearly 200 patrol vehicles equipped with intelligent cameras and a Command and Control Centre providing real-time monitoring. The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, recently commended the facility and urged other states to understudy it. It is rated as the most advanced such facilities in the country and an outstanding security investment in the South East. These investments do not make crime impossible, but they make a mockery of the suggestion that the state is indifferent to security. Amadi should interrogate actual security data rather than fabricating a weekly killing statistic.

His economic analysis is equally embarrassing. He repeatedly presents Enugu's impressive IGR growth as evidence that Governor Mbah is extracting more taxes from a relatively less productive economy. Has he bothered to examine the composition of that revenue? The 2025 figures, publicly available at the click of a button, show that tax revenue accounted for just ₦51.5 billion, or 12.6 per cent, of Enugu's ₦406.77 billion IGR. The remaining ₦355.2 billion, representing 87.4 per cent, came from non-tax sources, principally the recovery, revitalisation and commercial optimisation of previously moribund state-owned assets. Technology-driven revenue tracking, electronic payments and the plugging of leakages have also transformed collections. The days of indiscriminate cash collection have been replaced by traceable electronic platforms. How did Amadi arrive at the conclusion that this represents excessive taxation? He has confused revenue mobilisation with taxation and then built an indictment on that confusion. This is a disappointing failure of intellectual rigour expected of the Amadi we used to know. His pronouncement on Enugu's GDP performance is similarly unsupported. He offers no dataset, reporting period or methodology, yet speaks with such astonishing authority.

On political pluralism, nobody should excuse intimidation or violence against opposition supporters. Every incident deserves impartial investigation and prosecution where culpability is established. But allegations are not convictions, and political incidents do not automatically establish gubernatorial sponsorship. Even the Amadeo controversy must be examined in light of the management’s own account. Management explained that the booking was made by a charity organisation for a purpose different from the political gathering the organisers subsequently sought to hold. The organisation,

text:
The official BTTC Bridge is closed.

I still think it's one of the most useful things to study in the TRON ecosystem, because almost every lock-and-mint bridge you'll ever use makes the same trade-offs it did.

So here is how it actually worked, what the risks were, and what to do now.

𝐌𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐬 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭

Nothing could cross until a token was mapped.

Mapping pairs a token contract on a root chain (TRON, Ethereum or BNB Chain) with a child token contract on BTTC.

On deposit, the ChildChainManagerProxy contract minted the child token on BTTC. On withdrawal, the child token was burned.

That's why mapped assets carried suffixes showing where they came from, like AAVE_e from Ethereum or ADA_b from BNB Chain. TRX_e and TRX_b were the examples named in the shutdown notice.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐚 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐝

Using an ERC-20 as the example from the docs:

1. Approve the Predicate contract to move your tokens.

2. Call depositFor on the RootChainManager with the receiving address, the root token and the amount.

3. The tokens are locked on the root chain and a state-sync event is emitted.

4. Delivery validators pick up the event and the child token is minted on BTTC.

The docs put this at roughly 5 to 8 minutes.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐚 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐝𝐫𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐥 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐝

Coming back out was slower, and for a good reason:

1. Burn the child token on BTTC.

2. Wait until a checkpoint containing that burn transaction is committed to the root chain.

3. Call exit on the RootChainManager with a proof of the burn.

4. The Predicate releases the locked tokens.

The docs quoted around 30 minutes. A TRON-to-Ethereum move needed three transactions in total, and a Relayer could execute the final one for you through Auto Receive if the token and amount qualified.

𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

This is the part I'd want every user to understand, for any bridge.

➜ A child token is only as good as the collateral locked behind it and the contracts holding that collateral.

➜ Exits were secured by checkpoints signed by more than two-thirds of validators. DeliveryScan shows 12 online validators today, so that signer set is a trust assumption you should know about.

➜ Upgradeable contracts mean admin keys matter. In July 2026, Blockaid flagged roughly $13.3M leaving the bridge's Ethereum predicate contracts after a privileged proxy upgrade by the admin Safe. Justin Sun then confirmed this was the planned Bridge Sunset Program, and Blockaid updated its alert to say it was an internal operation, not an exploit.

The outcome was safe, but the lesson is real: whoever controls the upgrade keys controls the bridge.

➜ Contract addresses matter. Mapping one token to the wrong child contract is how people end up holding something worthless.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐈'𝐝 𝐃𝐨 𝐍𝐨𝐰

➜ Don't use any site claiming to offer BTTC Bridge services. The official app now warns about exactly this.

➜ Per BitTorrent's announcement, cross-chain moves can still be made through major exchanges such as HTX and Binance. Check which token version and network your exchange supports before sending anything.

➜ Remember the chain itself keeps running. Staking, delegation and block production were not affected.

A bridge is a product. The design lessons last longer than the product does.

text:
The regime behind the attacks is now being welcomed into the Mecca pact formed to stop them.

Pakistan’s army says there are no restrictions on the Islamic Republic joining the Mecca Joint Defense Pact, even though Iranian-backed Houthi attacks were the reason its collective-defense mechanism was activated.

According to Saudi coalition figures, the Houthis launched more than 1,100 ballistic missiles and 1,100 drones at Saudi Arabia between 2016 and October 2026. They have targeted airports, oil facilities, pipelines and civilian infrastructure while also deploying explosive boats and hundreds of naval mines.

The Islamic Republic supplied the weapons technology, components, training and operational assistance that transformed the Houthis into a regional strike force. It uses them to attack and pressure Saudi Arabia while retaining enough distance to deny responsibility.

If Iran joined the pact, would it be required to defend Saudi Arabia against the same Houthi arsenal it helped create? Of course not. The contradiction is self-defeating and exposes the pact’s strategic incoherence.

Pakistan and Turkey want Saudi financing, military cooperation and defense contracts without sacrificing their trade, energy ties or political access to Iran.

The Islamic Republic understands this balancing act and will exploit it.

It has no reason to dismantle the Houthi threat. It can temporarily reduce attacks when it needs diplomatic relief, economic concessions or protection from retaliation. It can then intensify them when negotiations stall, energy markets become vulnerable or Saudi Arabia makes decisions the regime wants to reverse.

That is the purpose of proxy warfare. The Islamic Republic can attack without formally declaring war, damage Saudi infrastructure without immediately exposing Iranian territory and then sell temporary restraint as a political concession.

Allowing Iran into the pact would reward this strategy. The regime could retain an armed proxy capable of attacking another member while gaining influence inside the institution supposedly responsible for defending that member.

Every future Houthi escalation could become another instrument of coercion. The Islamic Republic could use attacks to extract concessions, weaken Saudi security relationships and prevent any serious collective response against its proxies.

The pact would not deter proxy warfare. It would institutionalize its rewards.

Saudi Arabia is also assuming most of the financial burden. It provides deposits, oil support, investment and defense opportunities to partners unwilling to identify the Islamic Republic as the source of the threat. Iran enables the attacks and is still offered dialogue, mediation and potentially membership.

Saudi Arabia pays for the alliance while the Islamic Republic benefits from destabilizing it.

A defense pact that cannot distinguish between the attacked state and the sponsor of the attackers has no credible red line. If Iranian membership remains possible while Houthi attacks continue, the promise that an attack on one is an attack on all becomes political theater.

Unless the pact imposes real costs on the regime enabling the attacks, it will not contain the Islamic Republic. It will become another regional institution for the regime to penetrate, manipulate and neutralize from within.

text:
🍓💔 “DADDY, PLEASE DON'T BE SAD. I CAN WAIT UNTIL WE HAVE MORE MONEY.”

Seven-year-old Lily said those words in the middle of a crowded supermarket.

And her father, Daniel, felt his heart break in a way he had never experienced before.

It was an ordinary Saturday afternoon. The supermarket was busy, children were running through the aisles, and families were filling their shopping trolleys.

But Daniel wasn't thinking about the crowds.

He was standing in front of a display of fresh strawberries, calculating whether he could afford one small box.

Beside him stood his little daughter, Lily.

She was holding a bright red box of strawberries with both hands. Her eyes sparkled with excitement.

“Daddy, look! They're my favourite!”

Daniel smiled and checked the price.

Then he looked inside his shopping trolley.

Bread. Milk. Eggs. Rice. Vegetables.

The essentials.

He quietly calculated the remaining money in his account. There were still electricity bills, school expenses, car repairs, and groceries to consider.

He took a slow breath.

“I'm sorry, sweetheart. Perhaps we can get them another time.”

He expected Lily to be disappointed.

Perhaps she would ask again. Perhaps she would tell him how much she wanted them.

Instead, she slowly returned the box to the shelf.

Then she slipped her little hand into his.

“That's okay, Daddy,” she whispered.

“We can buy them when you have more money.”

Daniel looked down at her.

She continued, “I don't want you to worry about me. I can wait.”

He froze.

For a moment, the noise of the supermarket seemed to disappear.

His little girl wasn't simply accepting that she couldn't have strawberries.

She was trying to protect him.

Daniel knelt beside her.

“Sweetheart, why would you say something like that?”

Lily looked down at her shoes.

“Because sometimes you look at things and then put them back. And sometimes you sigh when you look at the bills.”

She paused.

“I know things are difficult, Daddy. I don't want you to be sad because of me.”

Those words went straight through his heart.

He gently held her hands.

“Listen to me, Lily. You are never a problem. Do you understand? You can always tell Daddy what you want. You don't have to hide your wishes or worry about grown-up problems.”

“But I don't want you to be sad.”

Daniel pulled her into his arms.

“I know, sweetheart. But looking after you is my responsibility. You don't have to look after my worries.”

She wrapped her little arms around his neck.

“I love you, Daddy.”

He closed his eyes.

“I love you more than anything in this world.”

And as he held her in the middle of that crowded supermarket, Daniel made himself a promise.

He would keep searching for a better future for his family.

But he would never allow his daughter to believe that she had to ask for less to make him happy.

Because sometimes, the most painful part of financial hardship isn't going without something you want.

It's watching the people you love begin to believe that their happiness is too expensive.

And Daniel was about to discover that changing his family's circumstances would require more than simply working harder.

It would require a different way of thinking.

👇 KEEP READING. BECAUSE WHAT HAPPENED NEXT CHANGED THE WAY THIS FATHER SAW HIS FUTURE.

🌙 THAT NIGHT, A FATHER MADE A PROMISE TO HIS FAMILY

After the children had gone to bed, Daniel sat at the kitchen table with his wife, Rachel.

The bills were spread across the table.

Electricity. Water. School expenses. Car repairs. Groceries.

Rachel rubbed her forehead.

“Daniel, I know we're doing everything we can. But I'm exhausted from worrying about money all the time.”

Daniel reached across the table and held her hand.

“I know, sweetheart. I feel the same way.”

They weren't careless with money.

They didn't spend recklessly. They didn't take expensive holidays or buy things they couldn't afford.

They simply had responsibilities that seemed to grow faster than their income.

Every payday brought temporary relief, followed by another collection of bills.

Rachel looked at him.

“Do you think things will ever get easier?”

Daniel wanted to say yes.

He wanted to promise that everything would change tomorrow.

But he couldn't make promises he wasn't certain he could keep.

He was forty-three years old. He had a job, a wife, children, and responsibilities that didn't disappear when he became tired.

He worked extra hours whenever possible. He sacrificed his own needs. He tried to make every dollar count.

Yet somehow, there never seemed to be enough breathing room.

Later that evening, after Rachel had gone to bed, Daniel opened his old laptop.

He stared at the screen for a moment before typing:

“How can I earn extra money online while keeping my full-time job?”

He discovered people offering website design, video editing, writing, social media management, online tutoring, and virtual assistance.

Some claimed they were earning thousands of dollars every month.

Others promised overnight success.

Daniel was sceptical.

He couldn't afford to gamble his family's savings on an online business. He didn't want to purchase an expensive course promising financial freedom in thirty days.

He needed something practical.

Something he could learn gradually, practise in his spare time, and test without risking the money his family depended on.

He began researching different skills.

Eventually, he settled on one idea.

Website design.

He had noticed that many small businesses had outdated websites, confusing information, or no proper online presence at all.

Perhaps he could learn how to help them.

He wrote three things in an old notebook:

Learn one useful skill.

Build something that demonstrates what I can do.

Find someone who genuinely needs that service.

Then he added a fourth:

Never risk the money my family needs to survive.

He closed the notebook.

He didn't know whether his plan would work.

But for the first time in months, he had something more than a collection of worries.

He had a direction.

💻 HIS FIRST MISTAKE ALMOST MADE HIM GIVE UP

Daniel started watching website design tutorials every evening.

After work, dinner, and family responsibilities, he would sit at his desk and practise.

He learned about website layouts, mobile-friendly designs, contact forms, navigation menus, and how businesses could make it easier for customers to find their services.

One tutorial became ten.

Ten became fifty.

His notebook filled with ideas.

He watched videos about finding customers, pricing services, and building an online business.

But there was one problem.

After several weeks, he had earned absolutely nothing.

He was learning endlessly without showing his work to anyone.

One evening, he leaned back in his chair.

“What if I'm wasting my time?”

He looked at the clock.

Another late night.

Another day closer to payday.

Another month of worrying about bills.

Then he remembered Lily standing beside that supermarket shelf.

He remembered her words.

“I can wait until you have more money.”

Daniel sat upright.

“No,” he whispered. “I need to stop waiting.”

He closed the tutorials and started creating.

He built a sample website for a fictional cleaning company.

It had a clear homepage, a list of services, contact information, customer testimonials, and a simple design that worked on mobile phones.

It wasn't perfect.

The first version looked terrible.

Some buttons didn't work. The spacing was wrong. The colours didn't match.

But instead of giving up, he corrected the mistakes.

He tested the links.

He improved the layout.

He learned how to make the website easier to navigate.

Eventually, he had something real to show someone.

It was a small achievement.

Nobody had paid him. Nobody had promised him a customer.

But he had moved from thinking about starting to actually starting.

And that taught him something important.

You can spend months preparing to begin, or you can begin learning by doing.

Daniel decided to continue learning, but he would no longer hide behind endless preparation.

He needed practical experience.

He needed feedback.

And most importantly, he needed to find out whether someone would actually pay for the service he was learning to provide.

❤️ THEN HIS DAUGHTER TAUGHT HIM A LESSON MONEY COULDN'T BUY

One Saturday afternoon, Lily appeared beside his desk holding her little pink toy teapot.

“Daddy! My café is open!”

Daniel glanced at his laptop.

“Give me five minutes, sweetheart.”

“Promise?”

“Promise.”

Five minutes became thirty.

Thirty became an hour.

Daniel was busy correcting the website he had been building.

When he finally went downstairs, the living room was quiet.

Lily was asleep on the sofa.

Her little tea party was still waiting.

Two toy cups.

Two small plates.

Two tiny chairs.

And beside his empty chair was a little biscuit.

She had saved it for him.

Daniel stood there, looking at the biscuit.

His throat tightened.

He had started learning a new skill because he wanted to give his family a better future.

But in the process, he was beginning to miss the very moments that made that future worth building.

He gently covered Lily with a blanket and kissed her forehead.

Then he returned to his desk, saved his work, and closed his laptop.

He made another promise to himself.

“I will work towards a better future. But I won't forget to be present while my children are growing up.”

Because what good is building a better life if you miss the people you're building it for?

From that evening onwards, Daniel tried to create a more realistic routine.

He dedicated specific hours to learning and finding customers.

But he also protected time for family dinners, conversations, and Lily's imaginary café.

He wasn't always perfect.

Some evenings were busy. Some plans changed.

But he began to understand something that had been missing from his original plan.

His family didn't simply need a father who worked harder.

They needed a father who listened, laughed, played, and showed up.

His goal wasn't just to earn more money.

It was to build a better life without forgetting to live it.

📩 FOUR PEOPLE SAID NO. THEN SOMEONE FINALLY LISTENED.

The following week, Daniel decided to approach small businesses.

He searched for local cleaning companies, gardening businesses, plumbers, and other service providers whose websites could genuinely benefit from improvement.

He didn't send hundreds of identical messages.

Instead, he researched each business and looked for specific things that could be improved.

Some had outdated websites.

Others had no clear contact information.

A few had websites that were difficult to use on mobile phones.

He prepared short messages explaining what he had noticed and how he might help.

His first prospect ignored him.

The second declined.

The third never replied.

The fourth already had someone managing its website.

By Friday, Daniel was discouraged.

He sat at the kitchen table, staring at his laptop.

“Maybe I'm just not good enough.”

Rachel sat beside him.

“Can I ask you something?”

“Of course.”

“Have you asked these business owners what they actually need?”

Daniel paused.

“Not really.”

Rachel smiled gently.

“You keep explaining what you want to sell. Perhaps you should start by listening.”

Her words made him think.

He had been so eager to earn money that he had forgotten something fundamental about business.

People don't buy a service simply because someone wants to sell it.

They buy when they believe that service can solve a problem they actually care about.

The following week, Daniel changed his approach.

Instead of immediately pitching his services, he started asking questions.

What was the biggest challenge with their current website?

Were customers finding the information they needed?

Did they receive enquiries through their website?

What would they like to improve?

He listened carefully.

He offered practical suggestions rather than promising overnight success.

He showed examples of his work and explained exactly what he could deliver.

Some people still said no.

But others were willing to have a conversation.

Then, one evening, his phone vibrated.

A message appeared.

“Hi Daniel. I saw your sample website. We're a small cleaning company, and we'd like to discuss getting a proper website. Are you available tomorrow?”

Daniel read the message once.

Then twice.

He stood up and walked into the kitchen.

“Rachel?”

She looked up.

“What happened?”

He handed her the phone.

She read the message and covered her mouth.

“Daniel! Someone wants to work with you!”

He laughed nervously.

“It's only a conversation.”

Rachel smiled.

“Then go and have that conversation!”

For the first time in weeks, Daniel felt a spark of possibility.

He wasn't successful yet.

He hadn't earned anything from this potential customer.

But someone had noticed his work.

And that was enough to make him prepare carefully for the meeting.

💻 HIS FIRST CUSTOMER DIDN'T MAKE HIM RICH. IT GAVE HIM SOMETHING HE HADN'T FELT IN A LONG TIME.

HOPE.

The business owner explained what the company needed.

Daniel listened, asked questions, and discussed the project.

They agreed on the work to be completed, the price, and a realistic deadline.

Then Daniel got started.

He designed the website, added the agreed information, tested it on different devices, corrected mistakes, and completed the requested revisions.

There were frustrating evenings.

There were problems he hadn't encountered before.

There were moments when he had to stop, research a solution, and try again.

But he kept going.

Eventually, the customer reviewed the finished website.

A few small adjustments were requested.

Daniel made them.

Then came the message he had been waiting for.

“Everything looks good. Thank you for your work.”

A few moments later, his phone displayed a payment notification.

PAYMENT RECEIVED.

Daniel stared at the screen.

His first paying customer.

His first completed project.

His first payment for a skill he had taught himself.

He called Rachel.

For a moment, neither of them spoke.

Then she hugged him tightly.

“I'm so proud of you.”

Daniel swallowed hard.

“I wish I'd started sooner.”

Rachel shook her head.

“You started now. That's what matters.”

That payment didn't solve every problem.

The bills were still there.

His family still needed him.

And one customer didn't guarantee another.

But something important had changed.

Daniel now had evidence that he could learn a skill, solve a real problem, and get paid for his work.

He had completed something.

He had gained experience.

He had received payment.

And he could take another step.

He didn't quit his job or spend money he couldn't afford to lose.

He continued improving his skills, looking for new opportunities, and treating each project as a chance to become better.

He wasn't chasing overnight riches.

He was building something one project at a time.

For the first time in a long while, he felt he was doing more than waiting for life to improve.

He was taking practical steps towards making it better.

🍓 THREE WEEKS AFTER THAT FIRST SUPERMARKET VISIT...

Daniel and Lily returned to the supermarket.

They walked past the bread.

Past the milk.

Past the vegetables.

Then Lily suddenly stopped.

The strawberries.

She looked at the bright red boxes and then at her father.

“Daddy?”

“Yes, sweetheart?”

“Can I ask you something?”

“Anything.”

“Can we buy strawberries today?”

She hesitated.

“But if we can't, it's okay. I don't want you to spend money if we need it for something important.”

Daniel felt that familiar ache in his chest.

He knelt in front of her.

“Lily, sweetheart, it's always okay to tell me what you want. You don't have to carry worries about money. That's for the grown-ups to manage.”

She studied his face.

“Really, Daddy?”

“Really.”

Daniel checked the price and thought about the family's budget.

This time, the strawberries fitted.

He smiled.

“Choose a box.”

Lily's eyes widened.

“The big one?”

He laughed.

“Let's not get carried away!”

She giggled and carefully selected a box.

Then she threw her little arms around his neck.

“THANK YOU, DADDY!”

Daniel hugged her tightly.

For a moment, he couldn't speak.

Because the most important thing wasn't that he could finally buy a box of strawberries.

It was that he was beginning to believe his circumstances could change.

He wasn't wealthy.

He hadn't solved every financial problem.

But he had learned something useful, completed a real project, earned his first payment, and discovered a path he could continue exploring.

Sometimes hope doesn't arrive as a miracle.

Sometimes it arrives as one small step that reminds you that your circumstances today don't necessarily define your possibilities tomorrow.

And sometimes, that hope fits inside a little red box of strawberries.

❤️ BUT THE MOMENT THAT TRULY CHANGED DANIEL HAPPENED LATER THAT EVENING.

Daniel was sitting at his laptop when Lily appeared in the doorway.

She was carrying her pink toy teapot.

“Daddy?”

He turned around.

“Is your café open again?”

She nodded excitedly.

“Are you coming this time?”

Daniel looked at his screen.

There were emails to answer, tutorials to watch, and potential customers to contact.

Then he looked at his daughter.

He saved his work and closed the laptop.

“Absolutely! What are we serving today?”

“Strawberry tea!”

He laughed.

“Does that actually exist?”

“It does in my café!”

Daniel sat on the living-room floor.

Lily poured imaginary tea and explained the rules of her business.

He was the customer.

She was the manager.

And Mr Bear had apparently been stealing all the biscuits.

For twenty minutes, Daniel forgot about invoices, deadlines, and emails.

He was simply Dad.

Later, Rachel sat beside him.

“Do you think your new business will succeed?”

Daniel thought for a moment.

“I don't know how far it will go. But I know I'm learning. I know someone paid for my work. And I know I want to keep trying without missing these moments with our children.”

Rachel smiled.

“Then you're learning two things at once.”

“What?”

“How to build a business. And how to build a life.”

Daniel looked towards Lily, who was busy serving Mr Bear another cup of imaginary tea.

And he knew his wife was right.

A better future wasn't something he wanted to reach at the expense of the present.

He wanted to build both.

Because the people he loved weren't waiting for him at the finish line.

They were here, right now.

And he didn't want to miss the journey.

🌍 SIX MONTHS LATER...

Daniel wasn't a millionaire.

He hadn't become an overnight success.

Some weeks, he found new customers.

Other weeks, enquiries were quiet.

But he had completed more projects, gained valuable experience, and received recommendations from satisfied customers.

He continued developing his skills while keeping his full-time job.

He became more confident discussing projects, understanding customer needs, and managing his time.

There were still bills to pay.

There were still difficult days.

But he was learning how to create opportunities instead of relying on hope alone.

One Sunday morning, Lily came running into the room holding a drawing.

“DADDY! LOOK WHAT I MADE!”

Daniel smiled.

“What is it, sweetheart?”

“Our business!”

The drawing showed a little shop with two windows.

Above the door, in uneven letters, she had written:

WEBSITES & STRAWBERRIES 🍓💻

Daniel burst out laughing.

“What exactly do we sell?”

“You make websites,” Lily explained patiently. “And I sell strawberries.”

“Sounds like a very successful partnership!”

She handed him a pencil.

“Now draw yourself.”

“Where should I stand?”

She pointed to an empty space beside her.

“RIGHT HERE, DADDY.”

Daniel looked at the drawing.

Then he looked at his little girl.

And suddenly, he understood something he had been struggling to learn for months.

The future he wanted to build wasn't somewhere far away.

It was sitting right beside him.

Sometimes success is paying a bill without panic.

Sometimes it's receiving your first payment for something you created.

Sometimes it's buying a box of strawberries without feeling that familiar knot in your stomach.

And sometimes, success is closing your laptop when your little girl asks you to play.

Because you can work towards a better future without forgetting to live in the present.

And no amount of money can buy back the childhood moments you missed.

💔 A MESSAGE FOR EVERY PARENT WHO IS QUIETLY STRUGGLING

Perhaps you're reading this story after a long day at work.

Perhaps you're sitting at your kitchen table, looking at bills and wondering how you're going to make everything work.

Perhaps you've worked two jobs and still find yourself calculating every purchase.

Perhaps you've watched your children ask for something small and felt that painful feeling when you couldn't say yes.

Or perhaps you're someone who wants to change your circumstances but doesn't know where to begin.

If that's you, please remember something.

Your current financial situation does not determine your worth as a parent, a partner, or a human being.

Your children don't need you to be perfect.

They need your love, your presence, your patience, and your encouragement.

And if you're looking for ways to improve your financial circumstances, remember that you don't necessarily need to change everything overnight.

You can start small.

Learn a useful skill.

Practise it.

Build something.

Find a genuine problem you can solve.

Listen to potential customers.

Improve your work.

And give yourself time.

Website design, video editing, social media management, writing, translation, online tutoring, and virtual assistance are examples of skills people can develop and potentially offer as services.

But be realistic.

Online income is never guaranteed. Building a business takes patience, effort, and the willingness to learn from setbacks.

Avoid unrealistic promises, expensive schemes, and anyone guaranteeing that you'll become wealthy overnight.

You don't need to risk your family's savings to explore a new opportunity.

One sensible step can be more valuable than a thousand empty promises.

And never forget the reason you're working so hard.

Your family deserves a better future.

But they also deserve to enjoy having you in their lives today.

💬 NOW, I WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU.

Please don't just read this story and scroll away.

Let's have a genuine conversation.

Somewhere out there, a parent is worrying about bills tonight.

Someone is working long hours and still struggling to make ends meet.

Someone is trying to find an extra source of income.

📍Staying with Coach Prime at Colorado is the stronger long-term move if Juju Lewis can unlock his high-end potential; the MAC (Eastern Michigan first, then Western or Central) is the better play if he plateaus and mainly needs immediate volume in a more even talent pool.**

⚪️⚪️ Case for staying with Coach Prime (if the potential is real and can still be realized)

Lewis arrived as a five-star, high-upside prospect who reclassified and enrolled early, with the arm talent, athletic traits, and winner pedigree that made him the centerpiece of Colorado’s post-Shedeur plans. Coach Prime’s environment offers unique advantages for a player who still has upside to climb:

- ⚫️Elite coaching pedigree and pro-style exposure**: The staff has included Hall of Famers and NFL-experienced coaches. Lewis previously highlighted the pro-style approach and the value of learning from people who have been there. Newer schemes (including Brennan Marion’s “Go-Go” elements) have been described as giving structure, a run game, and clearer development paths after earlier revolving-door seasons.
- **High ceiling and development resources**: At a Power conference program with strong NIL/branding visibility under Sanders, the physical development (strength, nutrition), competitive practice environment against better athletes, and national exposure are higher. If Lewis can refine decision-making, consistency under pressure, and leadership—areas Sanders has repeatedly emphasized as “on him”—the jump from solid college starter to higher draft consideration is more realistic here than in the MAC.
⚪️Still early in the process⚪️: He is young (sophomore eligibility window), has shown flashes (efficient stretches, big-yardage games against lesser competition), and the program has publicly invested in him as a long-term piece. Staying keeps him in a system built around developing the exact traits that made him a top recruit, rather than restarting elsewhere. If the arm talent and athleticism translate with better processing and fewer negative plays, Boulder remains the higher-reward path.

This is not a dismissal of the current struggles (benching, limited recent snaps, questions about engagement). It simply prioritizes the ceiling: if the potential is still there to be figured out, the resources and stage at Colorado give the best chance to maximize it.

⚫️Case for Eastern Michigan (or Western/Central Michigan) if the upside does not materialize soon

If Lewis is closer to a solid-but-not-elite Power conference QB who needs immediate reps, confidence, and production rather than continued development battles, the Mid-American Conference is a logical landing spot—particularly programs running spread-style offenses in a league where talent levels are relatively even and no single school dominates with overwhelming recruiting advantages year after year.

- ⚫️Eastern Michigan as the top option among the three**: The Eagles run a spread offense (multiple receivers, tempo elements, quarterback involvement in the run game historically). In a conference where roster talent composites are clustered and depth is more comparable across teams, a transfer with Lewis’s physical tools and prior high-level exposure can step in and produce volume right away without needing to “earn” every snap against superior depth charts. Immediate starting opportunity, simplified reads in spread concepts, and the chance to put up counting stats against MAC defenses create a clearer path to film and confidence. Eastern has shown it can feature productive passers and skill players in that style of attack.
- ⚪️Western Michigan or Central Michigan as strong alternatives**: Both also operate in the same parity environment. Western has shown recent success and continuity in parts of the roster; Central has run spread/option-influenced schemes that get the ball out and involve the QB. Either would likely offer a quicker path to the field than competing further at Colorado.

text:
Great Games. Great Moments. On America’s Sports Network, NBC.

NBC Sports has an opportunity to create a unified storytelling identity across all its sports properties by borrowing from the cinematic, emotional approach that has made the Olympics so compelling. The Olympics do more than showcase competition; they tell stories about athletes, families, rivalries, sacrifice, perseverance, and the pursuit of greatness. NBC can bring that same approach to every sport it covers.

The idea is to make every event feel like more than a game, match, race, or tournament. Sunday Night Football becomes a story about tradition, pressure, and the pursuit of a championship. The Premier League becomes a drama shaped by history, passion, and fierce rivalries. NASCAR becomes a story of speed, courage, and split-second decisions. The PGA TOUR becomes a showcase of the moments when one shot can change everything. Notre Dame football and Big Ten football can celebrate tradition, pride, and the pageantry of college Saturdays. The Kentucky Derby and Tour de France can highlight the history, endurance, and human drama behind iconic competitions.

The same philosophy applies to professional sports. The NBA and WNBA offer stories of individual greatness, team chemistry, and the growth of the game. Major League Baseball provides generations of history, unforgettable rivalries, and moments that define seasons and careers. Every sport has its own characters, traditions, stakes, and defining moments waiting to be told.

The creative approach should feel like a sports movie: cinematic photography, dramatic music, compelling narration, intimate athlete profiles, historical footage, emotional interviews, and powerful moments of triumph and heartbreak. Rather than simply advertising the next event, NBC should make viewers feel connected to the people and stories behind it.

All of these individual campaigns would lead back to one overarching identity:

“Great games, great moments on America’s Sports Network, NBC.”

It is a promise that wherever great competition happens, NBC will bring viewers closer to the stories, personalities, and moments that make sports unforgettable. The Olympics demonstrate the power of this approach. NBC Sports can make it part of its identity year-round.
