text:
A wolf has chosen to trust a human, and that sentence should bother you more than it charms you.

Not "put up with." Not "learned to tolerate." Trust. The kind that has to be earned from an animal whose entire species history is one long argument against it. Wolves did not survive for hundreds of thousands of years by giving people the benefit of the doubt. They survived by reading us correctly and staying out of reach.

The clip is seventeen seconds long. I have been thinking about it for much longer than that, and I want to explain why without spoiling a second of it.

Because the real story is not what happens in those seventeen seconds. The real story is everything that had to be true before they could exist.

Start with what a wolf actually is, because most of us carry around the wrong picture. The wolf in our heads was built by stories. It is the shape waiting at the edge of the village, the thing in the dark part of the fairy tale, the villain in a hundred bedtime warnings. Norse myth gave us Fenrir, a wolf so dangerous the gods bound him with a ribbon forged from impossible things. Medieval Europe gave us the werewolf, the idea that the monster could wear a human face and walk into town. Our nursery stories gave us a creature whose whole job was to eat somebody's grandmother and then lie about it.

And yet the same culture that feared the wolf also put one at the foundation of Rome. Romulus and Remus, the legend says, were saved by a she-wolf who nursed them. We have never been able to decide whether the wolf is our nightmare or our nurse. Maybe that confusion is the most honest thing we have ever said about it.

Here is what the stories get wrong about the real animal. A wolf pack is not a gang. It is a family: usually a breeding pair and their offspring from the past few years, with the older young staying to help raise the next litter. People who spend their careers watching wild wolves describe play, grooming, shared parenting, and behavior around the loss of a pack member that is hard to read as anything but grief. The famous "alpha wolf," the ruthless boss who fights his way to the top, came largely from watching unrelated captive wolves forced to live together. The biologist L. David Mech, whose 1970 book helped spread the idea, has spent more than twenty years trying to retire it.

So when a wolf bonds with someone, it is not breaking its nature. It is using the most sophisticated thing it has: the capacity to love a very small number of individuals with total commitment, and to treat everyone else as a risk to be managed. The question that keeps pulling at me is simple. Which category does a human fall into, and who gets moved from one to the other?

Wolves also talk, and almost none of it is in words we would recognize. A howl can carry for miles in open country, and it is not a cry of loneliness the way films use it. It is a way of keeping a scattered family in touch, a voice that says here I am, where are you. Beyond sound, the real conversation happens in the body: the angle of the ears, the carriage of the tail, how high or low the head sits, whether the gaze lands or slides away. A wolf can end an argument with a posture and start a friendship with a tilt of the head.

Which means that any person who gets close to a wolf is, whether they know it or not, learning a foreign language in real time. Every gesture is a sentence. Every misread signal costs something. The ones who get it right are not the bravest. They are the best listeners.

Dogs make all of this look easy, and that is the trap. We have lived with dogs so long that we assume closeness is what canines do. It isn't. In a well-known set of experiments, researchers gave dogs and wolves an impossible task: food inside a container that could not be opened. The dogs gave up on the puzzle almost immediately and turned to look at the nearest person, as if to say, you, help me. The wolves, even ones hand-raised by people from infancy, mostly kept working at the problem alone. They did not look back.

Think about what that means. A dog leaning on a human is a design feature, shaped over thousands of years of living beside us. A wolf doing anything remotely like it is not following a built-in program. It is making an individual choice, against the grain of what its species tends to do. That is why a dog's affection is lovely and a wolf's is something else entirely. One is a gift we engineered. The other cannot be engineered at all.

There is a second translation problem, and it is hidden in the way we use our eyes. Among humans, a steady look is warmth, honesty, attention. Among many wild canids, a hard, direct stare can read as a challenge. So a person who wants to show affection by looking into a wolf's eyes may be saying something very different from what they mean. People who work around wolves learn to soften their gaze, look away, turn their body slightly, make themselves less of an event.

I find that fascinating, because it suggests that real closeness between species is not about the animal learning to be more like us. It is about us learning, painfully and in detail, to be legible to them. The burden of translation falls mostly on the human. Which is exactly why so few people ever pull it off.

People who raise wolf pups describe another constraint: the window is short. Very young animals pass through an early period when the world is still being sorted into familiar and frightening, and what a pup meets during those weeks can shape its whole relationship with humans. Miss that window, and the same animal may never relax around people no matter how much patience follows. Hit it, and the bond can be extraordinary, but it also becomes a responsibility that lasts as long as the animal lives.

So there is a strange arithmetic to a friendship like this. The trust may be built on years of care, but it may also rest on a few critical weeks that nobody gets to repeat. I don't know which story belongs to the wolf you are about to meet. I know that either one would mean someone showed up when it counted, and kept showing up after.

Add one more fact to the pile: wolves are not just wary, they are brilliant in a particular way. They live and hunt in coordinated groups, remember places and individuals across long stretches of time, and in some cooperation experiments wolves have outperformed dogs at working together on a shared task. Their intelligence is aimed at one another and at the problem in front of them, not at pleasing us.

An animal like that does not bond by accident. It collects data. It keeps score, not out of malice, but because remembering who was safe is how a family survives a winter. If a wolf like this has decided on someone, it did so after a long study, with an excellent memory and no incentive to be polite.

I should be honest about what I do not know. I do not know the history behind this particular bond. I don't know how many seasons it took, what the first day looked like, or whether anyone involved believed it would ever work. I know only what a camera can hold in seventeen seconds, and the camera cannot hold the only part that matters: the thousand quiet, unremarkable, unfilmed days underneath it.

That is what makes this worth your time. You are looking at the surface of something very deep, and the surface alone is already hard to explain.

Now add the scale. People who have never stood near a wolf tend to picture something like a large dog. It is not. A big male gray wolf can weigh well over a hundred pounds in parts of the world, with long legs built to cover enormous distances and jaws built to hold animals many times its own size. It is a machine optimized for one thing, and that thing is not cuddling.

This is where the whole emotional weight sits. Gentleness only means something in proportion to capacity. A harmless animal being gentle is a pleasant fact. A powerful animal choosing gentleness is a decision, and decisions can be made differently the next day. Everything you feel when you watch a creature like this stay calm near a person comes from knowing how easily it could have gone another way.

Every animal guards its head and neck. That is where the eyes, the ears, the nose and the airway live, everything it needs to stay alive. A predator allows contact there only from those it is certain of. Wolves also have a rich vocabulary of closeness that they use inside the family: leaning, nuzzling, muzzle contact, quiet greeting rituals between pack mates who have known each other for years. That vocabulary is not handed out. It is reserved.

When I think about what the clip represents, that is the part that makes my chest tighten. Not that an animal tolerates a person. Anyone can tolerate. It is that an animal may have extended to a human something its species normally keeps for its own.

Then there is the nose. A wolf's sense of smell is better than ours by orders of magnitude, tens of thousands of times more sensitive for some odors. A wolf standing near you is receiving a running report on you that you never agreed to send: whether you are tense, whether you are afraid, whether you are lying to yourself about being calm. Most of the signals we use to manage each other, a smile, a tone, a confident posture, mean nothing to a creature that reads the chemistry underneath.

So you cannot fake your way into a wolf's trust. There is no performance that works. Whatever is happening between a wolf and a person who is truly at ease around it has to be real on both sides, because the animal has direct access to evidence we spend our whole lives hiding from each other.

One more distinction matters, and it is the one people miss. A tame animal is not the same as a trusting one. Tameness is general: an animal that accepts anyone who walks in. What makes a bond like this remarkable is selectivity. A bond aimed at a single individual, not handed out to the room.

That selectivity is the entire value of it. If a wolf were comfortable with everyone, its comfort with you would mean nothing. It is precisely because wolves are exacting that being chosen counts. The same is true of people, if we are honest. The friendships that change us are not the ones offered to anybody. They are the ones that had to pass a test we never saw.

Go back far enough and this is an old story. Dogs are descended from ancient wolves, and the split happened somewhere between about fifteen and forty thousand years ago, depending on which study you trust. The popular version goes like this: some wolves were slightly less afraid of people, slightly more willing to hang around the edge of a camp, and that tiny difference in nerve paid off in food. Over generations, a small tolerance became a temperament, and the temperament became a species.

Which means every dog on earth descends from a wolf who took a chance on us. Somewhere very long ago, an individual animal had to decide that being near a human was worth the danger. That decision, repeated, built the most successful partnership in the history of two species. What strikes me is that the original moment never really ended. It just happens one animal at a time, quietly, wherever someone is patient enough to deserve it.

And we have not always deserved it. This is the part of the history that rarely makes it into the cute version. For centuries we hunted wolves with bounties, poison and organized extermination campaigns. Britain lost its wolves long ago. In the United States, wolves were driven out of nearly all of the lower forty-eight states by the middle of the twentieth century, and the people doing it were not villains in their own minds. They were protecting livestock, protecting families, protecting a way of life. Fear was not only a feeling. It was public policy, with funding.

So the animal in this video belongs to a species we tried hard to erase. Sit with that for a moment. Whatever you see in those seventeen seconds is happening between us and a survivor of our own campaign. If trust can exist there, then the usual rules about who forgives whom do not apply.

The strangest part is how badly our fear is calibrated. In North America, the number of documented fatal wolf attacks on people across a century is very small, far smaller than the number of people killed by dogs in a single bad year, and smaller still than the toll from something as ordinary as hitting a deer with a car. The animal we built our worst myths around has been, statistically, one of the least dangerous large predators to live near.

None of that means a wolf in a human's life is safe. A wild wolf avoiding people and a captive one that has lost its distance are very different situations, and the odds from one do not carry over to the other. But it does mean the fear we inherited was never really about the numbers. It was about the symbol. And symbols are exactly the thing a quiet moment can unseat.

The twist is that we later found out how much the wolf had been holding up. When wolves were brought back to Yellowstone in the mid-1990s, a few dozen animals released over two winters, ecologists started tracking what changed. How far the effects went is still argued over, and good scientists disagree about the details. But nobody serious disputes the larger lesson: the thing we feared was doing work we never noticed until it was gone.

That is a pattern worth paying attention to. The creature we treated as the enemy turned out to be part of the structure. I think about that every time someone tells me an animal is just a threat, just a nuisance, just a symbol. The world is rarely as simple as the story we tell about whatever scares us.

Some wolves also walk away from everything they know. Young wolves often leave the family they were born into in search of a mate and a territory of their own, sometimes crossing a distance that is hard to wrap your head around. One famous male known as OR-7 left his pack in Oregon in 2011 and wandered more than a thousand miles, becoming the first wild wolf in California in nearly a century. He was not looking for us. He was looking for a place that felt like home.

I mention it because it captures the default setting of the species: independence, distance, a life measured in miles. Against that background, a wolf that stays put beside one specific person is not following the species' script. It is writing a very rare footnote to it.

I need to say something plainly, because this kind of clip can send people in the wrong direction. A wolf is not a dog, and it is not a pet. Wolves do not do well in living rooms, they are not predictable the way domestic animals are, and a wolf bonded with one person is not a wolf that is safe around everyone else. Most stories of people getting hurt begin with someone who watched a clip like this and decided the animal was basically a big, wild puppy.

If this makes you want a wolf, I would ask you to sit with that feeling until it passes. The people who live closest to wolves tend to be the ones who talk about taming them the least. They speak in terms of respect, boundaries, distance, and a permanent awareness that the relationship is a privilege and not a possession. If anything, that humility is the most useful thing in the story.

Because trust like this is not built through grand gestures. It is built through boredom. Through doing the same careful things every day: moving slowly, never forcing contact, being predictable, letting the animal decide when and how close, and accepting a no without taking it personally. Months of apparently nothing. A wolf will not be hurried into belief. It wants evidence, and evidence only comes with time.

Notice how small the true ingredients are. A person standing still instead of stepping forward. A hand kept low. A voice held even on the days it would have been easier to raise it. Not one of those choices would make a headline, and not one is dramatic. But stack ten thousand of them and you get a creature that chooses your company. That is the arithmetic of trust: tiny, almost invisible actions, multiplied by time, producing something that looks like a miracle from the outside.

We underestimate this in every part of life. We expect big acts to carry big outcomes, and we overlook how often the biggest outcomes are made of restraint.

Most of what we call relationships do not survive that standard. We want results quickly. We expect warmth on a schedule. We get impatient when someone does not open up on the timeline we have in mind. The wolf runs the opposite policy, and it works better than almost anything we do.

There is also an inner requirement that nobody sees. If a wolf can read the chemistry of your fear, then being calm cannot be an act. It has to be a condition. The person has to do the unglamorous internal work first: learning the animal well enough that the fear drops away because it has been replaced by knowledge, not because it has been hidden. Courage in the movie sense, the swagger, the bravado, would be useless here. It would register as exactly what it is, a performance of calm sitting on top of alarm.

Real calm around a dangerous animal is earned the same way trust is: through repetition, attention, and the humility to be wrong occasionally without being reckless about it. The people who make this look effortless have usually spent more time being careful than anyone watching could imagine.

There is something quietly uncomfortable in watching it. We talk about trusting people as if it were a decision, something you simply choose. But trust looks much more like an accumulation: a long stack of small moments where someone could have done the wrong thing and didn't. Seeing it between a person and a creature with every reason to stay guarded makes you notice how rarely we invest at that depth in each other.

Now, a caution about the word "love." I will not tell you what this wolf is feeling, and neither can anyone else. When we say an animal loves us, we are using a human word for behavior we can actually observe: it approaches when it could leave, it stays when it could go, it lowers its guard when guarding is easy. Scientists have measured a hormone loop between dogs and their owners, with oxytocin rising in both when they look into each other's eyes. In the same research, hand-raised wolves did not show the same pattern.

I find that more moving, not less. If the usual biological shortcut is not what is at work, then whatever a wolf is doing when it settles in beside a human is something we do not fully understand. An honest scientist and a poet might both stand in front of it and say the same thing: we don't have a good name for this yet.

So can an apex predator be a friend? It depends what you think friendship is. If you define it as a voluntary, mutual preference that holds up over time, even when leaving is possible, then the question is not whether a wolf can feel what we feel. It is whether the pattern is there: choosing, returning, staying close by choice. By that measure, the word is not absurd. It is just carrying more weight than it normally has to.

And maybe that is the lesson in the title. We use "friend" for people we barely know. Using it for a creature that could walk away from us at any second, that owes us nothing, that has a thousand reasons for caution, forces the word to mean something again.

Then comes the ethical question, and I do not think there is a clean answer. Is it right for a person to form this kind of bond with a wolf at all? Some people argue that wolves in human care need relationships and enrichment, and that a stable bond with a trusted caretaker can be good for the animal. Others argue it blurs a line that should stay bright, that it teaches the public to see wolves as companions rather than as wild animals, and that it does not help the species survive in the places it still lives.

I can make a good case for both sides, and I keep changing my mind depending on which argument I heard last. If you are certain, I would honestly like to know what you are certain of and why.

There is also the matter of time. Wolves in the wild often live less than a decade, and even in human care they rarely reach the lifespans of the dogs that descended from them. Anyone who gives their heart to a wolf is signing up for a short clock and an early goodbye. That makes every ordinary day count differently, and it is part of why an image of closeness between a person and a wolf can feel tender and heavy at the same time.

Whether or not it applies here, that tension runs under every story like this. The deeper the bond, the more the ending matters. And the people who understand it best are rarely the loudest ones.

Some clips teach you a fact. Some make you feel something quickly and let you move on. A small number do a rarer thing: they make you quietly revise a belief you did not know you were holding. The belief, in this case, is that fear and tenderness are opposites. That something dangerous cannot also be safe. That a creature this powerful must always be a threat to someone.

Maybe the truth is more complicated. Maybe the most trustworthy presence is the one that could hurt you and shows, again and again, that it won't.

I think this is why a short video can stick with you for days. It is not the novelty of a wolf. It is the collapse of a category. We spend most of our lives sorting everything into safe and unsafe, tame and wild, friend and enemy, and then something shows up that refuses to be sorted. It is both. It has always been both. We just stopped looking.

There is a reason clips like this travel. Psychologist Jonathan Haidt called one emotion elevation: the warm, lifting feeling you get when you witness someone behaving with unexpected goodness. People who feel it tend to want to be better themselves, and to tell someone else. It is different from being entertained. It is closer to being reminded that something in the world is still working.

Elevation does not require a human hero. It only requires moral beauty of some kind: patience, restraint, mutual care. Nature rarely hands it to us in such a compact form. That is part of why this will get forwarded to the one friend you know will understand it, and also why the comment section will fill with people trying to name the feeling and failing.

I can already predict the replies. One group will say it is the most beautiful thing they have seen all week. Another will worry, loudly, about safety and the ethics of keeping wolves. A third will lecture everyone about the difference between wolves and dogs. All three are right about something, and all three are missing something the others have.

The wonder without the caution turns people into fools. The caution without the wonder turns them into cynics. The knowledge without either turns into a lecture nobody wanted. The interesting place is the overlap, the place where you can admire a bond and still insist the animal remains wild, where you can be moved and still be clear-eyed.

There is a quieter question underneath all of this, and it has little to do with wolves. If a species we hunted, poisoned and wrote into our nightmares can still reach toward one of us, what does that say about how quickly we write people off? We decide who is dangerous before we know anything about them. We let a reputation do the work of an introduction. And then we are surprised when the world feels smaller and colder than it should.

An animal does not care what the old stories say about you. It only weighs what you do in front of it today. I am not saying that makes the past irrelevant. I am saying it is a harder and fairer standard than the one we apply to each other.

So here is what I am asking, and I mean it as a real question and not a trick. When you imagine an animal like this deciding to trust someone, what do you think that person did to deserve it? Not what they said. Not what they posted. What did they actually do, day after day, when nobody was watching and nothing was being gained?

I have a guess. I would rather hear yours before I share it.

One last thing about what separates a bond from a transaction. Food, commands and rewards can produce closeness quickly, and plenty of animals will stand near anyone holding something they want. Proximity is cheap. What cannot be bought is an animal that stays when nothing is on offer. If that is what you are looking at here, it may not be love as we define it, but it is the nearest thing nature has to an unconditional vote, and it deserves a careful look. Look for the stillness, not the spectacle, because that's where answers live.

I'll leave you with the numbers once more. Seventeen seconds. One species we nearly erased. One person who, whatever it took, paid the price that trust costs. And one animal that, as far as anyone can tell, made up its own mind.

Watch it once for the animal. Then watch it again for the patience you cannot see.

text: A thought experiment: Many people equate freedom of religion -- state laws protecting people's right to live according to their faith within limits -- as an end in itself. It isn't. Freedom of religion provides space for people to actively make a positive case, through word and deed, free of violence (enforced by the state's sword), for the truth of their religion. I am very happy to live in a society where I am free to tell my atheist/Muslim/Jewish/etc. neighbour, why Christianity is the most plausible framework for understanding life, and for living well and for them to make the case (again, in word and deed, peacefully) to me. This necessarily means seeing common ground in some spaces, but serious differences in others -- indeed, freedom of religion from someone who has a robust vision of the good life entails the freedom to say that other religions are false or even harmful. Liberalism extends this to say that there really is no plausible, or even better or worse, answer to what constitutes a good life; a robust pluralism emerging from, say, a religious tradition doesn't have that problem. Part of what troubles me about, for instance, Quebec's desire to ban kids from wearing religious garb is that it changes the nature of a school. Schools are supposed to be communities acting in loco parentis where teachers and students search for truth and for wisdom and acquire the knowledge we have gained over time. They have a civic cohesion function, yes, but that is not their primary goal. They should, necessarily, include some chance to debate the metanarratives offered by a variety of traditions, including religion. And, it seems to me, that the goal of seeking wisdom and truth is cut off at the knees when kids are not able to bring their traditions to bear on that debate. It seems to me that the Quebec move to ban religious garb in the name of uniformity of community is a bit of a black mirror of liberalism. It doesn't outright say that hijabs etc. are bad. It just ducks the actual questions ("are hijabs good, bad, neutral, on what grounds are they good or bad, where do we draw the line on requirements for, say, modesty -- burqas, niqabs?") by putting the state's goal of uniformity above the real questions. In some way, a lot of the Anglos who are opposing Quebec secularism are upset that they aren't finding any traction vis-a-vis Quebec's laws because they aren't willing to make the case for what should, or should not be allowed in schools (see the recent lunacy about various sexual fetishes in schools). Their "the good life is up to you" philosophy doesn't have a robust positive alternative in which to frame difference and create allowances for difference, or even to justify its limits in a non-arbitrary way.

text:
Religious liberty is back at the Supreme Court. On Tuesday the justices will hear Catholic preschools in Colorado that say the state shut them out of its free preschool program because of their faith.

Colorado offers every 4 year old up to 15 hours of free preschool a week, worth over $6,000 a year, Courthouse News reports. To take part, schools must agree to give every family an equal opportunity to enroll regardless of religious affiliation, sexual orientation or gender identity, according to SCOTUSblog. The Archdiocese of Denver, which oversees 34 Catholic preschools, says that rule conflicts with church teaching on marriage, and the state turned down its request for a religious exemption, the ABA Journal reports. The schools point out that Colorado lets other preschools give preference to groups such as low income families or children with disabilities.

Colorado says the Catholic schools are welcome to join as long as they follow the same rules as every other publicly funded preschool, public or private, secular or religious. Two lower courts sided with the state. Mark Rienzi, president of the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty, which represents the schools, says the state is singling them out. “Our argument in St. Mary’s is that that’s precisely what’s going on, as the state is keeping them out because of their religious exercise,” he said, according to the ABA Journal.

What’s next: arguments are Tuesday, Nov. 3, which is also Election Day, and a ruling is expected by next summer. The case builds on Carson v. Makin, the 2022 ruling that Maine could not shut religious schools out of a tuition aid program.

Parents pay the same taxes no matter where their kids go to preschool. If Colorado can make room for other schools to serve their own communities, it can make room for Catholic schools too. That is what free exercise means!

Sources: SCOTUSblog, ABA Journal, Courthouse News Service, U.S. Supreme Court docket

The same Alexander Campbel that got mogged after a lot of members of his congregation became LDS and Joseph Smith published this letter in the papers as response:

Kirtland, Ohio, September 24, 1834.
Dear brother,—

I have, of late, been perusing Mr. A[lexander] Campbell’s “Millennial Harbinger.”

I never have rejoiced to see men of corrupt hearts step forward and assume the authority and pretend to teach the ways of God—this is, and always has been a matter of grief; therefore I cannot but be thankful, that I have been instrumental in the providence of our heavenly Father in drawing forth, before the eyes of the world, the spirits by which certain ones, who profess to be “Reformers, and Restorers of ancient principles,” are actuated!

I have always had the satisfaction of seeing the truth triumph over error, and darkness give way before light, when such men were provoked to expose the corruption of their own hearts, by crying delusion, deception, and false prophets, accusing the innocent, and condemning the guiltless, and exalting themselves to the stations of gods, to lead blind-fold, men to perdition!

I have never been blessed, (if it may be called such,) with a personal acquaintance with Mr. Campbell, neither a personal interview; but the great man, not unfrequently condescends to notice an individual of as obscure birth as myself, if I am at liberty to interpret the language of his “Harbinger,” where he says, “Joe Smith! Joe Smith! imposture! imposture!”
I have noticed a strange thing! I will inform you of my meaning, though I presume you have seen the same ere this. Mr. Campbell was very lavish of his expositions of the falsity and incorrectness of the book of Mormon, some time since, but of late, since the publication of the Evening and the Morning Star, has said little or nothing, except some of his back-handed cants.
He did, to be sure, about the time the church of Christ was established in Ohio, come out with a lengthy article, in which he undertook to prove that it was incorrect and contrary to the former revelations of the Lord.

Perhaps, he is of opinion that he so completely overthrew the foundation on which it was based, that all that is now wanting to effect an utter downfall of those who have embraced its principles is, to continue to bark and howl, and cry, Joe Smith! false prophet! and ridicule every man who may be disposed to examine the evidences which God has given to the world of its truth!

I have never written Mr. Campbell, nor received a communication from him but a public notice in his paper:— If you will give this short note a place in the Star you will do me a kindness, as I take this course to inform the gentleman, that while he is breathing out scurrility he is effectually showing the honest, the motives and principles by which he is governed, and often causes men to investigate and embrace the book of Mormon, who might otherwise never have perused it. I am satisfied, therefore he should continue his scurrility; indeed, I am more than gratified, because his cry of Joe Smith! Joe Smith! false prophet! false prophet! must manifest to all men the spirit he is of, and serves to open the eyes of the people.

I wish to inform him further, that as he has, for a length of time, smitten me upon one cheek, and I have offered no resistance, I have turned the other also, to obey the commandment of our Savior;
and am content to sit awhile longer in silence and see the great work of God roll on, amid the opposition of this world in the face of every scandal and falsehood which may be invented and put in circulation.
I am your brother in the testimony of the book of Mormon,
and shall ever remain.

JOSEPH SMITH jr.

To Oliver Cowdery.

Here are the reasons SpaceX should move to Argentina.

From a physics standpoint, yes, it is highly possible and actually advantageous for SpaceX to launch rockets from Argentina.
Argentina possesses unique geographical characteristics that make it an excellent location for orbital rocket launches:

1. Close Proximity to the Equator (For Equatorial & Eastward Orbits)

The Physics: Launching closer to the equator gives rockets a natural "speed boost" from the Earth’s rotational velocity (roughly 1,600 km/h or 1,000 mph at the equator). This saves fuel and allows rockets to carry significantly heavier payloads into orbit.
Argentina's Advantage: Northern Argentina (around 22°S latitude) is closer to the equator than SpaceX’s primary launch site in Vandenberg, California (34°N), and roughly comparable to Cape Canaveral, Florida (28°N).

2. Perfect Geometry for Polar and Sun-Synchronous Orbits

The Physics: To put satellites into polar orbits (imaging satellites that scan the entire globe), rockets must launch directly north or south.
Argentina's Advantage: Southern Argentina (Patagonia, around 40°S to 50°S) is ideally positioned for southward polar launches.

3. Clear Downrange Clearances (Safety & Flight Paths)

The Physics: Rockets cannot fly over populated areas during their initial ascent due to the risk of falling debris or catastrophic failures. They require thousands of miles of open ocean or uninhabited territory in their direction of flight.
Argentina's Advantage: Argentina has an extensive eastern coastline bordering the Atlantic Ocean. A rocket launching eastward or southward from the Argentine coast would fly safely over open water for thousands of miles without risking any populated landmasses.

4. Ideal Territory for Rocket Booster Recovery

The Physics: SpaceX relies on landing its Falcon 9 and Starship boosters back on Earth—either returning to the launch site or landing on a drone ship hundreds of miles "downrange" (in the direction of the launch).
Argentina's Advantage: The vast, open waters of the South Atlantic Ocean provide the perfect trajectory and staging ground to position autonomous drone ships for Falcon 9 booster recoveries. For Starship, the wide-open, low-population plains of Patagonia could theoretically offer massive land-based recovery zones.
If you want, I can explain how much payload capacity a rocket gains by launching closer to the equator, or we can look at how Argentina's geography compares to SpaceX's current launch sites in Florida and Texas. Which would you prefer?

text:
Zack Swanwick has one of the best recruiting stories out there.

When Swanwick was able to contact college coaches after his sophomore year in high school, the Kiwi’s WhatsApp message to Florida head coach J.C. Deacon accidentally went unread. Months later, Deacon happened to come across Swanwick’s message, and he soon was flying out to New Zealand to watch Swanwick play in the NZ Super 6s.

But right before the tournament, Swanwick’s hometown of Hawke’s Bay was devastated by Cyclone Gabrielle. Swanwick’s grandparents had to be rescued from floodwaters by helicopter, and Swanwick’s golf clubs were buried in a mudslide at his home course, Napier Golf Club.

Swanwick’s father, Vinny, tried to salvage the clubs but was unable, and he and his son had to travel through a roadblock and across some unstable bridges just to get to the airport to fly out for the event.

Using borrowed clubs, Swanwick finished eighth, and Deacon left that trip by texting assistant Dudley Hart, “We got our guy.”

Swanwick was offered and committed shortly after that, and two months later won the Australian Junior Amateur.

Fast forward to now, and though Swanwick has struggled this fall, qualifying for just two of the Gators’ tournaments and failing to crack the top 50 in either of them, he remains ranked inside the top 25 of WAGR at No. 24. He’ll also enter this weekend at the Asia-Pacific Amateur in his home country in solo fourth, just four shots off the lead.

NovelMage is just a shell, though, so you still have to use LM Studio to run the LLM. So those are 2 things you have to have running for one purpose because LM Studio only provides chatbot functionality at its core.

Then there is the problem with how most LLMs handle creative writing. Most of them are retarded. They write like a Millennial Reddit user with ADHD who speeds through everything and wants to end it quickly and cannot stop using emdashes no matter how hard you try to train them to stop. After a long hasslesome struggle you may get a good story going. But you gotta repeat the same process every time because NovelMage offers no Author's Note to remind the thing.

And the reason I didn't bother describing KoboldAI is because it's even stupider than LM Studio. Every problem I mentioned in my second paragraph is amplified.

text:
An empty prison in Appleton, Minnesota, was offered to the state for $75 million in 2025. About 15 months later, the federal government paid $495.6 million for it, using taxpayer money.

Records obtained by KARE 11 Investigates show that CoreCivic, the private company that owned the Prairie Correctional Facility, offered to sell the vacant building to Minnesota for $75 million. The state turned the offer down, and then the Trump administration agreed to buy the same building from CoreCivic for $495.6 million so that Immigration and Customs Enforcement can use it.

That works out to more than six times the price the company had been asking from the state. The purchase has been described as the most expensive property deal in Minnesota history.

Minnesota Corrections Commissioner Paul Schnell said he was stunned when he learned what the federal government had paid, given the offer the state received only a little over a year earlier. In his words: "I still can't figure it out."

The sale price is not the only money involved for CoreCivic. At the Minnesota site alone, the company estimates it will earn about $75 million a year once the prison reaches full capacity.

The Appleton sale is not the only ICE purchase drawing scrutiny. In September, the Government Accountability Office, a nonpartisan federal watchdog, warned of waste in ICE's wider detention-expansion spending, including its purchase of 11 warehouses.

text:
THE GRAINS COMPLEX
For November, 2026

The grain complex wrapped up October under heavy seasonal harvest pressure following sharp downside volatility sparked by the October 9 USDA WASDE report. Market psychology shifted back to a bearish tone after the USDA delivered a major surprise by raising national yield estimates for both corn and soybeans. Rapid combine progress across the Midwest combined with expanding projected ending stocks pushed prices to multi month lows through late October.

MARKET OVERVIEW

The marketplace transitions into November with fall harvest entering its final stretch, setting the stage for the upcoming November 10 Crop Production report and winter planning.

Corn experienced heavy selling pressure following the October WASDE report. The USDA unexpectedly raised national yield to 181.2 bu/acre, boosting 2026 production to 16.034 billion bushels and expanding 2026/27 ending stocks to 1.849 billion bushels. December corn futures broke through key support levels, falling from early autumn highs to settle at $4.47 1/2 by month end.

Soybeans saw a record national yield estimate of 53.1 bu/acre, lifting overall crop production to a record 4.562 billion bushels. January futures settled at $12.34 0/0 into the end of October as harvest deliveries peaked, though robust domestic crush pace and firm vegetable oil values helped cushion overall losses compared to corn.

Wheat followed the row crop complex lower across Chicago, Kansas City, and Minneapolis. A strong U.S. dollar and cheaper foreign export competition offset localized global stock concerns, pulling Chicago December wheat down to $6.03 1/4 by month end.

FUTURES

Corn
December Corn (CZ26): $4.47 1/2

Overall Tone: Bearish to defensive short term under active harvest supply pressure and expanded carryout projections.

Corn Market Drivers
Bullish Drivers: Strong domestic ethanol grind rates, steady feed demand, and periodic flash export interest.

Bearish Drivers: October WASDE yield bump to 181.2 bu/acre, expanded ending stocks (1.849 billion bushels), and seasonal harvest hedge pressure.

Key Corn Levels
Support: $4.40–$4.45
Resistance: $4.65–$4.75

SOYBEAN REPORT
Record Yield Estimates Digest Harvest Surge

Soybean futures continue to absorb seasonal combine deliveries while market participants monitor South American planting progress and domestic processing demand.

Soybean Prices
January Soybeans (SF27): $12.34 0/0

Soybean Market Drivers
Bullish Drivers: Record domestic crush processing margins, steady soybean oil demand (Dec futures at 65.81 ¢/lb), and tight ending stocks relative to total use.

Bearish Drivers: Record projected crop of 4.562 billion bushels on a 53.1 bu/acre yield, coupled with favorable early planting rain across Brazil.

Key Soybean Levels
Support: $12.00–$12.15
Resistance: $12.50–$12.65

Soybean Watch List
Final harvest field wrap up across northern and western production zones
Weekly export sales inspections and Chinese purchasing pace
NOPA monthly crush data and vegetable oil balance sheets
South American rainfall distribution and early crop establishment in Brazil and Argentina

WHEAT REPORT
Wheat Settles Near Fall Lows
Wheat continues to trade defensively as sluggish export pace and global price competition weigh on domestic exchanges.

Wheat Prices
Chicago Dec Wheat (WZ26): $6.03 1/4
KC Dec Wheat (KWZ26): $6.43 1/2
Minneapolis Dec Wheat (MWEZ26): $6.24 1/4

Wheat Outlook: Defensive short term as export competition caps upside, though dry conditions across parts of the Southern Plains maintain an underlying weather risk.

USDA WATCH
What USDA Recently Reported

Corn Yield (October WASDE): Raised to 181.2 bu/acre.
Soybean Yield (October WASDE): Raised to a record 53.1 bu/acre.
Corn Ending Stocks: Increased to 1.849 billion bushels.

Upcoming USDA Reports to Watch
Weekly Crop Progress & Condition Updates (Mondays)
Weekly Export Sales Data (Thursdays)
November 10 WASDE & Crop Production Report
Monthly NOPA Crush Report

WEATHER CENTER

Harvest Finalizing & Winter Crop Establishment

Harvest conditions across the Midwest feature open weather windows allowing rapid completion, while moisture maps across the Southern Plains and South America remain critical.

Regional Global Themes

U.S. Corn Belt: Favorable harvest weather is enabling producers to complete harvest operations ahead of average pace.

U.S. Southern Plains: Dry conditions in key Hard Red Winter wheat areas are under close observation for crop emergence.

South America: Early season rains across Central Brazil have supported rapid soybean planting progress.

BASIS & CASH MARKET SIGNALS

Harvest basis levels are beginning to stabilize as commercial elevators absorb peak harvest runs. Interior processors continue to offer steady cash bids to maintain pipeline coverage for crush and ethanol plants.

OUTSIDE MARKET INFLUENCE

Crude Oil & Energy: Energy market fluctuations continue to dictate bio energy refining margins and freight costs.
U.S. Dollar Index: Currency strength presents a headwind for U.S. export competitiveness against foreign grain suppliers.

Input Planning: Fertilizer markets remain central to producer input purchasing decisions for the 2027 crop year.

FUND MONEY TRACKER

Managed money funds expanded short positions in corn following the October WASDE report. Speculative traders will closely monitor the November 10 USDA updates and weekly export performance for signs of trend shifts.

FARMER MARKETING CORNER

Questions Producers Should Ask This Month

For Corn: With Dec corn trading near $4.47 1/2 (CZ26), are carry structure and basis appreciation sufficient to cover post harvest commercial storage costs?

For Soybeans: With Jan soybeans near $12.34 0/0 (SF27), what price targets or reownership strategies are in place for stored bushels?

For Wheat: Have you established downside risk coverage while retaining upside flexibility on winter wheat?

WHAT TO WATCH THIS WEEK

Bullish Triggers: Surprise export demand, weather anomalies in the Southern Hemisphere, or downward yield adjustments in the November WASDE.

Bearish Indicators: Weak export pace, accelerating South American planting, and continued speculative short selling.

I invite you to come with us to leave the way clear for the heavenly armies. Yes, the last battles will be intense and decisive, and detachment, courage and determination are required.

I am El Morya Khan, Choran of the First Cosmic Ray — Cobalt Blue — with which we participate intensely in this transition and cleansing of this planet, as you may know.

There is great resistance from the system in the certainty of victory over you. Look and see everything these other lords are plotting against your choices and decisions. This system creates parties, festivals and distractions to keep you distracted all the time, they use holograms reflected in the sky as if they were miracles coming from heaven, and with all these illusions surrounding your lower bodies it becomes easy to manipulate your desires and choices. Beloved ones of El Morya, stay vigil all the time because you need to decipher all the enigmas of life and death, of time that does not exist, of the past and the future — internal states that occupy your minds all the time — not allowing you to discover why you don't remember where you came from, why you are here and where you are going. But I repeat: This cycle has come to an end and there is no more time to waste.

The majority have already made their choices, and at the right time they will be transferred to the places determined by their choices without discernment, without their own will, without research and without understanding the true reason for finding themselves in the Red Sea with no chance of evolution, as their boats have their hulls destroyed, with a chance of sinking. And the interesting thing is that you do not notice all the signs that the system itself is giving all the time and defend the system and its religious and political leaders even as you see destruction coming closer and closer to your homes and your bodies. React, O beloved ones.

What will you celebrate this year-end? Is this what the Higher Self desires? I say and repeat: If you do not wake up definitively and understand the entire process of purification, releasing all knots, detaching from everything, from all things and people — I say: from everything — and with determination you remain with clean and empty hands, with nothing in your pockets, nothing in your hands or feet, without a path to earthly and material illusions, aware that the majority, like cattle, are heading towards slaughter without mercy, and looking and wanting to see, exchanging the treasure of the Earth that none value it has for the New Life, and welcoming the true treasure that is the expansion of your consciousness, I say that you will remain in prison until you pay everything you owe in the Divine Accounting. And this is written.

We suggest that before night falls, while you can still see the path, walk without looking back, become aware of the present moment, look around yourselves and evaluate the entire situation of humanity that dresses in white to hide the darkness of their souls.

Christmas. What is Christmas? Can anyone explain what this represents?

We are grateful to all the last minute workers.

【今日財位】10/31 週六碰上定日——萬聖節的面具今晚最貴，獵人先蹲點，不追著跑
Today’s Wealth Spot | Oct 31 — Saturday meets a Ding day: Halloween masks cost the most tonight, so be the hunter who waits, not the one who chases

戊寅日｜冲猴｜煞在北｜定日｜司命黃道｜農曆九月廿二｜萬聖節
Wu-Yin day | Clash: Monkey | Sha: North | Ding (settling) day | Life Keeper (yellow path) | Lunar 9/22 | Halloween

週六晚上是萬聖節，街角的店把南瓜燈、面具、限定糖果全擺到門口，標價比上週高了一截。明天早上，同一個面具會被丟進半價籃。今晚追著買的人付全價，等得住的人付一半。今天建除輪到「定」，昨天把路鋪平，今天把心定下來：想要的東西先標好價錢，不急著出手。
Saturday night is Halloween. The corner shop has pumpkin lanterns, masks, and limited-edition candy stacked by the door, priced well above last week. Tomorrow morning, the same mask goes into the half-price bin. Whoever chases it tonight pays full price; whoever can wait pays half. Today’s cycle lands on Ding, “settling.” Yesterday you smoothed the road; today you settle your mind: put a price on what you want, and don’t rush to reach for it.

宜欄只有兩項：捕捉、畋獵，後面一樣跟著「餘事勿取」。畋獵是打獵，好獵人不滿山亂跑，是先找好位置、蹲著等。換到錢上，今天是做功課的日子：一檔想買的股票、一台想換的相機、一間想看的房子，查清楚、比好價，把「到這個價我才買」寫下來。值神司命走黃道，吉神有陽德、三合、五合，三合五合講的是人和，今天跟懂行的朋友聊聊行情，比自己悶頭查有用。
The OK list has just two items: catching, and hunting. Then the same tag: “nothing else.” A good hunter doesn’t run all over the hill; they find a spot and wait. In money terms, today is homework day. A stock you want, a camera you’d like to upgrade, a home you’d like to see—look it up, compare prices, and write down “I buy only at this price.” The duty god is the Life Keeper on the yellow path, and the good stars include Yang Virtue, Three Harmonies, and Five Harmonies. Those last two are about people, so talking prices over with a friend who knows the market beats digging alone today.

忌欄是開市、交易、祭祀、入宅、安葬。今天不成交：下單、付訂金、刷卡買限定款，都留到下週。彭祖兩句：「戊不受田，田主不祥」，受田是接下別人的田地，今天有人要把店面頂讓給你、把車或設備便宜轉手給你，先聽，不收。「寅不祭祀，神鬼不嘗」，今天不必特地去廟裡求財，功課做足比拜拜實在。凶煞裡有復日和九坎：復日是做過的事會重來一遍，今天衝動買一次，下次還會再犯；九坎是坑，看起來划算的組合包，多算一次單價。
The avoid list: opening for business, trading, worship, moving in, burials. No deals today: placing orders, paying deposits, swiping for limited editions—all of it waits for next week. Peng Zu has two lines. “On a Wu day, don’t accept land, or the owner meets misfortune”: accepting land means taking over someone else’s field. If someone offers to hand over their shop lease, or sell you their car or gear cheap, listen, but don’t take it. “On a Yin day, don’t make offerings; the spirits won’t taste them”: no need to go to the temple to pray for money today—solid homework beats incense. Among the bad stars are Repeat Day and Nine Pits. Repeat Day means what you do comes around again: buy on impulse today and you’ll do it again next time. Nine Pits are traps: that bundle deal that looks like a steal—work out the unit price one more time.

財神今天在北，福神也在北，喜神東南，陽貴東北，陰貴西南。北方今天財神、福神都到，偏偏煞也落在北：北邊適合坐著想、寫計畫，不適合在那頭鑽牆、動工。屬猴的今天被正沖，有人拉你「一起進場，現在不上車就來不及」，回一句「我先記下來，下週一再看」。
The Wealth God sits north today, and so does the Fortune God; the Joy God is southeast, the Yang Noble northeast, the Yin Noble southwest. Both Wealth and Fortune are in the north today, yet Sha falls there too. The north is for sitting, thinking, and writing plans, not for drilling or building. Monkey people take the day’s clash: if someone urges “get in now or you’ll miss the ride,” the answer is “I’ll note it down and look again Monday.”

補運動作：面朝北坐下，挑一樣這陣子一直想買的東西，寫下三件事：它現在的價格、你願意出的價格、你要等到哪一天。設好到價提醒，今天不下單。萬聖節的糖果、面具，等明早半價再說；省下來的差價記在同一張紙上，月底加起來，就是你等出來的錢。
Today’s move: sit facing north, pick one thing you’ve been wanting to buy, and write down three things: its price now, the price you’re willing to pay, and how long you’ll wait. Set a price alert, and place no order today. Halloween candy and masks can wait for tomorrow’s half-price bin; jot the difference you save on that same sheet, and at month’s end, the total is money your patience earned.

時辰：子丑（23–3 點）、辰巳（7–11 點）、未時（13–15 點）、戌時（19–21 點）走黃道；寅卯（3–7 點）、午時（11–13 點）、申酉（15–19 點）、亥時（21–23 點）走黑道。早上七點到十一點查資料、比價最順；中午別被萬聖節限定款吸走；下午一點到三點設到價提醒、跟朋友聊行情；傍晚三點到七點街上活動多，錢包收好、限定款別碰；晚上七點到九點把今天定下的價錢寫進記事本，九點後別熬夜盯盤。
Timing: 11 p.m.–3 a.m., 7–11 a.m., 1–3 p.m., and 7–9 p.m. run on the yellow path; 3–7 a.m., 11 a.m.–1 p.m., 3–7 p.m., and 9–11 p.m. are black-path hours. From 7 to 11, research and price comparisons go smoothest; from 11 to 1, don’t get pulled in by Halloween limited editions; from 1 to 3, set your price alerts and talk prices with a friend; from 3 to 7, the streets get busy, so keep your wallet zipped and leave the limited stuff alone; from 7 to 9, write today’s settled prices into your notebook; after 9, don’t stay up watching the market.

獵人不追著跑，蹲得住，獵物自己會走過來；價錢先定好，錢就不會被牽著走。
A hunter doesn’t chase; the one who can wait sees the prey walk right in. Set your price first, and your money won’t get led around.

text:
**No. Most gender clinics do not offer dedicated or comprehensive specialized detransition services.**[](<https://t.co/yrkQB4YEC3>)

Dedicated clinics focused on detransition are rare. Texas Children’s Hospital recently opened what has been described as the first dedicated U.S. detransition clinic (as part of a 2026 legal settlement). Cleveland Clinic also provides detransition care (including hormone management and exploration of surgical options) and has committed funding for it, but these are exceptions rather than the norm.[](<https://t.co/9tNyNeVSun>)

### Evidence of gaps
- The 2024 Cass Review (UK) identified a lack of adequate, consistent service provision for people considering detransition and recommended that NHS England create pathways. It noted that many may not wish to return to the original gender clinic. NHS England has been developing such a pathway, but specialized support has been limited, with GPs often left to manage cases without clear guidelines. A 2026 BMJ report described detransitioners as “abandoned” in this regard.[](<https://t.co/yrkQB4YEC3>)
- Patient surveys and qualitative studies (e.g., work by researchers like Kinnon MacKinnon) commonly report healthcare avoidance, clinician stigma or lack of relevant knowledge, and patients managing hormone cessation themselves or through non-specialist providers. Many never inform their original clinic of their decision.
- Rates of detransition vary by study and definition (often cited in the low single digits to around 10% in some cohorts with better follow-up), but high rates of clinic disengagement make it hard for original providers to track or support these patients systematically.

### What is typically available
Gender clinics (and general endocrinology/primary care) can often handle the basics of stopping or adjusting cross-sex hormones and monitoring health effects if a patient returns and requests it. Comprehensive, specialized support—such as coordinated psychological care, surgical revision/reconstruction options, fertility counseling, or multi-disciplinary teams experienced in detransition—is not standard in most places. There are limited formal clinical guidelines for this in many systems.[](<https://t.co/cJQlasblzl>)

In short, basic medical management is possible in some settings, but the specialized, accessible services that the Cass Review and patient reports indicate are needed are not what most gender clinics currently offer.

text:
Elizabeth Holmes became the youngest self-made woman billionaire at 30 with a $4.5 billion fortune. Walgreens opened 40 Theranos centers. in 2022 she was sentenced to 11 years in prison.

she dropped out of Stanford in 2004 after two years and started Theranos. the company raised more than $700 million from investors, Oracle founder Larry Ellison among them, and reached a valuation of more than $9 billion.

the pitch was one device. she told investors it could detect conditions like cancer from a single drop of blood and that the company offered more than 200 tests. the company was later found to be running tests on other companies' machines.

the partners signed anyway. Walgreens put in a $40 million convertible note and paid a $100 million innovation fee. Safeway agreed to a $350 million deal. Walgreens later closed its 40 centers.

Forbes had counted her fortune at $4.5 billion. later it put the number at zero. she owned about half of the company's stock, and the investors had to be repaid first.

in January 2022 a jury convicted her on four counts: one of conspiracy and three of wire fraud. she was found not guilty on the patient-related charges. in November 2022 the judge sentenced her to 11 years and 3 months, plus three years of supervised release.

she and Ramesh Balwani, her former business partner, were also ordered to pay about $452 million in restitution. nearly $398 million of it was attributed to 12 investors.

on May 30, 2023 she began serving the sentence at a minimum security women's prison camp in Texas.

a $4.5 billion fortune at 30: genius or just the right story?

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians flooding President Trump’s Instagram comments after Flávio Bolsonaro’s flight is the microcosm of a progressive institutional sequence that treats electoral and judicial continuity as non-negotiable while converting opposition into a security problem.

Lula da Silva won the 25 October 2026 runoff 51.79 % to 48.21 % after trailing in the first round. A Supreme Court justice extended voting by two hours amid reported disruptions; Bolsonaro refused to concede and called for annulment. Days later, facing a money-laundering investigation and a court order to surrender his passports, he and his family crossed into Argentina, flew via Ecuador, and landed in Miami after the U.S. State Department issued visas. Argentina’s migration authority confirmed the transit with valid documents and no impediment. Lula called the departure “shameful.” https://t.co/765uLiJSI9 https://t.co/M7R8dYLgsw https://t.co/nrdJgB4YFI https://t.co/ISgS43dggZ

The macrocosm is the progressive use of electoral and judicial institutions to lock in outcomes while treating conservative or populist resistance as illegitimate. The same pattern appears wherever progressive continuity holds the administrative and judicial levers: courts and electoral bodies expand process at the margin (poll extensions, passport orders, investigations timed to the loss of immunity), then label any exit or external appeal as proof of guilt. In Brazil the sequence produced the Instagram flood—ordinary citizens treating an external conservative executive as the remaining available interlocutor once internal institutional channels are framed as closed. This is the networked state in operation: centralization does not require open violence when courts, electoral authorities, and media continuity can convert a narrow runoff into a non-reviewable fact and convert opposition figures into flight risks. Where conservative interruptions have occurred (Milei’s fiscal reversal in Argentina, prior border and institutional measures under Jair Bolsonaro), the pressure on independent actors declines; where progressive continuity is restored, the pressure and the external appeals both rise.

The novel observation is the scale of the comment flood itself as a measurable residual. Posts that normally draw low engagement received tens or hundreds of thousands of Brazilian comments begging for intervention. That volume is not random; it records the number of people who concluded that internal mechanisms no longer offer a usable exit. Progressive institutions that expand process (poll hours, judicial orders) while contracting review produce exactly this residual: citizens who still believe a sovereign alternative exists elsewhere. The same residual appears wherever progressive capture advances—Poland’s Tribunal confrontation, European migration frameworks, U.S. institutional pressure—when native or traditional actors treat external conservative actors as the last available check.

The proportionate solution is transparent, time-limited review of the runoff irregularities (poll extension, turnout anomalies) under rules that do not treat the request itself as evidence of bad faith, combined with protection for opposition figures under active judicial orders timed to electoral defeat. President Trump’s existing willingness to issue visas is the immediate practical step that interrupts the flight-to-silence sequence. Longer-term, the Brazilian electorate and any remaining independent institutions decide whether progressive continuity continues to convert narrow wins into non-reviewable facts. The documented international pattern shows that when that continuity is interrupted, both institutional pressure and external residual appeals decline.

text:
The Hog Complex
For November, 2026

The lean hog futures market enters November navigating steep autumn technical degradation and an aggressive market repricing. Nearby December futures have traded down sharply into the $59.00/cwt handle (closing at $59.000 in the latest session) as seasonal cutout premiums soften and market participants price in expanding fall slaughter throughput.

With the complex setting up for late autumn fundamentals, front month futures are adjusting to peak seasonal weight gains, swelling slaughter availability, and the typical post holiday drop in retail grilling demand.

Technical Pressures vs. Seasonal Transition

The lean hog board remains heavily defensive following a broad multi week selloff across the livestock sector. December futures have broken through major moving average support levels, weighed down by relentless seasonal cash index decay and broader macro commodity volatility.

While physical packing facilities maintain elevated harvest schedules, direct cash bids remain restricted as spot availability continues to swell. Historically, November marks the peak phase of rising carcass weights and heavy daily slaughter counts. Market participants are monitoring whether technical support near the upper $50's can trigger short covering or if further price discovery to the downside is required.

Supply Foundations: Hog and Pig Inventories

Data from the USDA Quarterly Hogs and Pigs report shows total U.S. inventory at 74.3 million head, maintaining full availability to satisfy autumn processing capacity.

Key herd metrics continue to underscore a constrained sow base offset by high productivity:

Breeding Herd Discipline: The breeding inventory remains contracted near 5.88 million head (down 1 percent year over year), reflecting producer caution regarding long term herd expansion.

Productivity Benchmarks: Offsetting sow herd contraction, litter rates reached a record high at 11.96 pigs saved per litter. Total market hog inventory stands recorded at 68.4 million head.

USDA projections indicate total annual pork production will finish approximately 1 percent above year ago levels, driven primarily by heavier average dressed weights rather than significant expansion in head count.

Global Supply Risks and Export Dynamics

U.S. pork export shipments continue to absorb domestic supply, with total 2026 export volume running roughly 4 percent ahead of year ago paces.

While steady demand from Mexico anchors primary shipment flows, export expansion faces headwinds from subdued buying in Asian channels and competitive offers from Brazilian origin. Ongoing African Swine Fever monitoring across foreign herds maintains a baseline floor under international trade flows, though near term price action remains governed by domestic slaughter volume and CME index performance.

Slaughter Metrics, Throughput, and Packer Dynamics

Weekly slaughter totals are moving through their seasonal autumn crest. Favorable barn conditions across major production regions continue to advance daily rate of gain, driving average weights higher and expanding total pork tonnage in wholesale channels.

Packer operations are maintaining disciplined procurement strategies:

Margin Defense: Gross packer margins remain tight. As wholesale cutout values retreat from summer levels, processing plants continue modifying operational schedules and Saturday kill shifts to protect operating margins.

Procurement Leverage: Packers are relying heavily on captive inventory, formula contracts, and pre committed supplies for primary operational needs. Elevated spot hog availability gives processing plants leverage in negotiated cash channels, keeping spot bids under pressure.

Pork Cutout and Primal Breakdown

Wholesale cutout values continue to realign with late autumn demand patterns:

Bellies: Facing standard seasonal wholesale pressure following summer peaks. Cold storage movement has slowed, and belly values are adjusting into lower fall distribution channels.

Loins and Hams: Hams are experiencing steady seasonal trade demand as processors accumulate product for Q4 holiday needs. Loins maintain regular retail movement, with featuring focused on value options like shoulder butts and ground pork to compete with elevated retail beef pricing.

Cold Storage Reserves

USDA Cold Storage data reflects a manageable frozen inventory baseline. Total red meat and frozen pork stocks in commercial storage run approximately 9 percent above year ago levels while remaining seasonally balanced.

Pork belly inventories registered a month over month draw of 12 percent heading into the fall supply build, helping limit severe freezer accumulation.

Feed Cost and Margin Analysis

Input cost relief remains a key stabilizing factor for production economics. New crop corn and soybean meal futures trade in low multi year price ranges as Midwest harvest wraps up.

Lower feed costs have significantly reduced breakeven levels for farrow to finish operations, helping preserve operating margins even as lean hog futures undergo seasonal price compression.

Near Term Outlook: Late Autumn Fundamentals

Over the next 30 to 60 days, the market focus centers on packer absorption of peak market hog volume and monitoring retail post holiday movement.

Slaughter Pace & Weights: A primary market driver will be packer capacity to handle heavy autumn market weights without creating processing backlogs or additional cutout weakness.

Chart Levels: Nearby December (/HEZ26) and February contracts must establish technical support in the upper $50's to attract speculative buying interest. Expect prices to react closely to weekly export sales, slaughter numbers, and CME index convergence.

Long Term Outlook: Balanced Infrastructure and Cost Buffers

Looking into late 2026 and early 2027, the hog complex maintains a structurally balanced baseline:

The Efficiency Neutralizer: High facility construction costs and regulatory constraints continue to cap physical sow herd expansion, but record litter rates keep overall production elevated, containing long term price spikes.

Stable Feed Footing: Ample grain inventories provide foundational support for producer solvency, enabling the industry to navigate standard seasonal market pullbacks while maintaining manageable margins.

text:
SAT & ACT Scores for Top 30 US Universities (2027) | 25th, Median & 75th Percentiles

What SAT or ACT scores do students at America's Top 30 universities have?

In this video, we compare SAT and ACT score percentiles across the U.S. News 2027 Top 30 National Universities, using the supplied Common Data Set (CDS C9) records. We examine SAT composite scores, SAT Math and Evidence-Based Reading & Writing, ACT composite scores, and why score-reporting and superscoring policies matter.

Featured universities include MIT, Princeton, Harvard, Yale, Caltech, Stanford, Penn (UPenn), Duke, Johns Hopkins, Northwestern, UChicago, Columbia, Dartmouth, Carnegie Mellon, Cornell, Brown, Rice, Vanderbilt, WashU, UC Berkeley, UCLA, Notre Dame, Emory, Georgetown, Michigan, UVA, UNC, USC, Georgia Tech, and UC San Diego.

**Key findings**
- Reported SAT composite medians in this dataset are concentrated around 1530–1550.
- A 1550 SAT reaches or exceeds every *reported* SAT composite median in this university set, but it does **not** guarantee admission.
- A school's 25th / 50th / 75th percentile offers more context than one isolated score.
- Harvard, Caltech, and Penn have SAT section percentiles in the dataset but no reported composite percentile.
- The same 1550 composite score can reflect very different Math and Reading & Writing results.
- Colleges' superscore and testing policies vary; verify the current policy on each official admissions website.
- UC Berkeley, UCLA, and UC San Diego do not use SAT/ACT scores in undergraduate admissions decisions.

**Important:** These are percentiles for enrolled students who submitted scores, not hard admission cutoffs. The 2027 year refers to the *U.S. News ranking*, not necessarily the academic year of every school's CDS score record. Do not infer a composite median by adding two section medians.

Major U.S. stocks bleeding $ Trillions today! 

Has the AI debt load finally crossed a red line with stock market investors?

Friday's selloff says it may have. U.S. stocks lost an estimated $1.8 trillion to $2.2 trillion in value in a single day. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 alone was on course to erase more than $1.5 trillion.

The trigger was simple. Amazon said it still expects to spend about $220 billion this year building out AI, and "meaningfully more" in 2027. A day earlier, Google's parent Alphabet lost about $500 billion in market value, its worst day ever.

Investors are no longer cheering the spending. They want proof it pays.

Here is the part most headlines skip. The biggest AI companies are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to build data centers. That puts them in direct competition with the U.S. government for the same lenders.

When a tech giant offers lenders a better return than a Treasury bond, Washington has to pay more to keep borrowing. NBC News reports that this competition has helped push Treasury yields higher in recent months.

That is where the AI boom collides with the fiat debt system.

Washington already borrows record sums each week, much of it just to repay older debt. Now it must outbid the AI build-out for the same money. Higher rates mean bigger interest bills, and bigger interest bills mean even more borrowing.

Friday was not a bond market crash. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.92% as frightened money ran into government bonds.

But the question stock investors asked on Friday is the same one bond investors will eventually ask Washington.

When does the borrowing stop paying for itself?

text:
🚨 The US approved 500 Patriot interceptors for Ukraine on Friday, and allies are paying the entire bill

The State Department approved a possible foreign military sale to Ukraine of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors on Friday, October 30, at an estimated cost of $2.1B, and notified Congress the same day. The headline figure making the rounds at $21B is a decimal error. The notification itself prices the package at $2.1B.

• The package: 500 PAC-3 MSE interceptors, the most advanced Patriot variant in service and one of the few weapons able to intercept ballistic missiles, plus classified and unclassified spare parts and logistics and program support
• The contractor: Lockheed Martin $LMT is the principal contractor named in the notification. RTX $RTX builds the Patriot radar and launchers but is not the named contractor on this missile package
• The funding: Ukraine pays with donations from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through the JUMPSTART program, plus national funds financed by the European Union Ukraine Support Loan. The State Department stated plainly that no US funds are involved
• The status: an approval is not a contract. The package still needs a signed letter of offer and acceptance before the Army can place the order, and the notification gives no delivery schedule
• The backdrop: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this week Ukraine had waited almost a month for the sign off as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure ahead of winter
• The capacity race: in July the Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6B for interceptor production, and the company is raising PAC-3 MSE output toward about 2,000 missiles a year
• Tape: $LMT fell 1.0% Friday to close at $636.95 in a session where the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5%

▬▬▬

THE CATCH

Five hundred interceptors sounds like relief, but the approval carries no delivery date, and Ukraine is burning through the scarcest missile in the Western arsenal faster than factories currently make it. Every PAC-3 MSE Ukraine receives is also one the US and its other allies do not stockpile, which is why the funding structure exists at all: Washington supplies the missile, Europe supplies the money.

▬▬▬

THE TAKEAWAY

This is the new shape of US arms support: American production, allied payment, and a congressional notification instead of a drawdown. For $LMT the order adds to a multiyear interceptor backlog already funded by the $58.6B Army award. For Ukraine the only number that matters is not in the release: how many missiles actually arrive before winter.

Does the production ramp get interceptors to Ukraine in time to matter this winter, or does the approval outrun the factory? 👇 NFA
